The AWEA AG5-1620 is a gantry type five-axis machining center whose X and Y axes run on linear motors instead of ball screws. Travels are 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in X, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z over a fixed 1,600 x 2,000 mm (63.0 x 78.7 in) table, so the working area is wider than it is long. The cross beam does the moving. The part stays put.

Long parts are the case for the AWEA AG5-3220. Its X travel is 3,200 mm (126.0 in), twice that of the AG5-1620 , on the same 2,000 mm (78.7 in) Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) Z, and the fixed table measures 3,200 x 2,000 mm (126.0 x 78.7 in). Wing ribs, stringers, long mould halves and rows of smaller parts on one fixture plate are what that length is for.

The AWEA FV-560 is a compact 5-axis vertical machining center with an A / C rotary table of Ø220 mm (Ø8.7 in). Linear travels are 560 mm (22.0 in) in X, 510 mm (20.1 in) in Y and 460 mm (18.1 in) in Z. The A-axis swivels 100° ~ -100° and the C-axis turns a full 360˚.

The AWEA FV-960 combines a long X axis with a tilting rotary table. X travel is 960 mm (37.8 in), Y is 600 mm (23.6 in) and Z is 480 mm (18.9 in), and the table is listed as 560 x 365 mm (22.0 x 14.4 in) with a Ø350 mm platter. That layout leaves room beside the trunnion, so the machine can be used for 5-axis parts on the rotary table and for 3-axis work with a vise on the same setup.

The AWEA HVM-3018 is the entry size of the HVM five-face bridge type machining centers: 3,060 mm (120.5 in) of X travel, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.3 in) of Z over a 3,260 x 1,500 mm (128.3 x 59.0 in) table. It is the only HVM with a table rated at 10,000 kg (22,000 lb), and the only one with an X rapid of 20,000 mm/min (787.4 IPM).

Long, narrow work is the case for the AWEA HVM-4018. This five-face bridge type machining center pairs 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel with the narrowest cross-section in the HVM series: a 4,020 x 1,500 mm (158.3 x 59.0 in) table, 1,800 mm (70.9 in) between the columns and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y travel. Z is 1,000 mm (39.3 in).

The AWEA HVM-4025 opens the middle frame of the HVM five-face bridge range. Its columns are 2,500 mm (98.4 in) apart, the table measures 4,020 x 2,010 mm (158.3 x 79.1 in), and the travels are 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.3 in) in Z.

The AWEA HVM-4032 is a five-face bridge type machining center whose table is more than half as wide as it is long: 4,020 x 2,400 mm (158.3 x 94.5 in), under a bridge with 3,200 mm (126.0 in) between the columns. Travels are 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X, 3,900 mm (153.5 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.3 in) in Z. Among the HVM sizes this is the one for squarish work such as large plates, ring-shaped weldments and housings.

Five metres of X travel is where the AWEA HVM-5025 begins to trade speed for reach. The machine is a five-face bridge type machining center with 5,000 mm (196.8 in) in X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.3 in) in Z, and its X rapid is 10,000 mm/min (394 ipm). The HVM-4025 , one size shorter with an unchanged column spacing, is listed at 15,000 mm/min (590.6 IPM).

Table load is the reason to look at the AWEA HVM-5032. Rated for 18,000 kg (39,600 lb), it carries half as much again as the HVM-4032 or the HVM-5025 , both of which stop at 12,000 kg (26,400 lb). The machine is a five-face bridge type machining center with a 5,020 x 2,400 mm (197.6 x 94.5 in) table and travels of 5,000 mm (196.8 in), 3,900 mm (153.5 in) and 1,000 mm (39.3 in) in X, Y and Z.

The AWEA HVM-6025 stretches the 2,500 mm (98.4 in) column frame of the HVM series to its longest bed. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y is 3,200 mm (126.0 in), Z is 1,000 mm (39.3 in), and the table measures 6,020 x 2,010 mm (237.0 x 79.1 in). This five-face bridge type machining center is aimed at one kind of part: long, heavy, and not especially wide.

With the AWEA HVM-6032 the HVM table reaches its full size and its full rating: 6,020 x 2,400 mm (237.0 x 94.5 in) and 20,000 kg (44,000 lb). Neither figure grows on the two larger models. The HVM-6033Y and HVM-7033Y add travel, not table. For a buyer whose question is how much part the series can hold, this five-face bridge type machining center is already the answer.

The Y in AWEA HVM-6033Y stands for the axis that sets this machine apart. Y travel is 4,500 mm (177.2 in), the longest cross stroke in the HVM five-face bridge type machining center series, over a table that is only 2,400 mm (94.5 in) wide and columns 3,300 mm (129.9 in) apart. X is 6,000 mm (236.2 in) and Z is 1,000 mm (39.3 in).

At 7,000 mm (275.6 in) of X travel, the AWEA HVM-7033Y is the longest five-face bridge type machining center in the HVM series. It sits on the wide Y bridge, with 4,500 mm (177.2 in) of Y travel and 3,300 mm (129.9 in) between the columns, and has the 1,000 mm (39.3 in) Z stroke common to the range.

The AWEA LP-2516YF is the entry size of the LP-F range, the version of the LP bridge machine prepared for 5-face work. Travels are 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in X, 1,900 mm (74.8 in) in Y and 760 mm (29.9 in) in Z, over a 2,310 x 1,500 mm (90.9 x 59.1 in) table that carries 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).

Three metres of X is where many 5-face jobs start, and the AWEA LP-3016YF covers it with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel, 1,900 mm (74.8 in) of Y and 760 mm (29.9 in) of Z. Unlike the shorter model, its table is longer than the stroke: 3,260 x 1,500 mm (128.3 x 59.1 in), rated for 10,000 kg (22,046 lb). Clamps and stops can sit on the stretch of table that the spindle never has to visit.

The AWEA LP-3021YF is the shortest of the four LP-21YF bridge type 5-face machining centers: 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X, 2,400 mm (94.5 in) of Y and 760 mm (29.9 in) of Z over a 3,020 x 2,010 mm (118.9 x 79.1 in) table. Being the shortest also makes it the quickest and the tightest of its group. The X axis rapids at 20,000 mm/min (787 ipm), and positioning under VDI is P ≤ 0.025 mm over full travel with repeatability of Ps ≤ 0.020 mm.

The AWEA LP-3025YF is the shortest 5-face bridge machine built on the 2,700 mm (106.3 in) column spacing: 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y and 760 mm (29.9 in) of Z over a 3,020 x 2,400 mm (118.9 x 94.5 in) table. Its cross travel is longer than its table travel. That is unusual for a bridge mill, and it tells you what the machine is for.

An automatic head storage magazine with two cabinets holds a horizontal head and the spindle cap, and a vertical / horizontal ATC system loads tools into either.

The Accuway U-18H is a small 5-axis machining center built around a 60,000 rpm direct-drive spindle. The figures describe a machine for very small tools and small parts: a Ø200 mm (Ø7.9 in) table, a maximum workpiece of Ø200 x 200 mm (Ø7.9 x 7.9 in), a 60 kg (132 lb) table load and a spindle motor of 1.2 kW (1.6 hp).

Accuway's U-25 is a 5-axis vertical machining center with a Ø250 mm (Ø9.8 in) table and a BT40 direct-drive spindle. It takes a workpiece up to Ø250 x 220 mm (Ø9.8 x 8.7 in) and 60 kg (132 lb), and moves 500 mm (19.7 in) in X, 400 mm (15.7 in) in Y and 550 mm (21.7 in) in Z.

The Accuway UM-350 is a trunnion-style 5-axis vertical machining center: a Ø350 mm (Ø13.8 in) rotary table on an A axis that tilts -120/+30 degrees, under a BT40 direct-drive spindle. Linear travels are 700 mm (27.6 in), 550 mm (21.7 in) and 550 mm (21.7 in).

With a Ø500 mm (Ø19.7 in) table and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of X travel, the Accuway UM-500 is the largest of the maker's 5-axis vertical machining centers. Y is 650 mm (25.6 in), Z is 550 mm (21.7 in), and the largest workpiece is Ø500 x 300 mm (Ø19.7 x 11.8 in).

The Akira Seiki 5AX-AC650 is a five-axis simultaneous machining center of the trunnion type: the workpiece tilts on an A axis and rotates on a C axis under a vertical spindle. The table is ∅500 mm (∅19.7 in), and the maker gives the largest workpiece as ∅650 x 350 mm (∅25.6 x 13.8 in) at up to 200 kg (441 lb).

On the 5AX-BC650, Akira Seiki tilts the table about a B axis and rotates it on C. B swings -50° ~ +110° and C turns a full 360°, with indexing of 0.001°. The table is ∅650 mm (∅25.6 in) and takes 300 kg (661 lb), a larger and stronger table than the one on the 5AX-AC650 .

The Akira Seiki RMV160RT is a very small multi-face machining center. A ∅160 mm (∅6.3 in) rotary table rotates 360° on C and swings on B through +30 / -120, so a part can be reached from every side but its base in one clamping. Maximum loading is 20 kg (44.09 lb).

A ∅250 mm (∅9.8 in) tilting rotary table and a BT40 spindle make the Akira Seiki RMV250RT the larger of the maker's two multi-face production machines. The table rotates 360° on C, swings +30 / -120 on B and carries 60 kg (132.28 lb).

The Alzmetall GS 600/5-T is a compact 5-axis machining center: 460 × 600 × 400 mm (18.1 × 23.6 × 15.7 in) of travel, an HSK-A63 spindle and a table rated for 500 kg (1,102 lb) including the clamping set-up. The two rotary motions are an NC swivel axis (A) and a rotary axis (C), listed with 3-fold torque drives.

The Alzmetall GS 800/5-T is a 5-axis machining center with 660 × 800 × 550 mm (26.0 × 31.5 × 21.7 in) of travel, an HSK-A63 spindle and a disc magazine for 40 tools. Its table takes 500 kg (1,102 lb), a figure that includes the clamping set-up.

The Alzmetall GS 1000/5-FDT is a 5-axis machining center with 800 × 800 × 600 mm (31.5 × 31.5 × 23.6 in) of travel whose spindle takes HSK-T63 tooling. That taper is the row to read first, because it is the one headline figure separating this model from the GS 1000/5-T , which has HSK-A63 with the same 1,000 kg (2,205 lb) table load, the same 33-tool chain magazine and the same standard control.

The Alzmetall GS 1000/5-T is a 5-axis machining center built around a square working field: 800 mm (31.5 in) in both X and Y, with 600 mm (23.6 in) of Z. The spindle interface is HSK-A63 and the standard table load is 1,000 kg (2,205 lb) including the clamping set-up.

The Alzmetall GS 1200/5-T is a large 5-axis machining center: 1,000 × 1,200 × 800 mm (39.4 × 47.2 × 31.5 in) of travel and a table rated for 2,500 kg (5,511 lb) including the clamping set-up, served by an HSK-A63 spindle and a 45-tool chain magazine.

The Alzmetall GS 1400/5-FDT is a 5-axis machining center with an HSK-T100 spindle, a 3,000 kg (6,614 lb) table load including the clamping set-up and travels of 1,200 × 1,300 × 800 mm (47.2 × 51.2 × 31.5 in).

The Alzmetall GS 1400/5-T is a heavy 5-axis machining center with an HSK-A100 spindle, 1,200 × 1,300 × 800 mm (47.2 × 51.2 × 31.5 in) of travel and a table load of 3,000 kg (6,614 lb) including the clamping set-up.

The Anderson Axxiom 1616 IP is the base model of the AXXIOM 5-axis series: a fixed bridge machine with a single moving table of 1600 mm (63”) by 1600 mm (63”) and 1000 mm (39.37”) of Z stroke. X and Y strokes are both 2200 mm (86”). An 18 HP spindle runs to 22,000 rpm on HSK-63, and the machine weighs 8,600 Kg (18,960 lbs.).

The Anderson Axxiom 1616 IP PT is the twin-table version of the AXXIOM 5-axis machine. It has two tables, each 1600 mm (63”) by 1600 mm (63”), with 2 vacuum zones in total, and the tables can be locked together to make one surface 3100 mm long. X stroke is 3810 mm (150”), Y stroke 2200 mm (86”) and Z stroke 1000 mm (39.37”).

The Anderson Axxiom 1631 IP stretches the AXXIOM 5-axis machine in one direction. Its table is 1600 mm (63”) by 3100 mm (122”), and the Y stroke grows to 3700 mm (145.6”) while X stays at 2200 mm (86”). Z stroke is 1000 mm (39.37”). Weight is 12,000 Kg (26,455 lbs.).

The Anderson FUV-170 is the smallest 5-axis machining center in the FUV series, with a Ø170 mm (Ø6.7 in) trunnion table that carries 30 kg (66 lb). Travels are 360 mm (14.2 in) in X, 420 mm (16.5 in) in Y and 465 mm (18.3 in) in Z. Anderson describes it as an ultra-compact 5-axis solution for small precision parts.

The Anderson FUV-250 is a compact trunnion-type 5-axis machining center with a Ø255 mm (Ø10.0 in) table rated for 100 kg (220 lb). It shares its frame with the smaller FUV-170 : X travel is the same 360 mm (14.2 in), Z the same 465 mm (18.3 in), and both machines weigh 4,500 kg (9,921 lb). Y travel is slightly longer at 440 mm (17.3 in).

The Anderson FUV-400 is the mid-size machine of the FUV 5-axis series and the first on the larger frame. Its trunnion carries a Ø400 mm (Ø15.7 in) rotary table rated for 200 kg (441 lb), and travels are 460 mm (18.1 in) in X, 500 mm (19.7 in) in Y and 500 mm (19.7 in) in Z.

The Anderson FUV-500 tops the compact FUV 5-axis range. Anderson calls it the maximum capacity model, with a Ø500 mm (Ø19.7 in) table and 300 kg (661 lb) of load. Travels are 600 mm (23.6 in) in X, 700 mm (27.6 in) in Y and 520 mm (20.5 in) in Z, and the machine weighs 8,700 kg (19,180 lb).

The Anderson Mass 5 is a large open-gantry 5-axis machine for composites and aluminum. It is built to size: the table is listed at 3000 - 6000 mm (118 - 236 in) wide and 6000 - 16000 mm (236 - 630 in) long, with a Z stroke of 1000 - 3000 mm (39.3 - 118 in). The head tilts ± 100° in B and rotates ± 200° in C.

The Anderson MAXXIS Series is a fixed bridge, moving table 5-axis machine for plastics, aluminum and composite materials. Anderson's page shows two configurations under one name, and this page carries only the rows that are the same for both: a table 800 mm (31.5 in) high, a Z stroke of 800 - 1200 mm (31.5 - 47.2 in), ball screw drives on X, Y and Z, and a choice of FANUC 31i or SIEMENS 840D control.

The Anger Machining GT-500 is the smallest and liveliest of the GT 5-axis gantry machines. Its linear axes travel 610 mm (24.0 in) in X and Y and 510 mm (20.1 in) in Z and accelerate at 10/10/10 m/s², where the GT-630(F ) and GT-800E list 5/5/5 m/s².

The Anger Machining GT-630(F) is the mid-size GT gantry: a ø630 mm rotary-tilt table for 600 kg (1,323 lb) under linear axes of 760 mm (29.9 in) in X, 820 mm (32.3 in) in Y and 560 mm (22.0 in) in Z. Parts up to ø800x500 mm fit.

For the largest parts in the GT range, the Anger Machining GT-800E pairs a ø800 mm table rated at 800 kg (1,764 lb) with travels of 800 mm (31.5 in) in X, 820 mm (32.3 in) in Y and 560 mm (22.0 in) in Z. The maximum part is ø900x500 mm.

The Anger Machining HS700 is the small member of the HS series of horizontal 5-axis machining centers: 710 mm (28.0 in) of X travel, 910 mm (35.8 in) of Y and 810 mm (31.9 in) of Z around a ø650 mm table that carries up to 350 kg (772 lb). Anger designs the series for simultaneous 5-axis work on aerospace parts, and lists blisks, impellers and engine housings among the typical workpieces.

A 35,000 kg (77,160 lb) horizontal 5-axis machine for large aerospace structures, the Anger Machining HS1400 travels 1,800 mm (70.9 in) in X, 1,250 mm (49.2 in) in Y and 1,320 mm (52.0 in) in Z. It takes parts up to ø1,800/1,200 mm and loads of 2,000 kg (4,409 lb) on a table that the datasheet gives as ø1,000 - 1,400 mm.

Milling and turning in one clamping is what separates the Anger Machining HS1400T from the rest of the HS series. Its rotary axis runs at 700 rpm, against 70 rpm on the HS1400 . The spindle interface is HSK100T, and the table load is 3,200 kg (7,055 lb), the highest in the series.

A C-axis that spins at 1,000 rpm turns the Anger Machining SK800T from a 5-axis mill into a mill-turn gantry. Anger describes it as a high-speed C-axis for turning operations, and the tool interface changes with it to HSK63T, with HSK100T in brackets.

The Anger Machining SK800TR is a 5-axis gantry machining center with direct drives on both swivel axes and a table rated for 1,300 kg (2,866 lb). Travels are 800 mm (31.5 in) in X, 830 mm (32.7 in) in Y and 560 mm (22.0 in) in Z, for parts up to ø900x500 mm on a ø800 mm table.

The AWEA MCP-8040 is the shortest machine in the MCP moving column range: a bridge type five-face machining center with 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel, 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y and 1,400 mm (55.1 in) of Z above a stationary 8,000 x 2,800 mm (315.0 x 110.2 in) table. The part never moves. Both columns carry the cross beam along it.

The AWEA MCP-8050 is the shortest of the seven moving column bridge machines built on the 5,400 mm (212.6 in) Y frame, with 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel and 1,400 mm (55.1 in) of Z. Its table measures 8,000 x 3,800 mm (315.0 x 149.6 in) and does not move. The columns travel along it instead, a layout AWEA says takes 40 % less space than a fixed column machine.

The AWEA MCP-8060 is the shortest machine of the widest MCP group: a moving column bridge type multi-face machining center with 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel and 6,400 mm (252.0 in) of Y. Its fixed table measures 8,000 x 4,800 mm (315.0 x 189.0 in). No other model in the 6,400 mm group has a work area this close to square, and that shapes what it is good at.

Floor space is the argument for the AWEA MCP-10040. Its table is 10,000 x 2,800 mm (393.7 x 110.2 in) and stays where it is, while the columns travel 10,000 mm (393.7 in) in X. A machine that moved a table of that length would need room for the table at both ends of its stroke. AWEA puts the saving at 40 % less space than a fixed column machine.

Three AWEA moving column machines share 10,000 mm (393.7 in) of X travel, and the MCP-10050 is the middle one. It pairs that stroke with 5,400 mm (212.6 in) of Y and a fixed table of 10,000 x 3,800 mm (393.7 x 149.6 in).

Spindle choice matters more than length on the AWEA MCP-10060, a 10,000 mm (393.7 in) by 6,400 mm (252.0 in) moving column machine whose specification leaves the head open to five variants. The speed row is printed as "4,000 Gear Spindle (Std.)；5,000 / 6,000 Gear Spindle (Opt.)；8,000 / 12,000 Built-in Spindle (Opt.)". One motor rating covers the row: 22 / 26 kW (29.5 / 34.9 hp). The taper is BBT50 throughout.

With 12,000 mm (472.4 in) of X travel, the AWEA MCP-12040 is the first MCP size longer than anything in AWEA's MVP five-face range, where the MVP-8040 tops out at 8,000 mm (315.0 in). It is the narrow version of the 12,000 mm machine: 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y over a table 12,000 x 2,800 mm (472.4 x 110.2 in).

On a machine with 12,000 mm (472.4 in) of X travel, where the tools live matters as much as how fast the axes move. The AWEA MCP-12050 carries its magazine on the moving column, so a tool change happens wherever the column is standing. AWEA makes the point itself: the X-axis does not have to move for tool changes.

Multi-face work is the reason to look at the AWEA MCP-12060. It is a bridge machine whose columns run 12,000 mm (472.4 in) along a stationary 12,000 x 4,800 mm (472.4 x 189.0 in) table, with a head that crosses 6,400 mm (252.0 in), and AWEA fits an automatic head changer and a two positions ATC system as standard.

The AWEA MCP-14040 sits in the middle of the seven 4,400 mm (173.2 in) Y machines of the MCP range, with 14,000 mm (551.2 in) of X travel and a 14,000 x 2,800 mm (551.2 x 110.2 in) table. Three shorter and three longer models share every other row of its specification table.

Height is the reason to look at the AWEA MCP-14050 instead of AWEA's other 14-metre machine. Its Z travel is 1,400 mm (55.1 in), and the spindle nose works between 800 and 2,200 mm (31.5 ~ 86.6 in) above the table. The LG-14050 has the same 14,000 mm (551.2 in) of X but 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z and a nose range of 200 ~ 1,200 mm (7.9 ~ 47.2 in). One machine is laid out for tall fabrications, the other for work close to the table.

AWEA builds two machines around a 14,000 x 4,800 mm (551.2 x 189.0 in) table, and the MCP-14060 is the taller and wider-reaching one. Its X travel is 14,000 mm (551.2 in), Y is 6,400 mm (252.0 in) and Z is 1,400 mm (55.1 in), with 1,600 mm available.

Sixteen metres of fixed table is a building decision as much as a machine decision, and the AWEA MCP-16040 should be read that way. X travel is 16,000 mm (629.9 in), Y is 4,400 mm (173.2 in), Z is 1,400 mm (55.1 in), and the table measures 16,000 x 2,800 mm (629.9 x 110.2 in).

Sixteen metres of X travel puts two demands on a moving column machine: both columns must stay in step, and the shop has to supply it. The AWEA MCP-16050, with 16,000 mm (629.9 in) of X and 5,400 mm (212.6 in) of Y, is where those questions start to dominate the purchase.

Planning the building comes first with the AWEA MCP-16060. This moving column multi-face machining center has a 16,000 x 4,800 mm (629.9 x 189.0 in) table, 16,000 mm (629.9 in) of X travel and a bridge spanning 6,400 mm (252.0 in) of Y, and its service figures deserve a look before its cutting figures.

Height is what separates the AWEA MCP-18040 from a long plate mill. Beneath the bridge, the spindle nose stands 800 ~ 2,200 mm (31.5 ~ 86.6 in) above the table top and the ram travels 1,400 mm (55.1 in) in Z. Order the 1,600 mm Z option and the lower limit drops to 600 mm. Under that sits a table 18,000 x 2,800 mm (708.7 x 110.2 in), served by 18,000 mm (708.7 in) of X travel and 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y.

The AWEA MCP-18050 has a fixed table 18,000 x 3,800 mm (708.7 x 149.6 in), and most of what makes it useful follows from the fact that the table never moves. Parts are craned onto a stationary surface. AWEA describes a big, open machining area with low side structures and a very low profile, both aimed at making loading and unloading of large workpieces easier and safer.

Eighteen metres of bed moving at a walking pace: the AWEA MCP-18060 pairs 18,000 mm (708.7 in) of X travel with a rapid traverse of 10 / 10 / 10 m/min (394 / 394 / 394 ipm). Y travel is 6,400 mm (252.0 in) and the table is 18,000 x 4,800 mm (708.7 x 189.0 in).

The AWEA MCP-20040 is the longest machine of its width: 20,000 mm (787.4 in) of X travel over a 20,000 x 2,800 mm (787.4 x 110.2 in) table, with 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y and 1,400 mm (55.1 in) of Z. No AWEA model in the catalogue lists a longer X stroke.
At 20,000 mm (787.4 in) of X travel, the AWEA MCP-20050 is the longest size in the MCP tables. With no larger model above it, the choice at this length is only how wide to go.

No MCP has a bigger table than the AWEA MCP-20060: 20,000 x 4,800 mm (787.4 x 189.0 in), served by 20,000 mm (787.4 in) of X travel and 6,400 mm (252.0 in) of Y. It is the top of the series in both directions at once.

The AWEA MEGA5 G4037 is the shortest of the MEGA5 G gantry type 5-axis machining centers: 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel, 3,700 mm (145.7 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z above a 4,000 x 3,800 mm (157.5 x 149.6 in) table. The workpiece stays still. A gantry carries the two-axis B and C milling head over it.

Six metres of X is where AWEA's two MEGA5 designs meet, and the AWEA MEGA5 G6037 is the gantry answer at that length: 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X, 3,700 mm (145.7 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. The fixed-bridge MEGA5 P6032 has the same X travel but moves the table under the bridge. On the G6037 the table is fixed and the gantry travels.

The AWEA MEGA5 G6047 opens the wide frame of the MEGA5 G series. Its gantry spans 5,800 mm (228.3 in) between columns and gives 4,700 mm (185.0 in) of Y travel, paired with 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. No shorter machine is offered at this width.

The AWEA MEGA5 G8037 is a gantry type 5-axis machining center with 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel, a length AWEA's fixed-bridge MEGA5 P range does not reach: its longest model, the MEGA5 P6032 , stops at 6,000 mm (236.2 in). Y travel is 3,700 mm (145.7 in) and Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in).

The AWEA MEGA5 G8047 sits in the middle of the wide-frame MEGA5 G gantry machines, between the MEGA5 G6047 and the MEGA5 G10047 . Travels are 8,000 mm (315.0 in) in X, 4,700 mm (185.0 in) in Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) in Z, and the two-axis milling head works over a table of 8,000 x 4,800 mm (315.0 x 189.0 in).

With 10,000 mm (393.7 in) of X travel, the AWEA MEGA5 G10037 is the longest standard length in the MEGA5 G gantry series on the narrower of its two frames. Y is 3,700 mm (145.7 in), Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in), and the fixed table measures 10,000 x 3,800 mm (393.7 x 149.6 in).

Nothing in AWEA's 5-axis range is larger than the AWEA MEGA5 G10047. The gantry covers 10,000 mm (393.7 in) in X and 4,700 mm (185.0 in) in Y, with 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z, over a 10,000 x 4,800 mm (393.7 x 189.0 in) table, and the machine itself weighs 167,000 kg (368,166 lb).

The AWEA MEGA5 P2526 is the smallest fixed-bridge machine in the MEGA5 5-axis range: 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of X, 2,620 mm (103.1 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z under a two-axis B/C milling head. Unusually for a bridge mill, the cross travel is longer than the table travel. That surplus is there for the fork head, which needs room beside the part before it can lay the spindle over and work a side face.

Two fixed-bridge MEGA5 machines offer 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel, and the AWEA MEGA5 P3026 is the narrower, faster one. Its bridge spans 1,700 mm (66.9 in) between the columns, Y travel is 2,620 mm (103.1 in), Z is 1,000 mm (39.4 in), and the listed spindle is an HSK-A63 unit that runs to 24,000 rpm.

With an HSK-A100 spindle and 2,700 mm (106.3 in) between its columns, the AWEA MEGA5 P3032 opens the heavier half of the MEGA5 P range. Travels are 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z, and the Z stroke can be ordered as 1,200 mm.

Length starts to cost something at the AWEA MEGA5 P4026. This fixed-bridge 5-axis machine has 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel with the 2,620 mm (103.1 in) Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) Z of the narrow MEGA5 P frame, and it is the first size where the X-axis figures step down.

AWEA sells three 5-axis machines with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel, and the AWEA MEGA5 P4032 is the middle one in every respect that matters for installation: part width, mass and tool size. It is a fixed-bridge machine with 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y, 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z (1,200 mm optional) and a 4,020 x 2,400 mm (158.3 x 94.5 in) table.

A 5,000 x 1,500 mm (196.9 x 59.1 in) table under a 24,000 rpm 5-axis head: the AWEA MEGA5 P5026 is built for parts that are long and slim. Wing ribs, spars, rail sections, extrusion dies and machine beams fit that shape. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in), which matches the table, with 2,620 mm (103.1 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z.

Feed rates are the first thing to read on the AWEA MEGA5 P5032. This wide fixed-bridge 5-axis machine has 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z, and its table carries 18,000 kg (39,683 lb). Moving that much table and load comes at a listed cutting feed of 8 m / min and an X rapid of 10 m / min.

At 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel the AWEA MEGA5 P6032 is as long as the fixed-bridge MEGA5 gets. Beyond this length AWEA's 5-axis machines are gantry designs. Y travel is 3,200 mm (126.0 in), Z is 1,000 mm (39.4 in) or optionally 1,200 mm, and the 6,020 x 2,400 mm (237.0 x 94.5 in) table is rated for 20,000 kg (44,092 lb), the highest table load in the P line.

The AWEA MVP-4032 is the shortest machine in the MVP series of moving cross rail, five-face bridge machining centers: 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z, with 1,200 or 1,400 mm of Z as options. The cross rail itself travels 1,250 mm (49.2 in) on the W axis, so the head can be brought down to a low plate or raised over a tall weldment without changing the Z stroke.

Square is the word for the AWEA MVP-4040. X and Y travel are both 4,000 mm (157.5 in), which is unusual in a bridge machine and suits parts that are as wide as they are long: ring-shaped fabrications, large flanges, press platens, square machine bases. The table is 4,020 x 3,010 mm (158.3 x 118.5 in) and the clear distance between the columns is 3,500 mm (137.8 in).

The AWEA MVP-5032 carries 18,000 kg (39,683 lb) on a 5,020 x 2,400 mm (197.6 x 94.5 in) table, and that rating is the main reason to pick it over the shorter MVP-4032 , which is listed at 15,000 kg (33,069 lb). It is a double column bridge machine with a moving cross rail and a spindle head that cuts both vertically and horizontally. Travels are 5,000 mm (196.9 in) in X, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z.

The AWEA MVP-5040 pairs 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of Y on a cross rail that moves up and down, and the vertical side of the machine is the part of the specification that most often decides whether a job fits.

At 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel, the AWEA MVP-6032 is the first size in the MVP five-face range to get two things: the 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) table rating and a vibration damping mechanism on the X-axis ball screw. AWEA applies that mechanism to models of 6 m travel and above only. A screw this long is prone to whip and vibration, and the maker's stated aim is to keep cutting accuracy over the full travel.

Two accuracy standards appear on the AWEA MVP-6040's sheet, and on a machine with 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel and 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of Y they tell different stories. Under JIS the positioning figure is ± 0.010 mm over full travel with ± 0.003 mm repeatability, and AWEA prints those same numbers for every MVP. Under VDI the figures are P = 0.035 mm and P = 0.026 mm, and these do change with bed length. Anyone comparing this machine with another should compare like with like, and for a large-part machine the VDI line is the more telling one.

Choose the AWEA MVP-7032 for the length of the part and nothing else. Its 7,000 mm (275.6 in) X travel and 7,020 x 2,400 mm (276.4 x 94.5 in) table are the reason it exists; in table load it matches the MVP-6032 at 20,000 kg (44,092 lb), and in speed and accuracy it gives ground to it.

A part that fills the AWEA MVP-7040 will spend many hours on the table, and most of the gain on such a job comes from not stopping: no re-clamping, no manual tool loading, no head change by crane. The machine has 7,000 mm (275.6 in) of X travel, 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of Y and a 7,020 x 3,010 mm (276.4 x 118.5 in) table, and its tooling system is laid out for long unattended sequences.

The AWEA MVP-8032 is the longest five-face bridge machine AWEA builds on the 3,200 mm (126.0 in) Y frame, with 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel and an 8,040 x 2,400 mm (316.5 x 94.5 in) table. A machine of this size is an installation project before it is a machining decision, so the service and weight figures deserve to be read first.

The AWEA MVP-8040 is the top of the MVP range: 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel, 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of Y, and an 8,040 x 3,010 mm (316.5 x 118.5 in) table. It is also the one model whose sheet departs from the pattern of the rest of the series in three rows.

Description: Our best estimate for a 5-axis machining center in this class — not a quote from Breton. Configuration moves it a long way.

The Breton Hawx E1 K40 is a 5-axis gantry machining centre for trimming and high-speed milling of light alloys, polymers, resins and composites, with travels of 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X, 1,900 mm (74.8 in) in Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) in Z. It is the shorter of the two E1 sizes. The Breton Hawx E1 K60 has the same Y and Z with 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X.

Six metres of X travel on a one-piece frame is the point of the Breton Hawx E1 K60. The 5-axis gantry machining centre lists 6,000 mm (236.2 in) in X, 1,900 mm (74.8 in) in Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) in Z, and Breton aims it at milling and trimming of complex shapes in light alloys, polymers, resins and composite materials.

The Breton Hawx E2 K18 is the starting size of the modular Hawx E2: a 5-axis gantry machining centre whose bridge spans 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y while X is only 1,800 mm (70.9 in). Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in). The envelope is wider than it is long, which is unusual for a gantry and worth understanding before comparing it with the other columns of the table.

With 3,800 mm (149.6 in) of X and 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y, the Breton Hawx E2 K38 is the Hawx with the most balanced work area: a 5-axis gantry machining centre for milling, contouring and trimming of light alloys, polymers, resins and composites. Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in).

The Breton Hawx E2 K58 is a 5-axis gantry machining centre with 5,800 mm (228.3 in) of X, 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of Z. Read its spindle rows first, because they say more about the intended work than the travels do.

At 7,800 mm (307.1 in) of X travel the Breton Hawx E2 K78 is the largest machine in the Hawx version table. It is a 5-axis gantry machining centre with 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of Z, intended for high-speed milling and trimming of light alloys, polymers, resins and composites.
This model was not found in Breton's current lineup when we checked on 2026-10-03 . It may be a superseded or older model; the specifications below are as we last recorded them.

The Breton Matrix E1 800 K20 is the lowest of three Z heights of the Matrix E1, a monobloc 5-axis gantry machining centre for steel, lightweight alloys and special composites. Travels are 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in X, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in Y and 800 mm (31.5 in) in Z. Breton positions the E1 for hi-feed roughing, semi-finishing and finishing of medium-size workpieces, with moulds and dies named first among the applications.

One metre of Z is what the Breton Matrix E1 1000 K20 offers over the entry version of the series. This monobloc 5-axis gantry machining centre travels 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in X, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z, and carries a workbench listed at 2,500 mm (98.4 in) by 1,000 mm (39.4 in).

The Breton Matrix E1 1200 K20 is the tall version of Breton's monobloc 5-axis gantry machining centre: 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z above a 2,500 mm (98.4 in) by 1,000 mm (39.4 in) workbench, with 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of X and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y.

The Breton Matrix E2 1100 K25 is a 5-axis vertical gantry machining centre with a square plan: 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in X, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in Y, and 1,100 mm (43.3 in) in Z. Breton developed the E2 for hi-feed roughing, semi-finishing and finishing of medium-large workpieces in steel, lightweight alloys and special composites, with large moulds and dies as the home ground.

Four metres of X is the reason for the Breton Matrix E2 1100 K40. It is the long-bed version of Breton's 5-axis vertical gantry machining centre for large moulds, dies and structural parts, with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in Y and 1,100 mm (43.3 in) in Z.

The Breton Ultrix E2 is the smallest of Breton's trunnion-table machining centres for combined milling and turning. It is a 5-axis vertical machine on a gantry architecture with travels of 1,150 mm (45.3 in) in X, 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Y and 700 mm (27.6 in) in Z, and a rotary table 1,250 mm (49.2 in) in diameter that carries 1,500 kg (3,307 lb).

The Breton Ultrix E3 moves the Ultrix idea, 5-axis milling and turning on a trunnion table under a gantry, up to parts weighing 2,500 kg (5,511 lb). Linear travels are 1,700 mm (66.9 in) in X, 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z.

Torque defines the Breton Ultrix E3 HD. In the rotary-table block of the version table, its maximum torque in S6 is 4,200 Nm (3,097.9 lb-ft), where the Breton Ultrix E3 column reads 2,700 Nm (1,991.5 lb-ft). The machine is otherwise the large Ultrix: a 5-axis vertical machining centre with trunnion table for milling and turning, travelling 1,700 mm (66.9 in) in X, 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z.

The Campro NU 170C is the smallest of the NU series 5-axis machining centers: a trunnion-table machine with a Ø170 mm (Ø6.6 in) table and travels of 400 mm (15.7 in) in X, 430 mm (16.9 in) in Y and 480 mm (18.8 in) in Z. The A axis swivels ±100° and the C axis turns through 360°. Campro gives the maximum workpiece as Ø220x 350 mm.

With a Ø255 mm (Ø10 in) table, the Campro NU 255C sits one step above the entry model in the NU series of trunnion-type 5-axis machining centers. X travel is 400 mm (15.7 in), Y is 520 mm (20.4 in) and Z is 450 mm (17.7 in). The A axis swivels +30°~-120° and the C axis rotates 360°.

The Campro NU 400C is the largest of the three C-suffix trunnion machines in the NU series, a 5-axis machining center built around a Ø400 mm (Ø15.7 in) table. Travels are 550 mm (21.6 in) in X, 600 mm (23.6 in) in Y and 530 mm (20.8 in) in Z, with an A axis range of +30°~-120° and a 360° C axis.

Campro builds the NU 550 as a monoblock column 5-axis machining center: a one-piece column and base with a tilting rotary table of Ø550 mm (21.6 in). Travels are 940 mm (37 in) in X, 800 mm (31.4 in) in Y and 550 mm (21.6 in) in Z. The A axis swivels +30°~-120° and the C axis rotates 360°.

The Campro NU 630 is the traveling column member of the NU series and works differently from the trunnion machines beside it. Instead of tilting the part, it tilts the tool: a swivel head forms a controlled B axis with a ±110° range, and a rotary table set into the fixed work table supplies the 360° C axis.

The Chevalier UNi5X-400 is a compact five-axis vertical machining center with a tilting and rotating table Ø12.6 in (Ø320 mm) across. The trunnion carries 220 lb (100 kg), tilts through 150° (+30° / -120°) on the A axis and turns 360° on the C axis, so a part can be cut on five sides and at compound angles without being re-clamped.

The Chevalier UNi5X-800 is a large five-axis machining center with a Ø31.5 in (Ø800 mm) rotary table that carries 2,866 lb (1,300 kg). It is a different class of machine from the UNi5X-400, which shares the name: that model's table takes 220 lb (100 kg), and this one weighs 44,092 lb (20,000 kg) against 15,510 lb (7,050 kg).

Length is open-ended on the Emco Dynamill. The longitudinal axis starts at 4500 mm and more (in steps of 2500 mm), so the gantry is built to the part and not the other way round. Cross travel is 3000 / 4000 mm and vertical travel 1500 / 2000 / 2500 mm (2500 mm only for S version).

The Emco Maxxmill 630 is a compact vertical machining centre for 5-sided machining in a single set-up. A swivel-rotary table of 630x500 mm sits under a moving-column spindle, with travels of 500+50 mm in X, 460 mm (18.1 in) in Y and 450 mm (17.7 in) in Z. Emco notes that the machine is now also available in a 3-axis version.

Emco calls the Maxxmill 750 a machine for 4+1-axis machining. In practice that means a moving-column vertical spindle over a 750x600 mm swivel-rotary table, used to reach five sides of a part in one clamping. Linear travels are 750+50 mm, 610 mm (24.0 in) and 500 mm (19.7 in) in X, Y and Z.

The Emco Megamill is the heavy gantry in the range, built for torque. Its standard spindle motor is 40 kW 1200 Nm, with 50 kW 1500 Nm (S1) / 61 kW 1800 Nm (S6) as the option. The longitudinal axis starts at 7500 mm and more (in steps of 2500 mm), cross travel is 4000 / 5000 / 6000 / 7000 mm and vertical travel 1500 / 2000 / 2500 mm.

The Emco MMV 3200 is a travelling-column machining centre with 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of X travel over a fixed table of 3500x1050 mm. It is the shortest of four MMV lengths. The column carries a swivelling head, which is why the spindle clearance is given twice: 0-950 mm (vertical) / 250 - 1200 mm (horizontal).

Bulky, heavy workpieces are what Emco built the Powermill for. This gantry milling machine has a longitudinal travel of 6000 mm and more (in parts of 2000 mm), a cross travel of 4000 / 5000 / 6000 / 7000 mm and a vertical travel of 1500 / 2000 / 2500 mm, with a box-in-box structure around a ram of 550 x 640 mm.

The Emco UMILL 630 is the smallest of Emco's universal machining centres for 5-axis simultaneous machining. Its swivel-rotary table measures 630x500 mm, is driven by torque motors with direct measuring systems, and swivels through +/- 100°. Linear travels are 500 mm (19.7 in), 460 mm (18.1 in) and 450 mm (17.7 in).

With 750 mm (29.5 in) of X travel and a 750x600 mm swivel-rotary table, the Emco UMILL 750 is the mid-size machine in Emco's simultaneous 5-axis range. It keeps the moving-column layout of the smaller UMILL 630 and scales up the table, the load and the magazine.

The Emco UMILL 1000 moves Emco's 5-axis simultaneous machining into a gantry structure. Travels are 900 mm (35.4 in) in X, 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Y and 700 mm (27.6 in) in Z, and the swivel-rotary table takes 1,000 kg (2,205 lb). That is more than twice the load of the UMILL 750 , on a machine that weighs 18,000 kg (39,683 lb).

The Emco UMILL 1500 is a 5-axis gantry machine that mills and turns. Its three linear axes travel 1,500 mm (59.1 in), 1,500 mm (59.1 in) and 1,100 mm (43.3 in), and the part sits on an NC rotary table that comes in two forms: a milling table of 1400 x 1200 mm for 6,000 kg (13,228 lb), or a mill-turn table of ø 1400 mm that spins at up to 260 rpm.

Ten tonnes on a rotary table under a 5-axis head: the Emco UMILL 1800 carries 10,000 kg (22,046 lb) on its 1700 x 1400 mm milling table and 6,000 kg (13,228 lb) on the ø 1800 mm table for mill-turn operations. X travel is 1,800 mm (70.9 in) and Z travel 1,250 mm (49.2 in). Emco's brochure and its product page state different Y travels, so that row is left out here and should be confirmed.

The Fadal VM5ax320 is the one trunnion machine in the Fadal range: a 5-axis vertical with a 320 mm (12.60 in) rotary table that tilts on the A axis from +30° to -120° and turns 360° on C. Linear travels are 460 mm (18.11 in) in X, 610 mm (24.01 in) in Y and 510 mm (20.07 in) in Z. Unlike the VMC models, whose tables Fadal gives in inches, this one is specified in metric first.

The Feeler RG-3020 is a gantry machining center with a five-axis head, built for high-speed machining of large aluminium parts. It is the shortest of four RG models: 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z, over a 2,000 x 3,000 mm table.

Six metres of X travel puts the Feeler RG-6020 in the size class where one machine can hold two large parts end to end. X is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y is 2,000 mm (78.7 in), Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in), and the table is listed as 2,000 x 6,000 mm.

The Feeler RG-9020 extends the RG gantry to 9,000 mm (354.3 in) of X travel. Cross travel is 2,000 mm (78.7 in), vertical travel 1,200 mm (47.2 in), and the spindle is the series' 20,000 rpm HSK-A63 unit in a five-axis head.
Longest of the RG gantries, the Feeler RG-12020 travels 12,000 mm (472.4 in) in X. Y travel is 2,000 mm (78.7 in) and Z travel 1,200 mm (47.2 in). Feeler prints the table as 2,000 x 12,000 mm.

The Feeler U-250 is a compact 5-axis machining center for small parts, with a φ250 mm tilting rotary table and a 7/24 No.30 spindle that runs to 10,000 rpm. Feeler's table marks the spindle DDS. Linear travels are 350 mm (13.8 in) in X, 300 mm (11.8 in) in Y and 250 mm (9.8 in) in Z.

Feeler's U-600P is a 5-axis machining center with a φ600 mm table and a 7/24 No.40 spindle, sized for mid-range parts up to 350 kg (772 lb). The linear travels are 465 mm (18.3 in) in X, 620 mm (24.4 in) in Y and 400 mm (15.7 in) in Z.

The Feeler U-800(T) is a gantry-type 5-axis machining center with a cradle-style φ800 mm table, the largest trunnion machine in the U series. The T in brackets marks a turning-capable variant: the taper row reads 7/24 Taper No.40(HSK63T) and the load row 1,200 (1,000) kg, with the bracketed values belonging to it.

Unlike the table-tilting machines in Feeler's U series, the UB-660 tilts the spindle. It is a moving column 5-axis machining center with a tilting head, a φ660 mm rotary C axis set into a fixed table area of 1,450 x 700 mm, and 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of X travel.

The Feeler VUX-300 is a small 5-axis machining center on a vertical frame: a φ210 mm tilting rotary table, a 12,000 rpm spindle with a 7/24 No.40 taper, and travels of 510 mm (20.1 in) in X, 420 mm (16.5 in) in Y and 395 mm (15.6 in) in Z. Feeler heads the series 4+1 axis and calls it a cost-effective entry into 5-axis machining.

Milling and turning on one small 5-axis table is what the Feeler VUX-300T adds to the VUX series. Feeler says the model emphasizes flexible milling and turning integration, and the spindle interface changes accordingly, from the 7/24 taper of the VUX-300 to HSK-A63.

In the middle of the VUX series, the Feeler VUX-400 carries a φ350 mm tilting rotary table rated 200/100 (H/V) kg. Travels are 650 mm (25.6 in) in X, 520 mm (20.5 in) in Y and 480 mm (18.9 in) in Z, and the spindle is a 12,000 rpm unit with a 7/24 No.40 taper.

The Feeler VUX-500 is the largest VUX model, with a φ410 mm table and the biggest envelope of the series: 750 mm (29.5 in) in X, 650 mm (25.6 in) in Y and 600 mm (23.6 in) in Z. Its spindle is a 12,000 rpm No.40 unit.

The Fehlmann PICOMAX 550 is a compact 5-axis machining center with 550 mm (21.7 in) of X travel and 400 mm (15.7 in) each in Y and Z. The swivelling B axis covers 180° (+135° / -45°), C turns 0° - 360°, and the maximum swing circle for 5-axis milling is 500 mm with a workpiece height up to 370 mm.

The Fidia ARIAL 3 is the smallest machine in the ARIAL range of 5-axis high-speed gantry milling centres for composites, resins, plastics, aluminium and light alloys. Axis travels are 2,900 mm (114.2 in) in X, 1,740 mm (68.5 in) in Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) in Z.

The Fidia ARIAL 4 takes the compact ARIAL gantry and stretches its Y axis to 4,300 mm (169.3 in). X travel is 2,900 mm (114.2 in) and Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in), in a 5-axis machine for composites, resins, plastics, aluminium and light alloys.

The Fidia ARIAL 40 is the shortest of Fidia's moving-beam ARIAL gantries, with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X, 1,800 mm (70.9 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. It is a 5-axis high-speed machine for composites, resins, plastics, aluminium, light alloys and wood.

The Fidia ARIAL 40L is the extended-Y version of the ARIAL 40 : X travel stays at 4,000 mm (157.5 in) and Y grows to 2,600 mm (102.4 in). Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in). It is a 5-axis moving-beam gantry for composites, plastics, resins and light alloys.

At 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel, the Fidia ARIAL 50 is the middle size of the moving-beam ARIAL gantries. Y travel is 1,800 mm (70.9 in) and Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in). The machine is a 5-axis high-speed milling centre for composites, resins, plastics, aluminium and light alloys.

The Fidia ARIAL 50L combines 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X with the extended 2,600 mm (102.4 in) Y of the L versions, plus 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. It is a 5-axis moving-beam gantry aimed at composites, resins, plastics, aluminium and light alloys.
The Fidia ARIAL 60 is the longest standard-width ARIAL: 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel, with 1,800 mm (70.9 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z, in a moving-beam 5-axis gantry.

The Fidia ARIAL 60L has the largest working envelope in the ARIAL range: 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X, 2,600 mm (102.4 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. Like its siblings it is a 5-axis moving-beam gantry for high-speed work in composites, resins, plastics, aluminium, light alloys and wood.

The Fidia Linea C3 is a 5-axis gantry for composites, the shortest of the three Linea C sizes, with 2,200 mm (86 in) of X, 3,000 mm (118 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47 in) of Z. What sets the line apart from Fidia's metal-cutting gantries is everything built around dust.

The Fidia Linea C4 is the mid-length composites gantry in Fidia's Linea range, with 4,500 mm (177 in) of X travel, 3,000 mm (118 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47 in) of Z. It machines CFRP, honeycomb, multi-layer composites and ceramic matrix composites in 5 continuous axes.
The Fidia Linea C6 is the longest Linea C composites gantry, at 6,200 mm (244 in) of X travel. Y travel is 3,000 mm (118 in) and Z is 1,200 mm (47 in), the same cross-section as the shorter sizes.

Description: The Fidia UHE 1000 is a 5-axis universal machining centre that splits its rotary axes between a swivelling head and a rotary table. Linear travels are 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in X, 800 mm (31.5 in) in Y and 700 mm (27.6 in) in Z, and the 1,000 x 800 mm (39.4 x 31.5 in) table carries 1,500 kg (3,307 lb).

The Fidia UHE 1600 is the heavy-duty model of Fidia's 5-axis universal machining centres, with travels of 1,620 mm (63.8 in) in X, 1,260 mm (49.6 in) in Y and 1,050 mm (41.3 in) in Z. Its rotary table is Ø 1,400 mm (55.1 in) and takes 4,000 kg (8,818 lb).

The Fidia VSE865-RT is the 5-axis member of the VSE family: a C-frame vertical machine with a roto-tilting table in place of the plain table. Linear travels are 800 mm (31.5 in) in X, 610 mm (24 in) in Y and 510 mm (20 in) in Z, at 30 m/min (1,118 ipm).

Fooke designed the ENDURA 400LINEAR for shops that live mainly in plastics. The Fooke ENDURA 400LINEAR is the smallest compact gantry in the ENDURA range: a 5-axis milling machine with 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of X, a choice of 2,000 / 3,000 mm in Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z, for large workpieces in plastics, CFRP/GFRP, modeling block material and aluminum.

The Fooke ENDURA 600LINEAR is a walk-in gantry milling machine for full-size models and large light-material parts. Its overhead portal travels 5,000 - 30,000 mm in X, with 2,800 / 3,500 mm of Y and 1,500 / 2,000 / 2,300 mm of Z. Fooke calls it the entry model for 1:1 processing in vehicle design, which is the classic use: a complete car body in clay or block material, milled from all sides in one set-up.

The Fooke ENDURA 900LINEAR Compact brings the metal-cutting side of the ENDURA range onto a closed, self-supporting bed. It is a 5-axis linear motor gantry for aluminium, cast iron and steel, with 3,500 mm (137.8 in) of Y, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of Z and an X travel listed as 2,500 / 4,000 / 5,500 mm.

Length is the whole idea of the Fooke ENDURA 1000LINEAR, a 5-axis long bed gantry milling machine whose X travel is listed as 5,000 - 60,000 mm. Y is 4,500 mm (177.2 in) and Z is 1,600 / 1,900 / 2,100 mm. Fooke says the design can be manufactured in almost any length and names its main trade plainly: aluminum profiles for rail technology.

The Fooke ENDURA PRO LINEAR is a profile milling machine: a 5-axis long bed gantry for stringers and other long, slender structural parts in aluminum and composites. X travel is 6,000 - 60,000 mm. Y is narrow by gantry standards at 1,600 / 2,400 / 3,100 mm, and Z is 1,100 / 1,500 mm.

The Fryer 5X-60 is a 5-axis machining center in which the spindle does the tilting and rotating and the part stays flat on the table. Travels are 60 x 30 x 35 in (1,524 x 762 x 889 mm) on linear ways, and the head, which Fryer identifies as a Kessler 2-axis unit, gives an A travel of +/- 95° and a C travel of +/- 200°.

The Fryer 5X-100 extends the articulating-head 5-axis concept to 100 in (2,540 mm) of X travel. It keeps the 18,000 rpm, 35 hp (26.1 kW) peak spindle and linear ways of the 5X-60 and sets them over a 30 x 112 in (762 x 2,845 mm) table. Y travel is 35 in (889 mm) and Z travel 34 in (864 mm).

The Fryer 5X-120 is the heavy-cutting member of the 5X articulating-head series. Against the 5X-100 it moves from linear ways to box ways, from a 35 hp (26.1 kW) spindle to 55 hp (41.0 kW) peak, and from 4,500 lb of axis thrust to 10,800 lb. Travels are 120 x 50 x 40 in (3,048 x 1,270 x 1,016 mm) over a 40 x 126 in (1,016 x 3,200 mm) table.

With 160 in (4,064 mm) of X travel the Fryer 5X-160 is the largest 5-axis machine in the 5X series. It has the box way frame and 55 hp (41.0 kW) peak spindle of the 5X-120 on a longer bed: a 40 x 165 in (1,016 x 4,191 mm) table, 50 in (1,270 mm) of Y, 40 in (1,016 mm) of Z and a 2-axis head with +/- 105° of A travel.

The Fryer SX-45 is a 5-axis machining center that splits its rotary axes between the head and the table. The spindle head swivels through a B travel of +/- 110°, and a rotary table supplies the C axis. Linear travels are 45 x 25 x 25 in (1,143 x 635 x 635 mm) on roller type linear ways.

The Fryer SX-60 offers 60 x 30 x 35 in (1,524 x 762 x 889 mm) of travel under a tilting spindle head, and its 35 in of Z is the detail that matters most. A head that swivels +/- 110° needs height: with the spindle laid over toward horizontal, the 11 in (279 mm) between spindle nose and centre of rotation swings out sideways, and the machine must lift the head clear of the part first. The SX-60 has that height, where the SX-45 has 25 in (635 mm) of Z.

The Fryer SX-80 is the large model of the SX tilting-head 5-axis series, with 80 x 35 x 34 in (2,032 x 889 x 864 mm) of travel. Two things grow besides the stroke: the table load reaches 10,000 lb (4,536 kg), and the built-in rotary table is 30 in (762 mm) where the SX-60 lists 24 in (610 mm). Fryer's series text names the 30” flush mounted table specifically for the SX-80.

The Hartford 5A-65E is the mid-size simultaneous 5-axis vertical machining center of the 5A series, with a Ø 650 mm (25.6 in) table that carries 500 kg (1,102 lb). Linear travels are 650 mm (25.6 in) in X, 520 mm (20.5 in) in Y and 460 mm (18.1 in) in Z. The B axis tilts +110° ~ -40° and C rotates 360°.

A 15 / 18.5 kW motor option on a trunnion machine with a Ø 650 mm (25.6 in) table: the Hartford 5A-65EF is the 4+1 axis version of the 5A-65 and the one with the heavier spindle drive. Travels are 650 mm (25.6 in), 520 mm (20.5 in) and 460 mm (18.1 in) in X, Y and Z.

The Hartford 5A-95Q is the largest trunnion-table machine in the 5A series, here in its 4+1 axis form. The table is Ø 800 mm (31.5 in) and carries 850 kg (1,874 lb). X travel is 950 mm (37.4 in), Y is 850 mm (33.5 in) and Z is 650 mm (25.6 in).

Hartford's 5A-95Q-5X, written 5A-95Q / 5X on the maker's site, is the simultaneous 5-axis version of its largest trunnion machine. An 850 kg (1,874 lb) part on a Ø 800 mm (31.5 in) table can be tilted ±120° on the A axis and turned 360° on C while the spindle contours it.

The Hartford 5A-350XL combines the travels of a normal 3-axis vertical machining center with a small tilting rotary table. X travel is 650 mm (25.6 in), Y is 610 mm (24.0 in) and Z is 510 mm (20.1 in), while the table is only Ø 350 mm (13.8 in). Hartford lists it as a 4+1 axis machine.

The Hartford Aero-432B has 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel and 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y over a table of 4,000 x 2,700 mm (157.5 x 106.3 in). It is the four-metre entry to Hartford's Aero gantry type 5-faced machining centers.

The Hartford Aero-432BL-5X is a four-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in), Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in), and the table measures 4,000 x 2,700 mm (157.5 x 106.3 in). Z travel is 1,100 mm, with 1,300 mm optional.

With a 4,000 x 3,100 mm (157.5 x 122.0 in) table and 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y travel, the Hartford Aero-436B is the wider of the two four-metre gantry type 5-faced machining centers in the Aero series. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in).

The Hartford Aero-536B is the narrowest of three five-metre models in the Aero range of gantry type 5-faced machining centers. Its table is 5,000 x 3,100 mm (196.9 x 122.0 in), with 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel and 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y.

The Hartford Aero-536BL-5X is a five-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center. It has 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel, 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y, 1,100 mm of Z with a 1,300 mm option, and a 5,000 x 3,100 mm (196.9 x 122.0 in) table.

Y travel of 4,100 mm (161.4 in) and a 5,000 x 3,600 mm (196.9 x 141.7 in) table place the Hartford Aero-541B in the middle of the five-metre Aero models. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in). Hartford describes the machine as a gantry type 5-faced machining center.

Hartford's Aero-541BL-5X is the middle of three five-metre gantry type 5-axis machining centers. The table is 5,000 x 3,600 mm (196.9 x 141.7 in), X travel 5,000 mm (196.9 in), Y travel 4,100 mm (161.4 in), and Z travel 1,100 mm or optionally 1,300 mm.

The Hartford Aero-546B is the widest five-metre model of the Aero gantry type 5-faced machining centers. Its table measures 5,000 x 4,100 mm (196.9 x 161.4 in), Y travel is 4,600 mm (181.1 in) and X travel 5,000 mm (196.9 in).

The Hartford Aero-546BL-5X spans 4,600 mm (181.1 in) in Y over a table of 5,000 x 4,100 mm (196.9 x 161.4 in). With 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel it is the widest five-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center in the Aero series.

The Hartford Aero-631G does not follow the pattern of the other six-metre Aero machines. It has 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel and 3,100 mm (122.0 in) of Y, and its table, 6,000 x 3,100 mm (236.2 x 122.0 in), is exactly as wide as the Y travel.

Six metres long and 2,700 mm wide at the table, the Hartford Aero-632B is the slim model among the six-metre Aero gantry type 5-faced machining centers. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in), and the table measures 6,000 x 2,700 mm (236.2 x 106.3 in).

Six metres of X travel over a table 2,700 mm wide: the Hartford Aero-632BL-5X is the slim six-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center of the Aero series. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in), and the table 6,000 x 2,700 mm (236.2 x 106.3 in).

The Hartford Aero-636B is a six-metre gantry type 5-faced machining center with a 6,000 x 3,100 mm (236.2 x 122.0 in) table, 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel and 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y travel. Among the four B models at this length it is the second narrowest.

The Hartford Aero-636BL-5X is a gantry type 5-axis machining center with a 6,000 x 3,100 mm (236.2 x 122.0 in) table. Travels are 6,000 mm (236.2 in) in X, 3,600 mm (141.7 in) in Y and 1,100 mm in Z, with 1,300 mm of Z optional.

A 6,000 x 3,600 mm (236.2 x 141.7 in) table and 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of Y travel define the Hartford Aero-641B. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in). The machine is a gantry type 5-faced machining center, one size below the widest six-metre Aero.

The Hartford Aero-641BL-5X has 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of Y travel above a 6,000 x 3,600 mm (236.2 x 141.7 in) table, with 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel. It is a gantry type 5-axis machining center from the six-metre group of the Aero series.

The Hartford Aero-646B is the largest of the B models in the Aero series of gantry type 5-faced machining centers. The table is 6,000 x 4,100 mm (236.2 x 161.4 in), X travel 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y travel 4,600 mm (181.1 in).

The Hartford Aero-646BL-5X is the largest Aero 5X machine with the L designation. Its table is 6,000 x 4,100 mm (236.2 x 161.4 in), X travel 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y travel 4,600 mm (181.1 in) and Z travel 1,100 mm, optionally 1,300 mm.
Hartford's Aero-836G is an eight-metre gantry type 5-faced machining center: 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel, 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y, and a table of 8,000 x 3,100 mm (315.0 x 122.0 in).

The Hartford Aero-841G sits in the middle of the eight-metre Aero models. It is a gantry type 5-faced machining center with a table of 8,000 x 3,600 mm (315.0 x 141.7 in), 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel and 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of Y travel.

The Hartford Aero-841G-5X is an eight-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center with a table of 8,000 x 3,600 mm (315.0 x 141.7 in). X travel is 8,000 mm (315.0 in), Y travel 4,100 mm (161.4 in), and Z travel 1,100 mm with 1,300 mm optional.

Eight metres by 4,100 mm of table, with 4,600 mm (181.1 in) of Y travel: the Hartford Aero-846G is the widest eight-metre gantry type 5-faced machining center in the Aero series. X travel is 8,000 mm (315.0 in) and the table measures 8,000 x 4,100 mm (315.0 x 161.4 in).

Eight metres by 4,100 mm of table and 4,600 mm (181.1 in) of Y travel: the Hartford Aero-846G-5X is the widest eight-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center in the Aero series. X travel is 8,000 mm (315.0 in), and the table measures 8,000 x 4,100 mm (315.0 x 161.4 in).

Ten metres of X travel on a table 3,100 mm wide: the Hartford Aero-1036G is the longest and slimmest format in the Aero series. In full, X travel is 10,000 mm (393.7 in), Y travel 3,600 mm (141.7 in) and the table 10,000 x 3,100 mm (393.7 x 122.0 in). Hartford classes it as a gantry type 5-faced machining center.

The Hartford Aero-1036G-5X is a ten-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center in the narrowest Aero cross section. X travel is 10,000 mm (393.7 in), Y travel 3,600 mm (141.7 in), Z travel 1,100 mm (1,300 mm optional), and the table 10,000 x 3,100 mm (393.7 x 122.0 in).

The Hartford Aero-1041G is a ten-metre gantry type 5-faced machining center with 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of Y travel. Its table is 10,000 x 3,600 mm (393.7 x 141.7 in) and its X travel 10,000 mm (393.7 in).

With 10,000 mm (393.7 in) of X travel and 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of Y, the Hartford Aero-1041G-5X is the mid-width ten-metre gantry type 5-axis machining center of the Aero series. Its table is 10,000 x 3,600 mm (393.7 x 141.7 in).

The Hartford Aero-1046G is the largest machine in the Aero series of gantry type 5-faced machining centers. It has a 10,000 x 4,100 mm (393.7 x 161.4 in) table, 10,000 mm (393.7 in) of X travel and 4,600 mm (181.1 in) of Y travel.

The Hartford Aero-1046G-5X is the largest 5-axis machine in Hartford's tables. It is a gantry type 5-axis machining center with a 10,000 x 4,100 mm (393.7 x 161.4 in) table, 10,000 mm (393.7 in) of X travel, 4,600 mm (181.1 in) of Y travel and 1,100 mm of Z, or 1,300 mm optionally.

The Hartford Aero-2225B is the smallest gantry type 5-faced machining center in the Aero series. X travel is 2,200 mm (86.6 in), Y travel 2,500 mm (98.4 in), and the table measures 2,200 x 2,000 mm (86.6 x 78.7 in).

The Hartford Aero-2225BL-5X is the compact model of the Aero gantry type 5-axis machining centers. X travel is 2,200 mm (86.6 in), Y travel 2,500 mm (98.4 in), Z travel 1,100 mm with 1,300 mm optional, and the table measures 2,200 x 2,000 mm (86.6 x 78.7 in).

On the Hartford Aero-2232B the table is wider than it is long. It measures 2,200 x 2,700 mm (86.6 x 106.3 in), under 2,200 mm (86.6 in) of X travel and 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y. Hartford classes the machine as a gantry type 5-faced machining center.

A table of 2,200 x 2,700 mm (86.6 x 106.3 in) and 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y travel make the Hartford Aero-2232BL-5X wider than it is long. X travel is 2,200 mm (86.6 in). It is a gantry type 5-axis machining center, the wide one of the two compact Aero 5X models.

The Hartford HSA-220EA is the smallest of the HSA five-face double-column machining centers: 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of travel in both X and Y over a 2,000 x 1,800 mm (78.7 x 70.9 in) table that carries 8,000 kg (17,637 lb). Hartford calls the type a Double Column 5 Faced Machining Center, and the side faces are reached with automatic angular heads that live in a switching head compartment.

The Hartford HSA-220EAY is a two-metre five-face double-column machining center whose Y axis reaches far outside its table. Y travel is 2,800 mm (110.2 in) while the table is 2,000 x 1,800 mm (78.7 x 70.9 in). X travel is 2,000 mm (78.7 in) and the table load 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).

A three-metre table only 1,800 mm wide defines the Hartford HSA-320EA. X travel is 3,000 mm (118.1 in), Y travel 2,000 mm (78.7 in), and the 3,000 x 1,800 mm (118.1 x 70.9 in) table takes 10,000 kg (22,046 lb). It is a five-face double-column machine, so side faces are cut with automatic angular heads kept in a switching head compartment.

Hartford gives the HSA-320EAY a 3,000 x 1,800 mm (118.1 x 70.9 in) table and 2,800 mm (110.2 in) of Y travel. The first figure says long, narrow parts; the second says those parts are meant to be machined along their sides. X travel is 3,000 mm (118.1 in) and the table carries 10,000 kg (22,046 lb).

The Hartford HSA-323EA is where the three-metre five-face HSA gets a wider table. It measures 3,000 x 2,200 mm (118.1 x 86.6 in), Y travel grows to 2,300 mm (90.6 in), and the T-slots step up to the 28 size where the HSA-320EA has 22. X travel stays at 3,000 mm (118.1 in).

A 3,000 x 2,200 mm (118.1 x 86.6 in) table, 3,100 mm (122.0 in) of Y travel and 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel: on the Hartford HSA-323EAY the gantry is wider than the machine is long. The table load is 10,000 kg (22,046 lb).

Take the 3,000 x 2,200 mm (118.1 x 86.6 in) table of the three-metre HSA five-face line, add Y travel, and the result is the Hartford HSA-327EA. Its Y axis covers 2,700 mm (106.3 in). The table, the 10,000 kg (22,046 lb) load and the 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X are unchanged from the HSA-323EA , which stops at 2,300 mm (90.6 in) of Y.

No three-metre machine in Hartford's five-face HSA family has more cross travel than the HSA-327EAY. Its Y axis covers 3,500 mm (137.8 in). The table underneath is 3,000 x 2,200 mm (118.1 x 86.6 in), rated for 10,000 kg (22,046 lb), and X travel is 3,000 mm (118.1 in).

Four metres long and 1,800 mm wide: the Hartford HSA-420EA is the slimmest of the four-metre five-face HSA machines. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in), Y travel 2,000 mm (78.7 in), and the 4,000 x 1,800 mm (157.5 x 70.9 in) table carries 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) on fifteen T-slots.

The Hartford HSA-420EAY combines a slim 4,000 x 1,800 mm (157.5 x 70.9 in) table with 2,800 mm (110.2 in) of Y travel. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in) and the table is rated for 12,000 kg (26,455 lb). It is the narrowest four-metre model of the long-Y five-face HSA line.

The Hartford HSA-423EA pairs 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel with a 2,200 mm wide table and 2,300 mm (90.6 in) of Y. Table size is 4,000 x 2,200 mm (157.5 x 86.6 in) and the load rating 12,000 kg (26,455 lb). It is a five-face double-column machining center with linear guideways.

At four metres by 2,200 mm, the Hartford HSA-423EAY is a general-purpose size in the long-Y five-face HSA range. The table measures 4,000 x 2,200 mm (157.5 x 86.6 in), Y travel is 3,100 mm (122.0 in), X travel 4,000 mm (157.5 in), and the load rating 12,000 kg (26,455 lb).

With 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y travel over a 2,200 mm wide table, the Hartford HSA-427EA is the four-metre five-face HSA for parts whose long sides need machining. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in). The table measures 4,000 x 2,200 mm (157.5 x 86.6 in) and is rated for 12,000 kg (26,455 lb).

The Hartford HSA-427EAY has the longest Y travel of the 12,000 kg four-metre models: 3,500 mm (137.8 in), over a table of 4,000 x 2,200 mm (157.5 x 86.6 in). X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in). The load rating of 12,000 kg equals 26,455 lb.

The Hartford HSA-428EA is the heavy four-metre model of the five-face HSA line. Its 4,000 x 2,500 mm (157.5 x 98.4 in) table is rated for 18,000 kg (39,683 lb), half as much again as the 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) of the HSA-427EA , and travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X by 2,800 mm (110.2 in) in Y.

Heavy parts and long Y travel come together in the Hartford HSA-428EAY. The 4,000 x 2,500 mm (157.5 x 98.4 in) table is rated for 18,000 kg (39,683 lb), X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in), and the Y axis covers 3,600 mm (141.7 in).

Long and comparatively light, the Hartford HSA-523EA has 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel but keeps the 2,200 mm table width and 2,300 mm (90.6 in) Y travel of the smaller x23 models. The table is 5,000 x 2,200 mm (196.9 x 86.6 in), has nineteen T-slots and is rated for 15,000 kg (33,069 lb).

The Hartford HSA-523EAY is a five-metre five-face double-column machine for long parts of moderate weight that need their sides machined. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in), Y travel 3,100 mm (122.0 in), and the 5,000 x 2,200 mm (196.9 x 86.6 in) table carries 15,000 kg (33,069 lb).

The Hartford HSA-528EA carries 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) on a 5,000 x 2,500 mm (196.9 x 98.4 in) table. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in) and Y travel 2,800 mm (110.2 in), which makes it the entry point of the heavier five-metre models in the five-face HSA line.

With a 5,000 x 2,500 mm (196.9 x 98.4 in) table for 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) and 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y travel, the Hartford HSA-528EAY is a five-metre five-face machine built for heavy parts that need work on every side. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in).

On the Hartford HSA-532EA the Y axis travels 3,200 mm (126.0 in) above a table that is 2,500 mm wide. The table measures 5,000 x 2,500 mm (196.9 x 98.4 in), X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in), and the load rating is 20,000 kg (44,092 lb).

Y travel on the Hartford HSA-532EAY is 4,000 mm (157.5 in), and the table below it is 2,500 mm wide. No other five-metre model with this table has as much. The table measures 5,000 x 2,500 mm (196.9 x 98.4 in), takes 20,000 kg (44,092 lb), and X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in).

The Hartford HSA-536EA is the widest five-metre machine in the five-face HSA line: a 5,000 x 3,000 mm (196.9 x 118.1 in) table under 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y travel. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in) and the table is rated for 21,000 kg (46,296 lb).

The Hartford HSA-536EAY has a 5,000 x 3,000 mm (196.9 x 118.1 in) table and 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y travel. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in). The table is rated for 21,000 kg (46,296 lb), and the machine is a five-face double-column type that changes angular heads automatically.

The Hartford HSA-546AAC is a five-metre five-face double-column machining center built around a magazine of machining heads. Hartford's AAC multi-head magazine holds 3 to 5 heads, and the machine supports an automatic universal head, an automatic 90° angle head and an automatic extension head.

Six metres of X travel and a 23,000 kg (50,705 lb) table: the Hartford HSA-628EA is the narrow six-metre model of the five-face HSA line. Its table is 6,000 x 2,500 mm (236.2 x 98.4 in) with twenty-three T-slots, X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in) and Y travel 2,800 mm (110.2 in).

The Hartford HSA-628EAY is the six-metre long-Y five-face HSA with the 2,500 mm table. Figures: X travel 6,000 mm (236.2 in), Y travel 3,600 mm (141.7 in), table 6,000 x 2,500 mm (236.2 x 98.4 in), load 23,000 kg (50,705 lb).

The Hartford HSA-636EA puts a 6,000 x 3,000 mm (236.2 x 118.1 in) table under a cross-beam with 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y travel. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), the table rating 24,000 kg (52,910 lb). It is a double-column five-face machine with linear guideways.

Six metres by three, with a gantry that travels 4,400 mm (173.2 in): the Hartford HSA-636EAY is one of the large machines of the long-Y five-face line. X travel is 6,000 mm (236.2 in), the table 6,000 x 3,000 mm (236.2 x 118.1 in), the load rating 24,000 kg (52,910 lb).

There is one seven-metre model with a 2,500 mm wide table in Hartford's five-face HSA range, and it is the HSA-732EA. The table is 7,000 x 2,500 mm (275.6 x 98.4 in), X travel 7,000 mm (275.6 in), Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in), and the load rating 25,000 kg (55,115 lb).

Hartford's HSA-736EA is a seven-metre five-face double-column machine with a 7,000 x 3,000 mm (275.6 x 118.1 in) table rated for 27,000 kg (59,524 lb). X travel is 7,000 mm (275.6 in) and Y travel 3,600 mm (141.7 in).

The Hartford HSA-736EAY is the only seven-metre model in the long-Y five-face HSA line. Its table is 7,000 x 3,000 mm (275.6 x 118.1 in) and rated for 27,000 kg (59,524 lb), with 7,000 mm (275.6 in) of X travel and 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y.

The Hartford HSA-828EA stretches the 2,500 mm wide five-face HSA to its full length. X travel is 8,000 mm (315.0 in), the table 8,000 x 2,500 mm (315.0 x 98.4 in) with thirty-one T-slots, and the rating 27,000 kg (59,524 lb). Y travel is 2,800 mm (110.2 in).

The Hartford HSA-828EAY is an eight-metre five-face double-column machine: X travel 8,000 mm (315.0 in), Y travel 3,600 mm (141.7 in), table 8,000 x 2,500 mm (315.0 x 98.4 in), load 27,000 kg (59,524 lb).

Eight metres long, with 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y travel: the Hartford HSA-832EA is the version of the long, 2,500 mm wide five-face HSA meant for work on the flanks of a part. Table size is 8,000 x 2,500 mm (315.0 x 98.4 in), X travel 8,000 mm (315.0 in), table load 27,000 kg (59,524 lb).

Four metres of Y travel on a table 2,500 mm wide and eight metres long: the Hartford HSA-832EAY has the most generous side clearance of the long, narrow five-face HSA machines. Y travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in), X travel 8,000 mm (315.0 in), the table 8,000 x 2,500 mm (315.0 x 98.4 in) and its rating 27,000 kg (59,524 lb).

The Hartford HSA-836EA is the largest model in the EA five-face line and the only one rated for 30,000 kg (66,138 lb). The table is 8,000 x 3,000 mm (315.0 x 118.1 in); travel is 8,000 mm (315.0 in) in X and 3,600 mm (141.7 in) in Y.

The Hartford HSA-836EAY is the largest machine in the HSA five-face family by every measure in the table: 8,000 mm (315.0 in) of X travel, 4,400 mm (173.2 in) of Y travel, an 8,000 x 3,000 mm (315.0 x 118.1 in) table and a 30,000 kg (66,138 lb) load rating.

The HNK 5S-GPM puts five spindles on one gantry. HNK designs it for high-speed machining of aircraft frame parts, and the idea is plain: cut five identical parts in the time of one.

The HNK GPM-60FX is a ram-type 5-axis gantry profiler with a working area of 6,000 x 12,000 mm (236.2 x 472.4 in). The gantry runs 12,000 mm (472.4 in) in X, the head crosses 6,300 mm (248.0 in) in Y, and the ram drops 4,250 mm (167.3 in) in Z.
Two spindles side by side over a 20,000 mm (787.4 in) X stroke: the HNK GST-2S is a gantry profiler that HNK builds for aerospace parts such as panel stringers.

The HNK HAP-V3 is a compact profiler by HNK's standards: a 2,500 x 6,000 mm (98.4 x 236.2 in) table, 6,200 mm (244.1 in) of X and 2,800 mm (110.2 in) of Y. HNK describes it as a high-speed, high-precision 3-spindle profiling machine for aircraft parts.

The HNK HFM 10X20 is the smallest of HNK's 5-axis high-speed milling machines: a 1,000 x 2,000 mm (39.4 x 78.7 in) table under a universal head, with an HSK63-A spindle listed at 16,000 rpm and 30,000 rpm in braces.
A table three times as long as it is wide defines the HNK HFM 10X30. It measures 1,000 x 3,000 mm (39.4 x 118.1 in) and travels 3,700 mm (145.7 in) in X beneath a 5-axis universal head.

The HNK HFM 15X40 sits in the middle of the HFM 5-axis range, with a 1,500 x 4,000 mm (59.1 x 157.5 in) table and 4,700 mm (185.0 in) of X travel. It is the largest size that still lists the 16,000 rpm spindle as its first figure, with 30,000 rpm in braces.

From the HNK HFM 20X40 upward, the HFM table lists 30,000 rpm as the spindle speed with no lower figure beside it. This is the first of the three 2,000 mm wide machines: a 2,000 x 4,000 mm (78.7 x 157.5 in) table, 4,700 mm (185.0 in) of X and 2,100 mm (82.7 in) of Y.
Five metres of table at two metres wide: the HNK HFM 20X50 is the middle of the three large HFM 5-axis machines, measuring 2,000 x 5,000 mm (78.7 x 196.9 in) with 5,700 mm (224.4 in) of X travel.
The HNK HFM 20X60 is the largest HFM listed. Its 5-axis head works over a 2,000 x 6,000 mm (78.7 x 236.2 in) table that travels 6,700 mm (263.8 in) in X.

The Hurco BM500U is a five-axis machining center with a 500 mm (19.7 in) × 500 mm (19.7 in) table and 850 mm (33.46 in) of X travel over 500 mm (19.7 in) of Y and 500 mm (19.7 in) of Z. Its CAT 40 spindle runs to 15,000 rpm with 11 kW (14.8 hp) and 70 Nm (51.6 ft-lb), and all three linear axes rapid at 35 m/min (1,377 ipm).
