The Huron GU3 Five is the smallest of the GU moving-gantry five-axis machining centres. It pairs a 320 mm rotary table with travels of 420 x 520 x 420 mm (16.5 x 20.5 x 16.5 in) and an 18,000 rpm electrospindle, in a machine that weighs 6,000 kg (13,228 lb) and stands on 3,000 x 2,000 mm.

The Huron GU5 Five is a moving-gantry five-axis machining centre built around a 500 mm rotary table. Travels are 600 x 700 x 500 mm (23.6 x 27.6 x 19.7 in) and the table carries 400 kg (882 lb), which places the machine in the most common size class for five-axis job-shop work.

Step up to a 650 mm table and 600 kg (1,323 lb) of load, and the GU range gives you the Huron GU6 Five. Its travels are 800 x 900 x 650 mm (31.5 x 35.4 x 25.6 in), and the spindle nose can be as much as 800 mm above the table plane.

The Huron GU8 Five is the largest GU model, a moving-gantry five-axis machining centre whose 800 mm rotary table carries 1,000 kg (2,205 lb). Linear travels are 1,000 x 1,100 x 650 mm (39.4 x 43.3 x 25.6 in).

The Huron K2X 10 Five puts a 630 mm two-axis table under the K2X high-speed portal, giving continuous five-axis machining on parts up to 750 kg (1,653 lb). Travels are 900 x 900 x 500 mm (35.4 x 35.4 x 19.7 in) with rapids of 50 m/min.

The Huron K3X 8 Five is a five-axis portal machining centre with a two-axis table mounted on a 55° plane. Linear travels are 780 x 700 x 500 mm (30.7 x 27.6 x 19.7 in), the table is 500 mm in diameter and the spindle is an 18,000 rpm HSK 63-A unit with 30 kW.

Three metres of X travel under a high-speed five-axis head: that is the Huron KX 50 L. Its travels are 3,000 x 1,700 x 900 mm (118.1 x 66.9 x 35.4 in), and the fixed table measures 3,300 x 1,250 mm with an admissible load of 6,000 kg (13,228 lb).

The Huron KX 50 M is a fixed-portal five-axis machining centre with a forked milling head and a 75 kW, 20,000 rpm spindle. Travels are 2,000 x 1,700 x 900 mm (78.7 x 66.9 x 35.4 in) over a fixed table of 2,200 x 1,250 mm. It is the shorter of the two KX 50 machines in what Huron calls the KX Large Series.

The Huron KX 100 is a double-column five-axis machining centre for heavy parts: a 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) table load, a square 2,300 x 2,300 mm X and Y stroke, and 1,000 mm of Z. Its forked head carries an 18,000 rpm HSK 63-A spindle with 240 Nm of torque.

The Huron KX 200 extends the KX 100 along X. It offers 3,300 x 2,300 x 1,000 mm (129.9 x 90.6 x 39.4 in) of travel and a fixed table of 3,500 x 1,250 mm, on the same double-column, forked-head design.

The Huron KX 300 is the largest fixed-portal machine in the KX Large Series: 5,000 x 3,100 x 1,500 mm (196.9 x 122.0 x 59.1 in) of travel and a 5,200 x 2,000 mm table rated for 20,000 kg (44,092 lb). Huron's series text speaks of work areas supporting up to 20 tonnes, and this is the model that figure belongs to.

The Huron MX 4 is a small five-axis machining centre driven by linear motors on Y and Z, with rapids of 120 m/min on those axes and 60 m/min on X. Travels are 750 x 700 x 500 mm (29.5 x 27.6 x 19.7 in), and the 24,000 rpm HSK 63-A spindle works over a 400 x 400 mm table that tilts and rotates.

The Huron MX 8 M is the milling version of the smallest universal-head MX machine. It has 1,160 x 1,000 x 900 mm (45.7 x 39.4 x 35.4 in) of travel, a rotary table rated for 2,000 kg (4,409 lb), and a 14,000 rpm HSK 63-A spindle with 277 Nm of torque.

Milling and turning in one clamping is the purpose of the Huron MX 8 MT. Its table is 800 mm in diameter and spins at up to 500 rpm, fast enough to turn diameters and faces on a part that is then milled, drilled and tapped without being moved.

The Huron MX 10 M is a five-axis universal-head milling centre with a square working plan: 1,200 mm (47.2 in) in both X and Y, and 1,000 mm in Z. The table is listed as Ø 1,250 x 900 mm and carries 2,000 kg (4,409 lb).

The Huron MX 10 MT combines a 1,000 mm turning table with a tilting universal milling head. The table reaches 500 rpm, and the HSK 100-A spindle delivers 43 kW and 415 Nm, so one machine covers lathe work on discs and rings up to a metre across plus full five-axis milling.

The Huron MX 11 M APC is the MX machine Huron lists with a pallet changer in its name. It is a five-axis universal-head milling centre with 1,250 x 1,250 x 1,000 mm (49.2 x 49.2 x 39.4 in) of travel and a rectangular table of 1,000 x 800 mm carrying 2,000 kg (4,409 lb).

The Huron MX 12 M doubles the table load of the smaller MX milling centres to 4,000 kg (8,818 lb). Its travels are 1,200 x 1,600 x 1,000 mm (47.2 x 63.0 x 39.4 in), with the long axis being Y, and the table is listed as Ø 1,600 x 1,250 mm.

With a 1,400 mm table that turns at 250 rpm, the Huron MX 12 MT brings mill-turn capability to parts well over a metre in diameter. It shares the 1,200 x 1,600 x 1,000 mm (47.2 x 63.0 x 39.4 in) travels of the MX 12 M and carries 3,000 kg (6,614 lb).

The Huron MX 16 M is a large five-axis milling centre: 2,300 x 2,300 x 1,250 mm (90.6 x 90.6 x 49.2 in) of travel and a 1,750 mm table that takes 10,000 kg (22,046 lb). From this size up, Huron fits the HSK 100-A spindle to the milling version as well as the mill-turn one.
The Huron MX 16 MT is a mill-turn centre for parts up to 5,000 kg (11,023 lb), with a 1,650 mm table that turns at 250 rpm inside a 2,300 x 2,300 x 1,250 mm (90.6 x 90.6 x 49.2 in) working volume.

The Huron MX 20 M is the largest MX milling centre, with 3,000 x 3,100 x 1,600 mm (118.1 x 122.0 x 63.0 in) of travel and a 2,200 mm table rated for 12,000 kg (26,455 lb). It applies the MX universal-head concept to parts the size of a small car.

The Huron MX 20 MT is a mill-turn centre with a 2,200 mm turning table. It carries 10,000 kg (22,046 lb), turns at up to 120 rpm, and sits inside travels of 3,000 x 3,100 x 1,600 mm (118.1 x 122.0 x 63.0 in). In effect it joins a vertical turning lathe and a five-axis machining centre in one frame.

The Huron Tachyon 4 Five is the Tachyon drilling-tapping centre fitted with a two-axis rotary table in place of the fixed one, which turns it into a small five-axis machine. Linear travels are 400 x 400 x 450 mm (15.7 x 15.7 x 17.7 in). The table plate is 200 mm in diameter and carries 30 kg (66 lb).

The Huron U Mill 5 is a compact five-axis machining centre with a fixed portal and a swivelling rotary table on a cradle. Travels are 500 x 560 x 450 mm (19.7 x 22.0 x 17.7 in), the table is 500 mm in diameter, and the ISO 40 spindle produces 173 Nm at up to 10,000 rpm.

The Huron U Mill 6 scales the U Mill concept up to a 630 mm table and 600 kg (1,323 lb) of workpiece. It is a fixed-portal five-axis machining centre with a swivelling rotary table on a cradle, and its travels are 700 x 740 x 550 mm (27.6 x 29.1 x 21.7 in).

The Hwacheon SIRIUS-2500/5AX is a large-format five-axis machining center: 3,100 mm (122.0 in) of X, 2,300 mm (90.6 in) of Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Z over a 3,300 x 2,000 mm (129.9 x 78.7 in) table rated for 10,000 kgf (22,046 lb). Because the table is a fixed rectangle with nine 22 mm T-slots at 200 mm pitch, the two rotary axes have to be in the head: B swings ±100° and C turns ±210°.

The Hwacheon SIRIUS-3000/5AX is the bigger of Hwacheon's two SIRIUS five-axis machines, with a 3,500 x 3,000 mm (137.8 x 118.1 in) table rated for 20,000 kgf (44,092 lb) and travels of 3,500 mm (137.8 in) in X, 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in Y and 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Z. The rotary motion is in the head, with B at ±120° and C at 300°, so the workpiece never has to be tilted.

The Ibarmia P26 is the smallest of the P26, P30 and P36, a 5-axis machining center for parts up to 2,600 mm (102.4 in) in swing diameter and 1,750 mm (68.9 in) tall. Ibarmia lists it in two versions: P Extreme for 5-axis milling, and P Multiprocess, which adds turning to the 5-axis milling.

The Ibarmia P30 sits in the middle of the P series: a 5-axis machining center with a 3,000 mm (118.1 in) maximum swing diameter and room for parts 1,950 mm (76.8 in) high. Below it the P26 is listed at 2,600 mm (102.4 in) by 1,750 mm (68.9 in), above it the P36 at 3,600 mm (141.7 in) by 2,150 mm (84.6 in).

At 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of swing diameter and 2,150 mm (84.6 in) of part height, the Ibarmia P36 has the largest work envelope of the P26, P30 and P36. It is a 5-axis machining center sold as P Extreme, for milling, or as P Multiprocess, where turning joins the 5-axis milling.

The Ibarmia T12 is the entry size of the T series, a 5-axis machining center whose envelope is taller than it is wide: 1,600 mm (63.0 in) of part height over a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) maximum swing diameter. That proportion sets it apart from the big end of the range. The T36, for comparison, swings 3,600 mm (141.7 in) but allows only 2,150 mm (84.6 in) of height.

The Ibarmia T16 is a 5-axis machining center for parts up to 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in swing diameter and 1,700 mm (66.9 in) high. In its T Multiprocess form, which turns as well as mills, the maximum turning load is 3,000 kg (6,614 lb). The T Extreme version is the milling-only 5-axis machine.

The Ibarmia T22 is a 5-axis machining center whose two versions come with different tables. T Extreme, the milling version, has a 1,250 x 1,250 mm (49.2 x 49.2 in) table. T Multiprocess, which turns and mills, has a rotary table of ø1,600 mm (63.0 in). Either way the envelope is a 2,200 mm (86.6 in) maximum swing diameter with 1,750 mm (68.9 in) of part height.

The Ibarmia T30 is a large T-series 5-axis machining center with a rectangular table on its milling version: the T Extreme lists 1,250 x 1,600 mm (49.2 x 63.0 in). The maximum swing diameter is 3,000 mm (118.1 in) and the maximum part height 1,950 mm (76.8 in).

The Ibarmia T36 tops the T series. This 5-axis machining center takes a maximum swing diameter of 3,600 mm (141.7 in), a part height of 2,150 mm (84.6 in), and in T Extreme form carries a 1,600 x 1,600 mm (63.0 x 63.0 in) table.

The Ibarmia ZLS5 is the large construction size of the Z series with the tilting ZS head. It lists 84 kW (112.6 hp) and 12,000 rpm on SK-50, BT-50, HSK A-100 or CAPTO 8 tool holders. Ibarmia's phrase for its size steps is "larger columns for even more powerful spindles", and this model is where that leads.

The Ibarmia ZMS4 is the medium-size member of the Z series of moving-column machining centers that takes SK-40 class tooling, built around the tilting ZS head. Its spindle is listed at 46 kW (61.7 hp) and 12,000 rpm, and the tool holder is a choice of SK-40, BT-40, HSK A-63 or CAPTO 6. X travel is built to order, up to 12,000 mm (472.4 in).

The Ibarmia ZMS4_30.08 Extreme Star Edition is a moving-column machining center with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel, 800 mm (31.5 in) each of Y and Z, and a tilting head on an SK-40 or HSK A-63 spindle. The table describes its ZS head as a continuous tilting head with a torque motor, giving 4-axis movement, and puts the B-axis range at +/- 120º.
Big tool holders on a medium column: that is the Ibarmia ZMS5. It takes SK-50, BT-50, HSK A-100 or CAPTO 8 tooling in a tilting ZS head, with a spindle listed at 43 kW (57.7 hp) and 8,000 rpm.

The Ibarmia ZMS5_30.08 Extreme Star Edition pairs a long work envelope with a big-taper spindle: SK-50 or HSK A-100, 43 kW (57.7 hp) and 8,000 rpm. Travels are 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X and 800 mm (31.5 in) in both Y and Z, on a moving-column structure.

Among the Large DMC models, the Johnford DMC-4000x2800-R2-AC4 is the high-speed one. Its head carries a spindle that runs from 50 to 20,000 rpm with 21 / 24 kW (28.2 / 32.2 hp), on a machine with 4,000 mm (157.4 in) of X, 3,600 mm (141.7 in) of Y and 1,066 mm (42 in) of Z.

The Johnford DMC-4000x2800-R2-AC5 carries the stronger of the two R2 heads on the Large DMC frame. Spindle power is 31 / 40 kW (41.6 / 53.6 hp), the highest in this group's table, across a speed range of 50~10,000 rpm. The taper is No.50 in the AC51 version and HSK A100 in the AC52 version.

Two heads on one eleven-metre bed: the Johnford SDMC-11000x3200x1066-2H-5F is a twin-spindle portal machining center. The table labels its travels X1/X2, Y1/Y2 and Z1/Z2, 11,000 mm (433 in), 3,200 mm (126 in) and 1,066 mm (42 in), and its tool storage as 60x2 arm type, one 60-tool changer for each head.

The Johnford SDMC-11000x3200x1400-2H-TU35 is a twin-head, five-axis portal machining center. Each head adds a B axis stroke of ±180° and a C axis stroke of 0 - 360° to linear travels of 11,000 mm (433.1 in), 3,200 mm (126 in) and 1,400 mm (55.1 in).

The JTEKT FA1050S 5-Axis is a box-way horizontal machining center with a trunnion table, built for heavy five-axis cutting. Its pallet is 41.33 x 41.33 in (1,050 x 1,050 mm) and carries 4,400 lb (2,000 kg). Travels are 59.05 in (1,500 mm) in X, 55.11 in (1,400 mm) in Y and 45.27 in (1,150 mm) in Z.

The JTEKT FH630SX-i 5-Axis is a horizontal machining center with a tilting spindle head on a 24.8 x 24.8 in (630 x 630 mm) pallet. The fifth axis is in the head, not under the part: JTEKT gives the head a 230° swivel range, while the pallet carries the workpiece as on a four-axis horizontal.

The JTEKT FH1250SX 5-Axis is a large horizontal machining center with an integral tilting spindle, sized for parts up to 11,000 lb (5,000 kg) on a 49.21 x 49.21 in (1,250 x 1,250 mm) pallet. Spindle speed is 15,000 RPM on a CAT50 taper. JTEKT describes the machine as capable of 4+1 or full simultaneous 5-axis machining.

The Juaristi TH3-MGX8 is the smaller of the two TH-series 5-axis universal machining centers: a table-type machine with a central head, a rotary table rated at 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) and X travel offered at 2,000, 3,000 or 4,000 mm. Y and Z each come in three steps, 1,500, 2,000 or 2,500 mm.

The KAAST V-Mill 600.5X is a 5-axis machining center built around a Ø600 mm (23 in) tilting rotary table, with 820 mm (32 in) of X travel, 750 mm (29.5 in) of Y and 500 mm (19 in) of Z. The spindle is a BT 40 unit running to 15,000 rpm, and KAAST lists the control as the Heidenhain iTNC 530.

The KAAST V-Mill 620.5X is a compact 5-axis machining center: 620 mm (24 in) of X travel, 520 mm (20 in) of Y and 460 mm (18 in) of Z over a Ø650 mm (25 in) table, in a machine that weighs 8,200 kg (18,070 lb). It runs a 12,000 rpm SK 40 spindle under the Heidenhain TNC 640 control.

The KAAST V-Mill 1000.5X is a 5-axis machining center with a rectangular 1000x800 mm table rated for 1,500 kg. The standard spindle is a BT 40 unit with 16,000 rpm, 15 / 22.5 kW and 48/72 Nm, and KAAST lists the control as the Heidenhain iTNC 640.

The Matec 30P | 40P turns the layout around: the table stands still and the gantry carries all the axis movements. That lets MATEC offer X travel from 3,000 to 40,000 mm (118.1 to 1,574.8 in), far beyond the 6,750 mm of the moving-table 30PT | 40PT , because the table no longer has to travel its own length.

The Matec 30PB | 40PB is the floor-running version of MATEC's moving gantry machine. The gantry travels beside a table set at shop-floor level, which MATEC sums up as ground-level accessibility: parts and fixtures can be brought to the table without lifting them onto a raised bed.

The Matec 30PBU | 40PBU pairs MATEC's floor-running moving gantry with a 2-axis universal head. MATEC puts the advantage of this version in two things: the versatility of the head and the accessibility of the workpiece, which stands on a table at floor level.
Stationary gantry | Moving table with pallet change

The Matec 30PPT | 40PPT combines the two productivity features of MATEC's gantry range: a pallet changer under the gantry and a torque fork head on the ram. The first keeps the spindle cutting while the next part is clamped; the second is the head listed with spindle speeds to 24,000 rpm.

Pallet change and a universal head come together in the Matec 30PPU | 40PPU. It is the version of MATEC's PP series for parts that are both slow to set up and awkward to reach: the pallet takes the setup out of the work area, and the head rotates ±180° in A and in C.

The Matec 30PT | 40PT is a 5-axis gantry machining centre with a stationary gantry and a moving table, fitted with a 2-axis fork head. MATEC lists it in two performance classes, HSK63 and HSK100, and as a set of sizes: X travel of 3,750, 4,750, 5,750 or 6,750 mm, Y of 3,400 or 4,400 mm and Z of 1,500, 1,800 or 2,100 mm (59.1, 70.9 or 82.7 in).

The Matec 30PTR | 40PTR adds an integrated CNC rotary table to MATEC's stationary gantry, moving table design. In place of the rectangular clamping table of the 30PT | 40PT , the table row lists a rotary table of Ø 1,800 or Ø 2,200 mm (Ø 70.9 or Ø 86.6 in).

The Matec 30PTT | 40PTT is the direct-drive member of MATEC's stationary gantry family. Its 2-axis fork head has direct drive in both axes, and MATEC names the applications plainly: volume machining in high-strength light metals, and tool and mould making with higher demands on precision and surface quality.

A 2-axis universal head with ±180° of rotation in both A and C is what defines the Matec 30PTU | 40PTU. The machine under it is MATEC's stationary gantry with a moving table, offered in the HSK63 and HSK100 performance classes with SIEMENS or HEIDENHAIN control.

On the Matec 30PU | 40PU, a 2-axis universal head rides a moving gantry over a stationary table. It is the long-bed machine in MATEC's range for work that needs the spindle at any angle: X travel is 3,000 to 40,000 mm and the head's swivel radius is 440 mm (17.3 in).

The Matec 50PB is the largest floor-running gantry MATEC lists, and the only one with a W axis. In addition to the Z axis in the ram, the whole gantry beam adjusts in height automatically, by 800 mm (31.5 in) or optionally 1,100 mm (43.3 in).

The Matec FUV170T is a travelling column machine with two work areas on one bed: a rigid table of 700 x 500 mm for 3-axis work and a swivel turntable with a Ø 650 mm (Ø 25.6 in) face plate for 5-axis work. The column covers 1,700 mm (66.9 in) in X, 540 mm (21.3 in) in Y and 460 mm (18.1 in) in Z, so it can serve either table or, as MATEC puts it, run pendulum and long bed machining.

With 1,900 mm (74.8 in) of X travel, the Matec FUV190T is the longer of MATEC's two travelling column 5-axis machining centres. The extra length goes entirely into the rigid table, which measures 900 x 500 mm and is rated for 1,600 kg (3,527 lb). Y and Z stay at 540 mm (21.3 in) and 460 mm (18.1 in).

The Matec FUV620 is the smaller of MATEC's two 5-axis universal machining centres with a swivelling rotary table. Travels are 620 x 520 x 460 mm (24.4 x 20.5 x 18.1 in), the table's clamping surface is Ø 650 mm (Ø 25.6 in), and the B axis swivels the table from -50° to +110° while the C axis turns a full 360°.

At 10,320 kg (22,751 lb), the Matec FUV720 is the larger and heavier of MATEC's two swivel-table 5-axis universal machining centres. It moves 720 mm (28.3 in) in X, 600 mm (23.6 in) in Y and 520 mm (20.5 in) in Z over a rotary table with a Ø 720 mm (Ø 28.3 in) clamping surface. MATEC's text describes the face plate as Ø 720 x 540 mm, which suggests a round plate with flats rather than a full circle.

The Matec FUV800 is a 5-axis machining centre in gantry design: the spindle travels 800 mm (31.5 in) in X, 920 mm (36.2 in) in Y and 650 mm (25.6 in) in Z above a swivel bridge carried in the machine's side walls. The table has an 800 mm (31.5 in) clamping surface, tilts 120° to either side in A and rotates 360° in C.

The Matec FUV800 B puts an HSK100 | SK50 spindle on MATEC's 5-axis gantry machining centre. The frame is the one used for the HSK63 machine: 800 x 920 x 650 mm (31.5 x 36.2 x 25.6 in) of travel, an 800 mm (31.5 in) table on a swivel bridge between the side walls, and 21,000 kg (46,296 lb) of machine weight. What changes is the tooling the spindle can carry.

The Milltronics VM200-5X is a compact 5-axis vertical machining center with a 7.8 in (198 mm) diameter rotary table, 21 x 16 x 19 in (533 x 406 x 483 mm) of X, Y and Z travel and a 10,000 rpm BIG-PLUS ISO No. 40 spindle. The C axis turns through 360° and the A axis tilts from +30° to -110°. That A range passes the right angle on one side, which gives the tool access to undercut faces without a second clamping.

The Milltronics VM250IL-5X sits above the VM200-5X as the bigger 5-axis vertical, pairing a 9.8 in (249 mm) rotary table with 30 x 20 x 20.5 in (762 x 508 x 521 mm) of linear travel and a 40-tool double-arm changer. Its BIG-PLUS ISO No. 40 spindle is listed at 12,000 rpm (15k optional). Next to the VM200-5X, with its 7.8 in (198 mm) table and 24 tools, this is a much more substantial machine: 13,068 lb (5,928 kg) against 7,738 lb (3,510 kg), about 69% heavier.

The Onsrud 140EX is the shortest EX-Series machine, a 5-axis machining center for aluminum and composite extrusions. The work area is 21 x 14 in (533 x 356 mm) in cross-section, the Z-stroke is 40 in (1,016 mm), and the spindle is 33 hp (24.6 kW) at 24,000 rpm.

The Onsrud 165X is the shortest model of the X-Series, Onsrud's lighter 5-axis line for extrusion machining. It has a work area of 21 x 14 in (533 x 356 mm), a 28 in (711 mm) Z-stroke and an 18 hp (13.4 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle.

With two material stop zones and 10-12 clamps, the Onsrud 265EX is the first EX-Series length that can run pendulum-style on extrusions. It is a 5-axis machining center, 418 in (10,618 mm) long, with a 33 hp (24.6 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle.

The Onsrud 291X is the X-Series model at 418 in (10,618 mm) of machine length, and the shortest with two material stop zones. It is a 5-axis extrusion machine with an 18 hp (13.4 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle and a 28 in (711 mm) Z-stroke.

The Onsrud 375EX is the mid-length EX-Series extrusion machining center: 531 in (13,488 mm) of machine, 12 clamps, 2 material stop zones. The 5-axis head is driven by a 33 hp (24.6 kW) spindle at 24,000 rpm and has 40 in (1,016 mm) of Z-stroke.

The Onsrud 401X measures 523 in (13,285 mm) in length and carries 12 clamps, the full count for the X-Series. It is a 5-axis machine for linear profile extrusions, with an 18 hp (13.4 kW) spindle at 24,000 rpm and 28 in (711 mm) of Z-stroke.

At 649 in (16,485 mm) the Onsrud 501EX is the second-longest EX-Series machine, built for extrusions that most machining centers cannot hold in one piece. It is a 5-axis machine with a 33 hp (24.6 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle, a 40 in (1,016 mm) Z-stroke and a work area cross-section of 21 x 14 in (533 x 356 mm).

The Onsrud 527X is the longest X-Series model with a complete set of published dimensions: 649 in (16,485 mm) long, 131 in (3,328 mm) wide and 140 in (3,556 mm) high. It machines extrusions on five axes with an 18 hp (13.4 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle.

The Onsrud 627EX is the longest machine in the EX-Series table, at 782 in (19,863 mm). It is a 5-axis extrusion machining center with a 33 hp (24.6 kW) spindle, 24,000 rpm, and a 40 in (1,016 mm) Z-stroke over a 21 x 14 in (533 x 356 mm) work area.

The Onsrud F98HM is the smaller of two HM-Series hybrid mills: a fully enclosed machine with twin tables of 60 in (1,524 mm) by 48 in (1,220 mm) each, a 40 in (1,016 mm) Z-stroke and a 33 hp (24.6 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle. Onsrud lists it with its 5-axis mills.

The Onsrud F144Q is the one model of the Q-Series, a fully enclosed 5-axis machine for high-speed trimming. Its table is 144 in (3,657 mm) by 60 in (1,524 mm), the Z-stroke is 40 in (1,016 mm), and the spindle is 18 hp (13.4 kW) at 24,000 rpm.

The Onsrud F148CH is the base model of the CH-Series, a fully enclosed compact high-rail mill. The table is 84 in (2,134 mm) by 142 in (3,607 mm), the Z-stroke is 52 in (1,321 mm), and the standard spindle is 33 hp (24.6 kW) at 24,000 rpm. Onsrud lists the series among its 5-axis mills.

The Onsrud F148CH W10 is the wide-table variant of the F148CH . It keeps the 142 in (3,607 mm) table Y and stretches table X to 120 in (3,048 mm), inside the same fully enclosed high-rail structure with a 52 in (1,321 mm) Z-stroke.

The Onsrud F148HM is the larger HM-Series hybrid mill, with twin tables of 60 in (1,524 mm) by 72 in (1,829 mm) inside a full enclosure. The standard spindle is 33 hp (24.6 kW) at 24,000 rpm and the Z-stroke is 40 in (1,016 mm).

The Onsrud F192CHW10 is the largest CH-Series mill Onsrud lists, with a table of 120 in (3,048 mm) by 190 in (4,826 mm). It is fully enclosed, has a 52 in (1,321 mm) Z-stroke, and carries a 33 hp (24.6 kW), 24,000 rpm spindle as standard.

Description: The PAMA Speedmat HP is the five-axis member of the Speedmat family. It keeps the T-type layout, a travelling table in front of a moving column, but the headstock carries a tilting milling head with a continuous A axis, not a boring bar. PAMA lists it under five-axis machining centers and builds it in seven sizes.

The PAMA Speedmat VM is the compact one in the catalogue: a five-axis vertical machining centre with a fixed portal, a crossrail that moves vertically and a table that travels beneath it. PAMA builds three sizes, for maximum workpiece diameters of 1500 mm, 2000 mm and 3000 mm.

The Pinnacle AX170 is the smallest AX 5-axis machining center: a Ø170 mm (Ø6.7 in) trunnion table with direct-drive A and C axes under a 15,000 rpm spindle. Linear travels are 360 mm (14.2 in) in X and Y and 440 mm (17.3 in) in Z.

The Pinnacle AX260 is a compact 5-axis machining center built around a BBT30 spindle and a Ø260 mm (Ø10.2 in) trunnion table. Travels are 510 mm (20.1 in) in X, 455 mm (17.9 in) in Y and 380 mm (15.0 in) in Z, and it is the fastest AX model in a straight line at 48 / 48 / 48 m/min.

The Pinnacle AX320 is a 40-taper 5-axis machining center with a Ø320 mm (Ø12.6 in) tilting rotary table and travels of 660 mm (26.0 in) in X and 610 mm (24.0 in) in Y and Z. It is the first AX model built on a full-size vertical machining center frame, at 6,500 kg (14,330 lb).

The Pinnacle AX450 gives the AX trunnion design a Ø450 mm (Ø17.7 in) table and a symmetrical tilt: the A axis swings 220°(±110°). Linear travels are 760 mm (29.9 in) in X, 610 mm (24.0 in) in Y and 560 mm (22.0 in) in Z.

The Pinnacle AX500 is the largest AX trunnion machine, with a Ø500 mm (Ø19.7 in) table driven by DD motors on both rotary axes. It shares its 760 mm (29.9 in), 610 mm (24.0 in) and 560 mm (22.0 in) travels with the AX450 but moves the table much faster: the A/C feed rate is 30/90 rev/min.

The Pinnacle BX300A is a swivel-head 5-axis machining center whose rotary table can be taken off. With the Ø 320 mm (Ø 12.6 in) table removed, the 1,300 x 610 mm (51.2 x 24.0 in) fixed table is free and the machine works as a 4-axis machine with a tilting spindle, a point Pinnacle makes explicitly for the BX A models.

The Pinnacle BX500 is a 5-axis machining center with a ± 120° swivel head and a Ø500 mm (Ø19.7 in) rotary table embedded in the main table and driven directly at 50 rpm. X travel is 1,300 mm (51.2 in) and Y 610 mm (24.0 in).

The Pinnacle BX500A combines a ± 120° swivel head with a detachable Ø 500 mm (Ø 19.7 in) rotary table on a 1,450 x 610 mm (57.1 x 24.0 in) fixed table. X travel is 1,300 mm (51.2 in), Y 610 mm (24.0 in) and Z 810 mm (31.9 in).

The Pinnacle BX500DD is the BX500 with direct-drive motors on both rotary axes. The B-axis head swivels ± 120° at up to 50 rpm and clamps with 2,950 Nm (2,175.9 lb-ft); the embedded Ø500 mm (Ø19.7 in) C-axis table also turns at 50 rpm.

The Pinnacle BX700 is a swivel-head 5-axis machining center with a Ø640 mm (Ø25.2 in) direct-drive rotary table built into a 1,600 x 700 mm (63.0 x 27.6 in) main table. Travels are 1,400 mm (55.1 in) in X and 710 mm (28.0 in) in Y, with Z listed as Vertical Milling 680 / Horizontal Milling 810 mm.

The Pinnacle BX700A is the heavy member of the BX A group, a swivel-head machine weighing 11,000 kg (24,250 lb) with a Ø 630 mm (Ø 24.8 in) separate rotary table. Travels are 1,400 mm (55.1 in), 710 mm (28.0 in) and 810 mm (31.9 in).
The Pinnacle BX700DD puts a direct-drive motor in the B-axis head of the BX700 . The head swivels ± 120° at 50 rpm, against 16.6 rpm on the worm-gear BX700, and clamps with 2,950 Nm (2,175.9 lb-ft).

The Pinnacle BX700T adds turning to the BX700DD . Its embedded Ø640 mm (Ø25.2 in) table is listed at 50(M) / 1,200(T) rpm, milling and turning, and the spindle takes HSK63T tooling so that a turning tool can be locked in the milling spindle.

The Pinnacle BX900 is the largest swivel-head model in the BX line: 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of X, 900 mm (35.4 in) of Y, and Z of Vertical 1,000 / Horizontal 1,100 mm. A Ø800 mm (Ø31.5 in) direct-drive rotary table is built into the 1,700x850 mm (66.9x33.5 in) main table.

The Pinnacle BX900DD is the direct-drive version of the BX900 , with DD motors on both the B-axis head and the Ø800 mm (Ø31.5 in) C-axis table. Each rotary axis is listed at 50 rpm, and the head clamps with 2,950 Nm (2,175.9 lb-ft).
The Pinnacle BX900T is the mill-turn version of the BX900 platform. The Ø800 mm (Ø31.5 in) table is listed at 50(Mill) / 800(Turn) rpm and the built-in spindle takes HSK63T tooling.

The Quaser MF500 is a multiple face / 5-axis vertical machining center with a Ø410 mm (Ø16.14") rotary table, sized for parts up to Ø500 x 300 mm (Ø19.6" x 11.8") and 300 kg (661.38 lbs). Linear travels are 550 mm (21.65") in X, 630 mm (24.80") in Y and 610 mm (24.02") in Z.

Quaser's MF700 is a 5-axis machining center with a column-moving C frame and a Ø650 mm (Ø25.59") rotary table, taking parts up to Ø700 x H500 mm (Ø27.56" x H19.69") and 500 kg (1102.30 lbs). Its design idea is separation: the three linear axes are on the column side, the rotary axes are on the table side, and the two never stack.

The Quaser MF700 (Flex) stretches the MF700 to 1680 mm (66.14") of X travel and puts two work platforms under one spindle: a rotary table and a fixed table. Quaser calls this a dual platform design and lets the user choose rotary or fixed table for each job.

The Quaser MK3000 (#40) is a 5-axis travelling column machining center for large components, with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel over a fixed 3,300 x 850 mm (129.9 x 33.5 in) table. This page covers the lighter of its two spindle classes: HSK-A63 or SK/BT40, listed at 15K ~ 24K.

In its heavier spindle class, the Quaser MK3000 (#50) takes HSK-A100 or SK/BT50 tooling on a built-in spindle listed at 10K ~ 15K. The machine around it is a 5-axis travelling column design with linear motors in X and Y, 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel and a 3,300 x 850 mm (129.9 x 33.5 in) table.

The Quaser MTG500 is a compact gantry-type 5-axis machining center whose rotary table Quaser says is specifically designed for high-speed mill/turn and grinding applications. It is also the only machine in the maker's range listed with an HSK T63 spindle interface.

The Quaser UX500 is a compact 5-axis machining center with a Ø410 mm (Ø16.1") table and a fixed 12K maximum spindle speed. It handles parts up to Ø540 x 400 mm (Ø21.3" x 15.8") weighing no more than 200 kg (441 lbs), with linear travels of 712 mm (28.0") in X, 540 mm (21.3") in Y and 515 mm (20.3") in Z.

Quaser describes the UX500APC as a highly versatile five-axis VMC with automatic pallet changer. The pallet is □400 mm (□15.8"), the maximum work piece is Ø500 x 350 mm (Ø19.7" x 13.8"), and the load capacity is 200 kg (441 lbs).

A double column structure is what distinguishes the Quaser UX600C from the rest of the maker's 5-axis machines. It carries a Ø500 mm (Ø19.7") table between the columns, takes work pieces up to Ø630 x 425 mm (Ø24.8" x 16.7") and 300 kg (661 lbs), and runs a 40 taper spindle at a listed 12K.

The Quaser UX600P is the higher-specification model on Quaser's double column 5-axis frame. Its table is listed as Ø600 x W500 mm (Ø23.6" x W19.7"), a diameter and a width, which suggests a round table with flats on two sides. It holds work pieces up to Ø600 x 430 mm (Ø23.6" x 16.9") and 300 kg (661 lbs).

The Quaser UX630 is a 5-axis machining center for medium-size parts: a Ø480 mm (Ø18.9") table carrying 500 kg (1,102 lbs), a maximum work piece of Ø630 x 600 mm (Ø24.8" x 23.6"), and a B-axis that Quaser gives as +/- 120 degrees.

Take the UX630 platform, add an automatic pallet changer, and the result is the Quaser UX630APC: a 5-axis machining center with a □500 mm (□19.7") pallet, a Ø630 mm (Ø24.8") swing and linear travels of 900 mm (35.4"), 660 mm (26.0") and 610 mm (24.0").

The Reiden RX10 is the smallest of the four RX 5-axis machining centers Reiden lists, with 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of X, 1,100 mm (43.3 in) of Y and 810 mm (31.9 in) of Z. The two rotary axes are split between head and table. An automatic swiveling head, listed as standard, takes the spindle between horizontal and vertical (A axis 0+/-90°), and an NC rotary table of Ø 1,000 x 800 mm supplies the 360° C axis. Reiden describes it as a compact machine with a very small footprint and considerable processing space in relation to its dimensions.

The Reiden RX12 is a 5-axis machining center with 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of X and 1,450 mm (57.1 in) of Y that can also turn. With the spindle clamped and the optional rotary table fitted, the workpiece itself becomes the turning axis: the table lists a Ø 1,200 mm (47.2 in) turning rotary table running at 400 rpm with a maximum torque of 4,570 Nm (3,371 lb-ft). Reiden's point is that the part no longer has to change machines between milling and turning. The model was launched in 2016.

The Reiden RX14 is a 5-axis machining center with a square 1,800 x 1,800 mm (70.9 in) X/Y field and 1,210 mm (47.6 in) of Z, built around what Reiden calls the trigonal milling head. The head carries a single A axis in a special arrangement, and Reiden states that dihedral angles from 0° to +105° can be machined with only that one axis. The table lists the A axis as +/- 105° and the C axis, in the rotary table, as 360°.

The Reiden RX18 is the largest machine in Reiden's RX range: a 5-axis machining center with 2,200 mm (86.6 in) of travel in both X and Y, 1,610 mm (63.4 in) in Z and a weight of 52,000 kg (114,638 lb). It was also the first of the range to turn. Reiden's history lists the RX18 for 2011 as its first 5-axis machining center with turning function, and a fully automatic pallet change system with turning function followed in 2015.

Simultaneous 5-axis machining is the purpose of the ROMI DCM 620-5X. It shares its casting, travels and trunnion table with the 5F model, and what Romi changes is the control and the spindle: a Siemens Sinumerik One runs all five axes together, and the only headstock offered is the 15,000 rpm one.

The Sharp SVX-160-F is the smallest of Sharp's trunnion-table 5-axis machining centers, built for parts that fit a 6.3 in (160 mm) C-axis platter and weigh no more than 132 lb (60 kg). X travel is 25.2 in (640 mm) and Y is 17.1 in (435 mm); the C axis turns a full 360°.

Sharp's SVX-300-F puts an 11.8 in (300 mm) rotary platter on a tilting trunnion inside a C-frame machining center with 29.92 in (760 mm) of X, 23.62 in (600 mm) of Y and 19.69 in (500 mm) of Z. The A axis tilts from -120 to +30° and the C axis rotates 360°, so the spindle can reach five sides of a part and undercut past horizontal on one side.

Unlike the two smaller SVX machines, the Sharp SVX-500-F is a box-in-box design: the spindle head moves in X and Y on top of a closed casting while the trunnion, anchored to the side walls, carries the part. Travels are 23.6 in (600 mm) in X, 31.9 in (810 mm) in Y and 19.7 in (500 mm) in Z, with A tilting -110 to +20° and C turning 360°.

The SW BA space5-12H is the longest machine in SW's range: 4,800 mm (189.0 in) of X travel, with 1,800 mm (70.9 in) of Y and 875 mm (34.4 in) of Z. It appears on SW's BA space5 page as the only model.

The MCG810i is an upper-gantry machining centre with a fixed table: the workpiece stays still on a 1,200 × 1,000 mm (47.2 × 39.4 in) clamping plate while the cross rail, cross slide and ram carry the spindle over it. Travels are 1,000 mm in X, 800 mm in Y and 600 mm in Z. In base form it is a three-axis machine; a two-axis CNC head or a two-axis rotary table, both optional, turn it into a five-axis one.

Two work tables under one gantry: the MCG820i stretches the Y axis of the ZPS small gantry to 1,800 mm (70.9 in) and puts a 1,200 × 2,000 mm clamping surface beneath it, made up of two fixed tables. X is 1,000 mm and Z is 600 mm.

Five-axis machining on a horizontal spindle is what the MCH800i FIVE AXIS offers. Tajmac-ZPS takes the MCH800i base, with its 1,000 x 1,050 x 1,200 mm travels, and replaces the B-axis table with a two-axis tilting rotary table: an A axis that tilts through 210° (±105°) and a C axis that rotates 360°. The brochure abbreviates the model as MCH800i FA.

The MCH1000i FIVE AXIS pairs the longest X travel in the ZPS horizontal range, 1,400 mm (55.1 in), with a tilting rotary table. On that table sits an 800 × 800 mm pallet or a ø 940 mm clamping plate, one size larger than its five-axis sibling carries. Y is 1,050 mm and Z 1,200 mm; the A axis covers 210° (±105°) and the C axis 360°.

The Tongtai CT-350 is a compact five-axis machining center built around a Ø350 mm (Ø13.8 in) table that carries up to 200 kg (441 lb). Linear travels are 400 mm (15.7 in) in X and 510 mm (20.1 in) in both Y and Z. The A axis is listed at +30 ~ -120° and the C axis at ±360°, so the tilt runs well past a right angle in one direction and a tool can reach undercut faces without a second setup.

The TOS Kuřim FRPN-A 150-400 is the compact portal machine of the range: a fixed gantry and fixed cross-rail with the table moving underneath. X travel comes in three lengths, 3,000/4,000/5,000 mm (118.1/157.5/196.9 in), which makes it far shorter than the travelling-gantry series.

One column of the catalogue covers two headstock classes, which is why the TOS Kuřim FRPN-B (C) 200-400 carries both letters. It is a fixed-gantry, fixed-cross-rail machining centre with a movable table. The table travels 5,500 - 13,500 mm (216.5 - 531.5 in) in X.

The Vision Wide ADM-2638 is a 5-axis machining center for composite materials, built around a 24,000 rpm spindle and two tables of 2,500 x 1,500 mm (98.4 x 59.1 in) each. Travels are 2,600 mm (102.4 in) in X, 3,800 mm (149.6 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z.

The Vision Wide ASM-1012 is a five-axis universal machining center built around a round table and a 45° universal head. The table is Ø1,000 mm (Ø39.4 in) and carries 2,000 kg (4,409 lb) in its central area; travels are 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in X, 1,260 mm (49.6 in) in Y and 1,050 mm (41.3 in) in Z.
A Ø1,200 mm (Ø47.2 in) table is what the Vision Wide ASM-1212 adds over the smallest ASM, with X travel growing to 1,250 mm (49.2 in). Y and Z stay at 1,260 mm (49.6 in) and 1,050 mm (41.3 in).

The Vision Wide ASM-1612 is the large-table ASM with the fast spindle. Its table is Ø1,500 mm (Ø59.1 in) and takes 3,000 kg (6,614 lb) in the central area, X travel is 1,620 mm (63.8 in), and the spindle speed is 10,000 rpm.

The G version trades speed for a slower, heavier spindle. The Vision Wide ASM-1612G lists a spindle speed of 7,000 rpm and a Z rapid of 24 m/min, where the ASM-1612 lists 10,000 rpm and 40 m/min on all three axes.

The Vision Wide FA-2123 is the smallest of the FA bridge-type five-axis machining centers, a moving-table double-column machine with a two-axis head. Travels are 2,100 mm (82.7 in) in X and 2,300 mm (90.6 in) in Y, with 800 mm of Z and 1,000 mm as an option.

Measurement is built into the Vision Wide FA-2623. The standard accessory list includes Blum TC 60 auto measurement compensation of rotation axis accuracy, and the feature list adds auto measurement compensation for tool accuracy. A five-axis machine is only as accurate as its knowledge of where the rotary axes really are, and here the machine checks that itself.

With the Vision Wide FA-3027 the FA series changes spindle. The table lists 12,000 rpm on an HSK-A100 taper, 34 / 43 kW (45.6 / 57.7 hp) and 162 / 205 Nm (119 / 151 lb-ft). Against the FA-3123 , which has the same 3,100 mm (122.0 in) X travel and 30 / 36 Nm (22.1 / 26.6 lb-ft), that is more than five times the torque.
The widest FA frame starts with the Vision Wide FA-3033. Port width is 2,700 mm (106.3 in), Y travel is 3,300 mm (129.9 in), and the table measures 3,000×2,450 mm (118.1×96.5 in).

The Vision Wide FA-3123 is the longest FA with the high-speed spindle: 3,100 mm (122.0 in) of X travel, 2,300 mm (90.6 in) of Y, and a 3,300x1,600 mm (129.9x63.0 in) table rated for 14,000 kg (30,864 lb).

The Vision Wide FA-4027 is a four-metre bridge-type five-axis machining center: 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of X travel, 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y, and a 4,000×1,800 mm (157.5×70.9 in) table for 12,000 kg (26,455 lb).

Sixteen tonnes on a five-axis machine: the Vision Wide FA-4033 has a 4,000×2,450 mm (157.5×96.5 in) table rated for 16,000 kg (35,273 lb), with 4,100 mm (161.4 in) of X travel and 3,300 mm (129.9 in) of Y.

Heat is the enemy of a five-metre five-axis machine, and the Vision Wide FA-5033 is sold with figures on the subject. Vision Wide says the FA is not affected by spindle thermal variation and environment temperature change, with thermal elongation less than 0.02mm, and that spindle vibration stays lower than 1 mm/sec.

The Vision Wide FA-6033 and the NF-6026 have the same table: 6,000×2,450 mm (236.2×96.5 in), rated for 22,000 kg (48,501 lb), under 6,100 mm (240.2 in) of X travel. What sits above the table is different, and the difference is the choice between five-axis and five-face machining.

Eight metres is as long as the FA series goes. The Vision Wide FA-8033 has 8,100 mm (318.9 in) of X travel, 3,300 mm (129.9 in) of Y, and an 8,000×2,450 mm (315.0×96.5 in) table that carries 24,000 kg (52,910 lb).

The Vision Wide GSF-1627 is a five-axis gantry machining center with a two-axis head. The table is fixed; the gantry carries a head whose B and C axes tilt and swivel a built-in spindle while X, Y and Z move, so all five axes can cut at once.

Rotary-axis quality decides what a five-axis head can finish, and the Vision Wide GSF-2227 states its figures. The B and C axes are driven without backlash, with a rotation positioning accuracy of ±5 arc-seconds, and the dynamic five-axis accuracy (TCPM) is given as 0.04mm.

The wide frame of the GSF series begins with the Vision Wide GSF-2232, which spans 3,200 mm (126.0 in) in Y on a gantry stroke of 2,200 mm (86.6 in). Its fixed table measures 2,200 x 3,200 mm (86.6 x 126.0 in).

When is continuous five-axis worth having over an indexing head? The Vision Wide GSF-3027 and the GSA-3027 pose the question directly: both are gantries with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel and 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y, both have a 15,000 rpm spindle, and the GSF is the one whose B and C axes move during the cut.

Tool capacity is the row to look at on the Vision Wide GSF-3032. The specification table lists 20/32/40/60 pcs, four sizes, while the accessory lists name a vertical type tool magazine 20T as standard and a 32T magazine as the option, and say nothing of 40 or 60.
Four head versions are listed for the Vision Wide GSF-4027, a five-axis gantry with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel and 2,700 mm (106.3 in) of Y.
A fixed table of 4,000 x 3,200 mm (157.5 x 126.0 in), rated 3,000 kg/m2, sits under the five-axis gantry of the Vision Wide GSF-4032. X travel is 4,000 mm (157.5 in) and Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in).

The Vision Wide GSF-5027 is one of the few machines in the maker's range offered with a choice of two five-axis controls. A HEIDENHAIN TNC640 controller is standard, and a SIEMENS 840D SL controller is the option.

Keeping a five-axis head accurate over years of work is a maintenance question as much as a design one, and the Vision Wide GSF-5032 comes with part of the answer built in. X travel is 5,000 mm (196.9 in), Y travel 3,200 mm (126.0 in), and the table 5,000 x 3,200 mm (196.9 x 126.0 in).

Six metres of X travel and a five-axis head make the Vision Wide GSF-6027 a machine for long parts with contoured surfaces: 6,000 mm (236.2 in) in X, 2,700 mm (106.3 in) in Y, over a 6,000 x 2,700 mm (236.2 x 106.3 in) fixed table.
The Vision Wide GSF-6032 is the largest five-axis gantry in the GSF series, with 6,000 mm (236.2 in) of X travel, 3,200 mm (126.0 in) of Y and a 6,000 x 3,200 mm (236.2 x 126.0 in) fixed table.

The WELE UG630 is a 5-axis machining center with a 650 mm (25.6 in) table that tilts on the B axis and rotates on C, under linear travels of 640 mm (25.1 in) in X, 520 mm (20.4 in) in Y and 460 mm (18.1 in) in Z. The spindle runs to 12,000 rpm and is listed as #40, in BBT, CAT, DIN or HSK A63 form.

Five axes in a cabinet 910 mm wide: that is the Willemin-Macodel 308S2. It takes the 270 mm, 120 mm and 220 mm travels of the 301S2 and puts a swivelling spindle and a C-axis divider where that machine has a slotted table. The maker aims it at small, complex prismatic parts, from billets or on pallets.

The Willemin-Macodel 408S2 is a 5 to 6-axis machining center for complex prismatic parts that also need turned features. It moves 250 mm in X, 200 mm in Y and 310 mm in Z at up to 40 m/min, and holds the part on a C-axis divider with a Ø180 mm plate.

With 400 mm of X and 385 mm of Z, the Willemin-Macodel 508S2 is the large prismatic 5-axis machine of the range. The maker describes a 5 to 6-axis linear motor machining center for milling and turning and quotes parts up to a diameter of 200 mm. Y travel is 200 mm.
This model was not found in Willemin-Macodel's current lineup when we checked on 2026-10-03 . It may be a superseded or older model; the specifications below are as we last recorded them.

The Willemin-Macodel 808S2 packs linear motors and direct-drive rotary axes into a cabinet 980 mm wide. It is a 5-axis machining center for complex, high-precision parts up to 120 mm in diameter, with 370 mm of X, 120 mm of Y and 210 mm of Z at 60 m/min.

The Yasda H40i is a horizontal 5-axis machining center for work that ranges, in Yasda's words, from 5-faces indexing to complex simultaneous 5-axis applications. The table working size is 400 x 400 mm (15.7 x 15.7 in), and travels are 875 mm (34.4 in) in X, 740 mm (29.1 in) in Y and 685 mm (27.0 in) in Z.

Workpieces up to 800 mm in diameter are the reason the Yasda H40i-80 exists. Yasda says it reached that figure by reviewing and optimizing the machine's internal dimensions, and the specification bears this out: the travels of 875 mm (34.4 in), 740 mm (29.1 in) and 685 mm (27.0 in) and the 400 x 400 mm (15.7 x 15.7 in) table working size are unchanged from the H40i.

The Yasda H40i-100 is the large model of the H Series, a horizontal 5-axis line that Yasda describes as established for high-speed simultaneous 5-axis and high-efficiency machining. This version handles workpieces up to 1,000 mm in diameter. Unlike the H40i-80, it gets there with a bigger machine: travels are 1,075 mm (42.3 in) in X, 940 mm (37.0 in) in Y and 735 mm (28.9 in) in Z, and the table working size is 500 x 500 mm (19.7 x 19.7 in).

The Yasda PX30i is a 5-axis machine sold as a complete production cell: 323 tools and 33 pallets are standard equipment, not options. Travels are 680 mm (26.8 in) in X, 400 mm (15.7 in) in Y and 500 mm (19.7 in) in Z, and the spindle runs 100-20,000 min-1 with a MAS BT40 taper.

Description: The YCM DCV2018A-5AX is a double-column 5-axis machining center with a two-axis head. The B and C axes are in the spindle head, driven by direct drive motors, and the spindle is a built-in motorized unit that reaches 18,000 rpm on a 70 kW (94 HP) motor with an HSK A63 taper.

Middle model of YCM's high-speed bridge-type 5-axis machines, the DCV3018A-5AX has 3,200 mm of X travel over a 3,000 x 1,500 mm table rated for 10,000 kg. The spindle head carries both rotary axes, B and C, and an 18,000 rpm spindle with an HSK A63 taper.

The YCM DCV4018A-5AX is the four-metre version of YCM's high-speed bridge-type 5-axis machine. X travel is 4,200 mm, the fixed table measures 4,000 x 1,500 mm and takes 12,000 kg, and the two-axis head carries an 18,000 rpm HSK A63 spindle.

The YCM DCV4030B-5AF is a heavy double-column 5-axis machining center with a fork-type universal milling head. Linear travels are 4,065 mm in X, 3,500 mm in Y and 1,016 mm in Z; the head swivels ±110° in B and turns ±180° in C. The table is 4,100 x 2,400 mm and carries 20,000 kg.

The YCM DCV4030B-5AX is a simultaneous 5-axis bridge mill for large, heavy parts. A fork-type head with B and C axes carries an HSK A100 spindle at 10,000 rpm, the C axis turns ±360°, and the control is a HEIDENHAIN TNC640. Travels are 4,065 mm in X, 3,500 mm in Y and 1,016 mm in Z.

Five metres of X travel under a 5-axis fork head: the YCM DCV5030B-5AX extends YCM's heavy bridge-type 5-axis machine to a 5,000 x 2,400 mm table rated for 23,000 kg. Travels are 5,200 mm in X, 3,500 mm in Y and 1,016 mm in Z.

The YCM DCV6030B-5AX is the largest 5-axis machine in YCM's list. It has 6,200 mm of X travel, 3,500 mm of Y and 1,016 mm of Z, a table of 6,000 x 2,400 mm that carries 25,000 kg, and a fork-type head with B and C axes around an HSK A100 spindle.

The YCM NFX400A is a compact 5-axis vertical machining center with a tilting and rotating table. The table is ø350 mm (ø13.78 in), the A axis tilts through 150°, from +30° to -120°, and the C axis turns a full 360°. Linear travels are 650 mm (25.59 in) in X, 520 mm (20.47 in) in Y and 480 mm (18.9 in) in Z.

The YCM TCV3000A-5AX is a travelling column 5-axis machining center with a swivelling spindle head (B axis) and a rotary table (C axis) set into a long fixed table. Linear travels are 3,000 mm (118.11 in) in X and 800 mm (31.50 in) in Y and Z.

YCM describes the UV650 as a simultaneous 5-axis vertical machining center for complex parts. It carries a ø650 mm (ø25.6 in) tilt and rotary table on B and C axes, with linear travels of 620 mm (24.4 in) in X, 520 mm (20.5 in) in Y and 460 mm (18.1 in) in Z.
up to 35,000 mm/min (1,378 ipm) (high torque) / 40,000 mm/min (1,575 ipm) (high speed)

The Zayer ARION is the smallest of Zayer's bridge type machines: a fixed cross beam over a moving table, with 3,000 or 4,000 mm (118.1 or 157.5 in) of X travel, 2,600 mm (102.4 in) of Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Z. Zayer positions it for speed, and it is offered with two head families that turn it into two different machines.

The Zayer TEBAS G is a bridge type machine built around a rotary table that also travels. The table is Ø 2,200 mm (86.6 in), serves for both milling and turning, and moves 2,500 mm (98.4 in) along the longitudinal axis on a ball screw. Zayer states that the machine can mill, turn and grind.

The Zimmermann FZG is a 5-axis portal milling machine with a low rail gantry, a layout in which the portal travels low alongside the work area instead of on top of raised side walls. Zimmermann introduced the series for particularly long workpieces, and the working ranges on its page are 60,000 mm (2,362.2 in) in X, 6,000 mm (236.2 in) in Y and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) in Z.

With up to 40,000 mm (1,575 in) of X travel, 6,000 mm (236 in) of Y and 3,000 mm (118 in) of Z, the Zimmermann FZP37 is a portal milling machine for the largest molds, models and structural parts. Zimmermann lists model making, tool and mold construction, aerospace and automotive work, shipbuilding and the alternative energy industry as its fields, and calls the machine a 5/6-axis design.

The Zimmermann FZP42 is the heavy-cutting machine of the FZP line. Zimmermann says it is primarily designed for heavy-duty machining of titanium, high-strength steel and aluminum, and the figures back that up: a table rated at max. 15,000 kg/m², HSK-A100 spindles with up to 444 Nm at S1, and a VH60 head whose rotary axes clamp with 5,600 Nm on A and 6,000 Nm on C.

No foundation pit: that is the selling point of the Zimmermann FZU37. Zimmermann states that the unibody machine dispenses with a fixed machine foundation and can be set up on solid industrial floors, yet the specification is that of its large portal machines. Standard linear accuracy is ≤8μm / ≤4μm (A/R to ISO 230-2), volumetric accuracy is ≤50μm / ≤30μm, and the linear axes accelerate at up to 5 m/s².

The Zimmermann FZU42 puts a titanium-capable portal milling machine on a normal factory floor. Zimmermann says it needs no fixed machine foundation: a reinforced base plate sits on eight support elements, and the side walls are filled with special concrete to reduce vibration. The machine is meant for simultaneous 5-axis machining of aluminum, steel and titanium.

The AWEA BL-2018FM is the shortest ram-type machine in the BL horizontal boring mill series: 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of X, 1,800 mm (70.9 in) of Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of Z, with a 600 mm (23.6 in) W stroke on the ram. FM marks the built-in spindle version, which AWEA labels for mold processing. It turns 6,000 rpm on a BT50 taper and delivers 600 Nm (443 lb-ft).

Boring comes first on the AWEA BL-2018S. Its spindle is a Ø120 mm quill driven through a 2-step gear box, good for 1,308 Nm (965 lb-ft) and topping out at 2,400 rpm, and the quill feeds 600 mm (23.6 in) along W. Axis travels are 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in X, 1,800 mm (70.9 in) in Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) in Z.

Tall rather than long: the AWEA BL-2024FM pairs the shortest BL bed, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of X, with the high column that gives 2,400 mm (94.5 in) of Y. It is a ram-type horizontal boring mill with a 6,000 rpm built-in BT50 spindle.

The AWEA BL-2024S is a quill-type horizontal boring mill whose vertical travel is longer than its bed: Y measures 2,400 mm (94.5 in) and X measures 2,000 mm (78.7 in). Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in). The boring spindle is a Ø120 mm quill with 600 mm (23.6 in) of W travel.

With 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel, the AWEA BL-3018FM is the middle bed length of the ram-type BL boring mills on the lower column. Y is 1,800 mm (70.9 in), Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in), and the ram adds 600 mm (23.6 in) as the W axis.

A quill-type horizontal boring mill with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X: that is the AWEA BL-3018S. It shares its 1,800 mm (70.9 in) Y and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) Z with the shorter and longer S machines and sits between them in every size-dependent row.

The AWEA BL-3024FM covers a 3,000 x 2,400 mm (118.1 x 94.5 in) X-Y field with a ram-mounted, built-in spindle. Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in). Among the six FM machines it is the mid-length bed under the tall column.

Six of AWEA's BL boring mills use the quill head, and the AWEA BL-3024S is the one with 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X under the tall column. Y travel is 2,400 mm (94.5 in), Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in) and the quill adds 600 mm (23.6 in) on W.

The AWEA BL-4018FM stretches the ram-type BL boring mill to 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X while keeping the 1,800 mm (70.9 in) column. Nothing else in the 18 group reaches this far sideways with the 6,000 rpm built-in spindle.

Long parts that need torque more than speed are the case for the AWEA BL-4018S, a quill-type boring mill with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X. Y is 1,800 mm (70.9 in) and Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in). The head carries a Ø120 mm quill on a 2-step gear box.

At 40,500 kg (89,286 lb), the AWEA BL-4024FM is the heaviest machine in the BL series and the one with the largest envelope: 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X, 2,400 mm (94.5 in) of Y, 1,300 mm (51.2 in) of Z and 600 mm (23.6 in) of ram travel on W.

For the biggest boring jobs in the range AWEA offers the BL-4024S: full-size BL travels of 4,000 mm (157.5 in) in X and 2,400 mm (94.5 in) in Y, combined with the high-torque quill spindle. It weighs 39,500 kg (87,081 lb).

In the middle of Emco's travelling-column line sits the Ecomill, a 3+2 axis machine with a horizontal ram. Its column travels 4000 - 14000 mm along the bed, the ram extends 1,300 mm (51.2 in) and the vertical axis comes in two heights, 2000 / 2500 mm.

The Emco Ecomill Plus is a travelling-column milling machine with a horizontal ram: the column runs along a bed of 4000 - 14000 mm, the head rises 3,000 mm (118.1 in) and the ram reaches 1,600 mm (63.0 in) across. Workpieces stand on a floor plate or tables in front of it and do not move during the cut.

The Emco Ecomill S is the entry to Emco's travelling-column machines and the only one whose bed starts at 3000 mm: longitudinal travel is 3000 - 14000 mm. Cross travel is 1,300 mm (51.2 in) and vertical travel 2,000 mm (78.7 in).

The Emco Mecmill is a large travelling-column machine with a cross axis: the column moves 6000 - 16000 mm along the bed and 1,600 mm (63.0 in) across it, and the head climbs 3500 - 4000 mm. It works in 3+2 axes as standard, with heads for 5 continuous axes available.

Up to five metres of vertical travel: the Emco Mecmill Plus is the tallest machine Emco lists, with a vertical axis of 4000 - 5000 mm, a longitudinal axis of 6000 - 16000 mm and a cross axis of 1600 - 1850 mm.

Feeler lists the SHM-11020RF in the first column of its SHB table: a horizontal boring and milling machine with a 110 mm (4.3 in) boring spindle, a 1,000 x 1,200 mm (39.4 x 47.2 in) rotary table and fixed travels of 2,000 mm (78.7 in) in X and 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in Y. It is the smallest machine on that page and the only one whose travels are single figures instead of ranges.

The Feeler SHM-630L is a table-type horizontal boring and milling machine with a 630 x 630 mm (24.8 x 24.8 in) indexing table and a gear-driven spindle. It is the smallest of the three SHM models, though its travels are large for the table: 1,400 mm (55.1 in) in X, 1,150 mm (45.3 in) in Y and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) in Z.

With 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of X travel, the Feeler SHM-800 is the wide model among the SHM horizontal boring and milling machines. Y is 1,100 mm (43.3 in), Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in), and the 800 x 800 mm (31.5 x 31.5 in) table takes 3,000 kg (6,614 lb).

Height is the special feature of the Feeler SHM-800L. Its Y travel is 1,600 mm (63.0 in), the tallest in the SHM series by a wide margin, on a horizontal boring and milling machine with an 800 x 800 mm (31.5 x 31.5 in) table. X travel is 1,500 mm (59.1 in) and Z is 1,200 mm (47.2 in).

The Fermat GANTRY HEAVY puts a horizontal boring mill's spindle on a gantry. Two columns travel 10,000 - 50,000 mm (393.7 - 1,968.5 in) along the floor, the headstock crosses 6,100 mm (240.2 in) between them, and a ram comes down 1,600 mm (63.0 in) with a 160 mm (6.3 in) boring spindle inside.

The Fermat GANTRY HEAVY-DUTY sits at the top of Fermat's gantry range: a machine for extra large workpieces whose crossbeam and columns form a closed O shape. Fermat credits that shape with high rigidity and precision. Column travel in X is 10,000 - 50,000 mm (393.7 - 1,968.5 in), and the headstock crosses 5,800/6,800/7,800 mm (228.3/267.7/307.1 in) in Y.

The Fryer HB-70 is a table-type horizontal boring mill with a moving quill: 70 x 50 x 36 in (1,778 x 1,270 x 914 mm) of X, Y and Z travel plus a 4.330 in (110 mm) boring bar that feeds 20 in (508 mm) on a fully programmable W axis. It shares its 36 x 80 in (914 x 2,032 mm) table and 10,000 lb (4,536 kg) load rating with the fixed spindle HR-70 .

Fryer's HB-120 puts a moving-quill boring spindle on a 120 in (3,048 mm) bed. The work table is 40 x 126 in (1,016 x 3,200 mm) with 7 T-slots and a 10,000 lb (4,536 kg) rating; Y travel is 50 in (1,270 mm), Z is 40 in (1,016 mm), and the 4.330 in (110 mm) bar adds 20 in (508 mm) of W.

The Fryer HB-160 is the largest boring mill in the HB series and, at 48,000 lb (21,773 kg), heavier than the fixed spindle HR-160 at 46,000 lb (20,866 kg). It has 160 in (4,064 mm) of X travel on a 40 x 165 in (1,016 x 4,191 mm) table, with the same 50 in (1,270 mm) of Y, 40 in (1,016 mm) of Z and 20 in (508 mm) of bar travel as the HB-120 .

The Hartford PBM-115A is a table-type horizontal boring mill, the smaller of the two PBM sizes. X travel is 2,000 mm (78.7 in), Y is 1,600 mm (63.0 in) and Z is 1,500 mm (59.1 in), with a W axis of 500 mm (19.7 in). The rotary table measures 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in) and carries 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).

Hartford's PBM-135A is the first of three PBM-135 horizontal boring mills, and the one with the smallest table: 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in) for 8,000 kg (17,637 lb). What it gains over the PBM-115A is everything around that table.

The Hartford PBM-135B is the middle model of the PBM-135 horizontal boring mills. Its table is 1,600 x 1,800 mm (63.0 x 70.9 in) and carries 12,000 kg (26,455 lb), half as much again as the 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) of the PBM-135A , on the same column, spindle and travel options.

Fifteen tonnes on the table: the Hartford PBM-135C is the largest PBM horizontal boring mill, with a table of 1,800 x 2,000 mm (70.9 x 78.7 in) rated for 15,000 kg (33,069 lb). It is also the only PBM whose standard X travel is 3,000 mm, with 4,000 mm as the option.

The HNK HFB-130 is the entry model of HNK's floor-type CNC horizontal boring machines. The column travels along a floor bed, 4,000 ~ 30,000 mm (157.5 ~ 1,181.1 in) in X, and carries a Ø130 mm (5.1 in) boring spindle on a ram.

The HNK HFB-150 is a floor-type horizontal boring machine with a Ø150 mm (5.9 in) spindle, and it shares most of its frame figures with the HFB-160 above it. Both have 2,500 ~ 4,000 mm (98.4 ~ 157.5 in) of vertical travel and 800 mm (31.5 in) of ram travel, with 1,200 mm (47.2 in) in braces. The HFB-150 is the lighter-table, shorter-quill version of that pair.

50,000 kg (110,229 lb) on a 3,000 x 4,000 mm (118.1 x 157.5 in) rotary table is what the HNK HFB-160 offers over the HFB-150 , together with a Ø160 mm (6.3 in) spindle. The column and ram figures are otherwise shared: 2,500 ~ 4,000 mm (98.4 ~ 157.5 in) in Y and 800 mm (31.5 in) of ram travel.

The HNK HFB-180 is the mid-point of the HFB floor-type boring machines and the largest that keeps a plain ISO 50 spindle taper. Its spindle is Ø180 mm (7.1 in), its vertical travel 3,000 ~ 6,000 mm (118.1 ~ 236.2 in), and its rotary table 4,000 x 5,000 mm (157.5 x 196.9 in) for 80,000 kg (176,367 lb).

ISO 60 arrives with the HNK HFB-200. The taper row for this floor-type boring machine reads ISO 60 [50 Adaptor], on a Ø200 mm (7.9 in) spindle that runs from 5 to 1,500 rpm. Smaller HFB models are ISO 50 only.
The HNK HFB-250 carries the largest boring spindle HNK lists: Ø250 mm (9.8 in), on a floor-type machine whose rotary table measures 5,000 x 9,000 mm (196.9 x 354.3 in). It tops the HFB series.

The HNK HIB-12 is the smallest of the HIB high-speed horizontal boring and milling machines, a series HNK says is designed for high speed boring and milling in the die and mold industry. The spindle range is 50 to 12,000 rpm, several times the ceiling of HNK's conventional HB boring mills, and travels are 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in X, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Y and 1,200 mm (47.2 in) in Z.

The HNK HIB-16 widens the HIB high-speed boring mill without making it taller. X travel is 2,000 mm (78.7 in) and the rotary table 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in), while Y stays at the 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of the HIB-12 . Z is 1,300 mm (51.2 in).

Table load nearly doubles at the HNK HIB-18. This high-speed horizontal boring and milling machine carries 12,000 kg (26,455 lb) on a 1,600 x 1,800 mm (63.0 x 70.9 in) rotary table, against 6,500 kg (14,330 lb) on the HIB-16 , and both X and Y grow: 3,000 mm (118.1 in) and 2,000 mm (78.7 in).

The HNK HIB-22 is the largest HIB high-speed boring and milling machine, and the only one with 1,600 mm (63.0 in) of Z travel. Its rotary table is 2,000 x 2,200 mm (78.7 x 86.6 in) and carries 15,000 kg (33,069 lb).

The HNK HKDB-130(1.2Mx7M) is the wide-table version of the seven-metre duplex boring machine. Its table is 1,200 x 7,000 mm (47.2 x 275.6 in), and the two spindle ends open from 300 to 1,500 mm (11.8 to 59.1 in), where the HKDB-130(1Mx7M ) stops at 1,300 mm (51.2 in).

Nine metres of X travel puts the HNK HKDB-130(1.2Mx9M) in the middle of the HKDB duplex boring machines. The moving table is 1,200 x 9,000 mm (47.2 x 354.3 in) and passes between two opposed Ø130 spindle heads.

The HNK HKDB-130(1.2Mx13M) has the longest table of the table-moving duplex boring machines: 1,200 x 13,000 mm (47.2 x 511.8 in), with 13,000 mm (511.8 in) of X travel between two opposed spindle heads.

The HNK HKDB-130(1Mx5M) is the smallest duplex boring machine in the HKDB series: two opposed Ø130 spindle heads, one on each side of a moving table that measures 1,000 x 5,000 mm (39.4 x 196.9 in). HNK designs the series to machine both sides of a workpiece at the same time, which it says cuts cycle time and gives precise symmetrical machining.

Seven metres of table on the narrow frame: the HNK HKDB-130(1Mx7M) is a table-moving duplex boring machine with a 1,000 x 7,000 mm (39.4 x 275.6 in) table and two Ø130 spindle heads working from opposite sides.

The HNK HKDB-130F(1.1Mx7M) is the mid-width, mid-length member of the column-moving duplex boring series. Its fixed table is 1,100 x 7,000 mm (43.3 x 275.6 in) and its two columns travel 7,000 mm (275.6 in).

The HNK HKDB-130F(1.1Mx16M) combines the 16,000 mm (629.9 in) column travel of HNK's longest duplex boring machines with the 1.1M cross-section: a fixed table of 1,100 x 16,000 mm (43.3 x 629.9 in), 600 mm (23.6 in) of Z travel per head and a spindle gap of 200 to 1,400 mm (7.9 to 55.1 in).

In the HNK HKDB-130F(1Mx5M) the table stands still and the two spindle columns move. HNK calls the HKDB-F series a column-moving CNC boring machine with two spindle heads, and states that the two columns can travel along the fixed table simultaneously or independently. This is the shortest version, with a 1,000 x 5,000 mm (39.4 x 196.9 in) table and 5,000 mm (196.9 in) of X travel.
The HNK HKDB-130F(1Mx16M) stretches the column-moving duplex boring machine to a 1,000 x 16,000 mm (39.4 x 629.9 in) fixed table, with 16,000 mm (629.9 in) of X travel for its two spindle columns.

The HNK HKDB-150(1.2Mx8M) is the heavy-spindle duplex boring machine. Each of its two heads carries a Ø150 spindle with a 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp) motor, cont/30min, against the Ø130 spindles and 22/26 kW (29.5/34.9 hp) of the HKDB-130(1.2Mx7M ).

The HNK HKDB-150(1.2Mx9M) is the largest table-moving duplex boring machine with the Ø150 spindles: a 1,200 x 9,000 mm (47.2 x 354.3 in) table, 9,000 mm (354.3 in) of X travel and a 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp) motor on each of its two heads.

The HNK HKDB-150F(1.3Mx8M) puts the heavy spindle on the fixed-table duplex machine. Two travelling columns each carry a Ø150 mm (5.9 in) spindle driven by a 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp) motor, cont/30min, over a table of 1,300 x 8,000 mm (51.2 x 315.0 in).

The HNK HKDB-150F(1.3Mx16M) is the largest duplex boring machine HNK lists. Two columns with Ø150 mm (5.9 in) spindles travel 16,000 mm (629.9 in) along a fixed table of 1,300 x 16,000 mm (51.2 x 629.9 in).

The Johnford BMC-110 is a table-type horizontal boring machining center with a Ø110 mm (Ø4.3 in) boring spindle. Middle of three table-type boring machining centers, the Johnford BMC-130 pairs a Ø130 mm (Ø5.1 in) spindle with a 30 / 37 kW (40.2 / 49.6 hp) motor. Its travels are 3,000 mm (118 in) in X, 2,300 mm (90.5 in) in Y, 1,600 mm (63 in) in Z and 700 mm (27.5 in) in W.

The Johnford BMC-160 is the largest table-type boring machining center in the BMC series: a Ø160 mm (Ø6.29 in) spindle, a 2,000 x 2,500 mm (78.7 x 98.4 in) rotary table that takes 25,000 kg (55,000 lb), and travels of 4,000 mm (157.4 in) in X and 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in Y.

The Johnford FBMC-X12 is a floor-type horizontal boring machining center. On this kind of machine the column travels along a bed, 12,000 mm in X here, and the workpiece stands still on a floor plate or on a separate rotary table in front of it. The FBMC-X12 is the shortest of four lengths.
With 13,000 mm (511.8 in) of column travel and an 8,000 mm (315 in) floor plate, the Johnford FBMC-X13 is the second length of the floor-type FBMC boring machining centers.

Sixty kilowatts continuous at the spindle: the Johnford FBMC-X14 is a floor-type boring machining center with a 60 / 75 kW (80.5 / 100.6 hp) drive, rated S1 / S6-60%, and 14,000 mm (551.2 in) of X travel.

The Johnford FBMC-X15 is the longest floor-type boring machining center in the maker's table, with 15,000 mm (590.6 in) of X travel and a 10,000 x 2,500 mm (393.7 x 98.4 in) floor plate. It weighs 159,000 kg (349,800 lb).

The Juaristi ML is a floor type universal milling machine with a travelling column, the compact member of Juaristi's floor type range: vertical travel from 1,500 mm to 3,000 mm in 500 mm steps, a RAM stroke of 1,300 mm (51.2 in) and a single 40 kW (53.6 hp) head rating.

The Juaristi MP5-RAM is the entry size of the MP-RAM floor type boring centers, the hydrostatically guided line. A 130-160 mm boring bar with 800 mm (31.5 in) of W travel sits in a 460 x 520 mm RAM whose Z stroke is 1,000-1,200 mm.

Juaristi's MP6-RAM puts 64/96 kW and 3,780-9,650 Nm (2,788-7,118 lb-ft) of spindle torque into the second-smallest frame of the hydrostatic MP-RAM floor type boring centers. The boring bar is 160-180 mm in diameter, W travel is 800-1,000 mm and the RAM stroke 1,200-1,500 mm.

The Juaristi MP9-RAM is where the hydrostatic MP-RAM floor type boring centers step up to a 520 x 580 mm (20.5 x 22.8 in) RAM. It carries boring bars of 180-205-225 mm, feeds them 1,200-1,400 mm on W, and delivers 5,000-10,300 Nm (3,688-7,597 lb-ft) of spindle torque from 71/100 kW.

At the top of Juaristi's hydrostatic floor type boring centers, the MP10-RAM lists 19,000-23,000 Nm (14,014-16,965 lb-ft) of spindle torque, 100/125 kW of spindle power and a RAM of 580 x 650 mm (22.8 x 25.6 in). Vertical travel starts at 4,000 mm and extends in 500 mm steps to 10,000 mm.

The Juaristi MX5 is the entry size of the MX floor type milling machines: a travelling column with a central head, a 460 x 520 mm (18.1 x 20.5 in) RAM with 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of Z stroke, and vertical travel that starts at 2,000 mm and grows in 500 mm steps to 4,000 mm.

The Juaristi MX5-RAM is a travelling column boring-milling center, the smallest of the three MX-RAM sizes. It combines a 460 x 520 mm RAM on a Z stroke of 1,200 mm (47.2 in) with a boring bar of 130-160 mm that feeds a further 800 mm (31.5 in) on W.

Juaristi's MX7 is the middle size of the MX floor type milling machines. Its vertical travel begins at 3,000 mm and is extended in 500 mm steps to 6,000 mm, and the RAM has a Z stroke of 1,650 – 1,800 mm (65.0 – 70.9 in). X is a base 4,000 mm plus N x 2,000 mm of added bed.

Spindle torque of up to 4,050 Nm (2,987 lb-ft) is the figure that separates the Juaristi MX7-RAM from the size below it. This travelling column boring-milling center carries a 160-180 mm boring bar with 800 mm (31.5 in) of W travel, on a RAM whose Z stroke is 1,200-1,500 mm.

With a 520 x 580 mm (20.5 x 22.8 in) RAM and 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of Z stroke, the Juaristi MX9 is the largest of the MX floor type milling machines. Vertical travel is listed from 2,000 mm in 500 mm steps up to 7,000 mm, and X as 4,000 mm plus N x 2,000 mm.

The PAMA Speedmill B is the dynamic floor-type boring mill in the range: a Speedmill milling machine fitted with a boring bar, which is what the B stands for. Its X and Y axes run on roller guideways, not the hydrostatic guides of the Speedram models, and rapid feed is up to 35,000 mm/min.

The Vision Wide VBE-110-1250 is a horizontal boring and milling machine with a 1,250 x 1,250 mm (49.2 x 49.2 in) table, a fixed column and a W axis of 550 mm (21.7 in). Travels are 1,600 mm (63.0 in) in X and 1,300 mm (51.2 in) in both Y and Z.

On the Vision Wide VBE-110-1416 the table grows to 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in) and the load rating to 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) in the central area, making it the larger of the two VBE horizontal boring and milling machines.

The Vision Wide VBH-110-1250 is a horizontal boring and milling machine with a 1,250 x 1,250 mm (49.2 x 49.2 in) table and a W-axis boring spindle travel of 550 mm (21.7 in). It is the smallest of the VBH series, which the maker describes as a high stability, high precision box in box structure.

Table load comes in two ratings on the Vision Wide VBH-110-1416: 6,000 kg as standard and 10,000 kg as an option, printed as 6,000 / 10,000 kg (13,228 / 22,046 lb) (Opt.) and measured in the central area. The table is 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in).

The Vision Wide VBH-110-1618 carries the heaviest loads of the 110 class: 15,000 kg as standard and 20,000 kg as an option, on a 1,600 x 1,800 mm (63.0 x 70.9 in) table. The row reads 15,000 / 20,000 kg (33,069 / 44,092 lb) (Opt.), central area.

The 130 class starts with the Vision Wide VBH-130-1416, and the step from the 110 class is in every spindle row. Speed is 3,000 rpm, power 22 / 30 kW (29.5 / 40.2 hp), torque 1,444 / 1,970 Nm (1,065 / 1,453 lb-ft), and the W-axis travel 700 mm (27.6 in).

With 1,970 Nm available in short-time duty, the Vision Wide VBH-130-1618 is a boring mill for heavy stock removal on parts up to 20,000 kg (44,092 lb). The continuous torque figure is 1,444 Nm, and the full row reads 1,444 / 1,970 Nm (1,065 / 1,453 lb-ft).

The Vision Wide VBH-130-1822 moves the series up a frame size. X travel is 3,000 mm, with 3,500 mm as an option, and Y travel 2,500 mm, with 3,000 mm as an option; the smaller VBH-130-1618 lists 2,000 mm and 2,500 mm for both.

Energy, shipbuilding and engine work are the markets Vision Wide names for its large boring mills, and the Vision Wide VBH-130-2025 is sized for them. Its table is 2,000 x 2,500 mm (78.7 x 98.4 in), with a load of 20,000 kg as standard and 30,000 kg as an option.

A square 2,500 x 2,500 mm (98.4 x 98.4 in) table rated for 35,000 kg, or 40,000 kg as an option, makes the Vision Wide VBH-130-2525 the first of the very heavy VBH models. The load row reads 35,000 / 40,000 kg (77,160 / 88,183 lb) (Opt.), central area.
The largest VBH is the Vision Wide VBH-130-2530. Its table is 2,500 x 3,000 mm (98.4 x 118.1 in), the load is 40,000 kg as standard and 45,000 kg as an option, and X travel is 4,500 mm, or 5,000 mm.

On the Vision Wide VBT-110-1250 the boring spindle can be fed past the centre of the table. The maker's row for the distance from spindle nose to table center reads -125~425~1,925 mm (-4.9~16.7~75.8 in), and the negative first value is the nose position with the W axis fully out and the table at its nearest.
The spindle of the Vision Wide VBT-110-1416 comes down to the table. The row for spindle center to table surface begins at 0: it reads 0~1,600 mm, or 0~2,000 mm with the optional Y travel.

Two VBT models share the 1,600 x 1,800 mm (63.0 x 70.9 in) table, and the Vision Wide VBT-110-1618 is the lighter-spindled, faster one. It lists 3,500 rpm, 18.5 / 22 kW (24.8 / 29.5 hp) and 972 / 1,155 Nm (717 / 852 lb-ft), with a W axis of 550 mm (21.7 in).

The Vision Wide VBT-130-1416 puts the larger VBT spindle over the second-smallest table in the series. The table is 1,400 x 1,600 mm (55.1 x 63.0 in); the spindle is rated 22 / 30 kW (29.5 / 40.2 hp) and 1,444 / 1,970 Nm (1,065 / 1,453 lb-ft) at up to 3,000 rpm.
Depth is the dimension the Vision Wide VBT-130-1618 extends. Z travel is 1,500 mm with 2,000 mm as an option, and the W-axis spindle adds 700 mm (27.6 in) of its own.
The Vision Wide VBT-130-1822 has a 1,800 x 2,200 mm (70.9 x 86.6 in) table rated for 20,000 kg (44,092 lb) and X travel of 3,000 mm, with 3,500 mm as an option. It is the first VBT on the longer bed.

The headstock of the Vision Wide VBT-130-2025 climbs a tall column: Y travel is 2,500 mm, with 3,000 mm as an option. The way that axis is guided is the one design point the maker singles out for the VBT, calling it a high stability and high precision Y-axis box way structure design.
Thirty-five tonnes as standard and forty as an option: the Vision Wide VBT-130-2525 lists a table load of 35,000 / 40,000 kg (77,160 / 88,183 lb) (Opt.) on a 2,500 x 2,500 mm (98.4 x 98.4 in) table.

At the top of the VBT series, the Vision Wide VBT-130-2530 takes 40,000 kg on its table as standard and 45,000 kg as an option. The table is 2,500 x 3,000 mm (98.4 x 118.1 in), and X travel is 4,500 mm, or 5,000 mm.

The Zayer ZERO is a bed type milling machine with a horizontal ram, a fixed bed and a moving table, built around accuracy more than size. X travel is 3,000 or 4,000 mm (118.1 or 157.5 in), Y is 1,200 mm (47.2 in) and Z is 1,600 mm (63.0 in), and none of the three carries an optional extension in Zayer's table.

The Zayer ZERO G puts a rotary table on the ZERO bed type platform. Zayer lists it together with the ZERO G-MT on one page with a single specification table: a 1,500 x 1,250 mm (59.1 x 49.2 in) rotary table, 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of X travel, 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of Y and 1,600 mm (63.0 in) of Z.

The Bourn & Koch 100H is a 6 axis horizontal CNC gear hobber for shafts and small gears: 127 mm (5.0 in) maximum workpiece diameter, a pitch range of 2.54 Module and 500 mm (19.7 in) of axial travel. It is the second size in the H-Series, above the 25H and below the 400H .

The Bourn & Koch 25H is the smallest of the four H-Series horizontal CNC gear hobbers, a compact machine for fine-pitch work. It takes workpieces up to 25 mm (1.0 in) in diameter, has a pitch range of 1 Module and offers 178 mm (7.0 in) of axial travel. That places it with small pinions, splined shafts and miniature gearing, not with general power-transmission gears.

The Bourn & Koch 400H is a 7 axis horizontal CNC gear hobber for gears and splined shafts up to 400 mm (15.7 in) in diameter and 6.4 Module. Maximum axial travel is 1,250 mm (49.2 in). It is the one H-Series model listed with seven CNC axes; the 100H below it and the 600H above it are both 6 axis machines.

The Bourn & Koch 600H is the largest H-Series horizontal CNC gear hobber, built around long and heavy shafts: 600 mm (23.6 in) maximum workpiece diameter, a 12 module pitch range and 2,400 mm (94.5 in) of maximum axial travel. At approximately 38,000 lb (17,237 kg) it weighs more than twice as much as the 400H .
