The Dener E-FTL 6012 is the smallest tube fiber laser cutting machine in Dener's range: a two-chuck machine for tube up to 120 mm (4.7 in) across the chuck and 7,000 mm long. It takes laser sources from 1.5 to 6 kW.

With a 180 mm (7.1 in) chuck, the Dener E-FTL 6018 covers the tube sizes most general fabricators handle, on the light two-chuck frame of Dener's E-FTL series. Maximum cutting length is 7,000 mm and laser power is 1.5-6 kW.

The Dener E-FTL 6025 moves the E-FTL tube laser series to a 250 mm (9.8 in) chuck and a higher power class. Laser power is 3-12 kW, double the ceiling of the two smaller models, and a BOCI BLT442T head is listed for 12 kW.
A 350 mm (13.8 in) chuck makes the Dener E-FTL 6035 the largest-capacity machine among the 7,000 mm E-FTL tube lasers. It accepts laser sources from 3 to 12 kW and bars up to 600 kg (1,323 lb).

The Dener E-FTL 9025 is a long-bed tube fiber laser: 9,300 mm (366.1 in) of maximum cutting length with a 250 mm chuck. It extends the E-FTL 6025 for stock that arrives in lengths beyond seven metres.

Top of the two-chuck series, the Dener E-FTL 9035 combines the 350 mm (13.8 in) chuck with a 9,300 mm cutting length. Its maximum cutting weight is 1,200 kg (2,646 lb), by a wide margin the highest of any E-FTL.
The Dener FTL 6018 opens Dener's three-chuck tube fiber laser series. It holds tube in a 180 mm (7.1 in) chuck, cuts lengths up to 6,200 mm and is offered with laser power from 3 to 20 kW.

The Dener FTL 6025 is a three-chuck tube fiber laser with a 250 mm (9.8 in) chuck and a 6,200 mm cutting length. In Dener's FTL table it sits between the FTL 6018 and the FTL 6035 on the same 16,100 mm frame.

Largest chuck of the six-metre group, the Dener FTL 6035 is a three-chuck tube fiber laser for sections up to 350 mm (13.8 in). Cutting length is 6,200 mm and the maximum cutting weight 600 kg (1,323 lb).
The Dener FTL 9025 is a nine-metre, three-chuck tube fiber laser. Maximum cutting length is 9,300 mm (366.1 in) with a 250 mm chuck, and both loading and unloading lengths are 9 m.

A 350 mm (13.8 in) chuck on the nine-metre frame gives the Dener FTL 9035 the widest section range of Dener's mid-length tube lasers. Maximum cutting length is 9,300 mm and maximum cutting weight 1,200 kg (2,646 lb).

Twelve metres is the standard mill length for much structural tube, and the Dener FTL 12025 is the smallest Dener tube fiber laser that takes it whole. Maximum cutting length is 12,300 mm (484.3 in), the chuck is 250 mm and the loading and unloading lengths are 12 m each.
The Dener FTL 12035 is a twelve-metre tube fiber laser with a 350 mm (13.8 in) chuck, and the first model in the range whose power band starts higher: laser power is listed as 6-20 kW.

The Dener FTL 12064 is the largest tube fiber laser Dener lists. Its chuck is 640 mm (25.2 in), nearly twice the next size down, and a single bar may weigh 2,600 kg (5,732 lb) at a cutting length of up to 12,300 mm.

The Dener Pro DC 3015 is the smallest table size of Dener's Pro DC fiber laser cutting machines, a gantry-type flatbed laser with an automatic pallet changer. Dener offers the Pro DC series with laser power from 3 kW to 20 kW and builds it in 3015, 4020, 6020 and 8025 table sizes.

Between the compact and the long tables of Dener's fiber laser range sits the Dener Pro DC 4020. It is a flatbed fiber laser cutting machine on the 4020 table size, with two exchange pallets and a choice of resonators from 3 kW to 20 kW.

The Dener Pro DC 6020 is the longest Pro DC fiber laser for which Dener publishes a specification table. It belongs to the 6020 table size and is aimed at long sheets and at nests that fill a large pallet.

The DMG MORI LASERTEC 100 PowerDrill is a 5-axis laser drilling machine for large turbine components: DMG MORI states a component diameter of up to 1,100 mm and a maximum height of 1,500 mm. Y and Z travel are each 1,000 mm (39.4 in). The work it is built for is cooling air holes in aerospace and IGT (industrial gas turbine) parts.

The Durma HD-F 3015 VI is a flat-bed fiber laser cutting machine for 3,048 x 1,524 mm (120.0 x 60.0 in) sheet, and the fastest of Durma's rack-and-pinion lasers. Its axes travel 3,100 mm (122.0 in) in X, 1,525 mm (60.0 in) in Y and 160 mm (6.3 in) in Z. Each of X and Y reaches 120 m/min, and with both moving together the head runs at 170 m/min with 28 m/s² of synchronized acceleration.

Unlike Durma's flat-bed lasers, the HD-FA is a 5 axis fiber laser for cutting formed, three-dimensional parts. The head moves 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Y and 650 mm (25.6 in) in Z, and tilts and turns on two rotary axes: B through ±135° and C through ±360° x n, meaning continuous rotation.

Durma positions the HD-FN 3015 as the plainer of its flat-bed fiber lasers: a 3,048 x 1,524 mm (120.0 x 60.0 in) machine with laser power up to 20 kW and moderate axis dynamics. X travel is 3,100 mm (122.0 in) and Y travel 1,525 mm (60.0 in). The Z axis is printed as 125 (270) mm, without an explanation of the bracketed figure.

The Durma HD-FO is a compact fiber laser cutting machine built for shops that are short of floor space. It cuts 3,048 x 1,524 mm (120.0 x 60.0 in) sheet, but it is laid out differently from Durma's other flat-bed lasers: the laser source and the chiller sit inside the machine, and the standard machine has a manual cutting table instead of a shuttle table.

Small tube at high rotation speed is the purpose of the Durma HD-TC 60170, the lightest of the bundle-loading HD-TC tube lasers. Its largest round is Ø170 mm (6.7 in), its largest square 120 x 120 mm (4.7 x 4.7 in) and its largest rectangle 150 x 100 mm (5.9 x 3.9 in). Material up to 6,500 mm (255.9 in) long is taken from a bundle of up to 3,000 kg (6,614 lb).

The Durma HD-TC 60220 is the centre of the HD-TC tube and profile laser range: Ø220 mm (8.7 in) round tube, 160 x 160 mm (6.3 x 6.3 in) square and 200 x 100 mm (7.9 x 3.9 in) rectangular profile, cut from lengths up to 6,500 mm (255.9 in). It is the machine Durma uses to present the series in its brochure.

The Durma HD-TC 60250 COMPACT is the short-footprint member of the HD-TC tube and profile laser family. It cuts round tube from Ø16 mm (0.6 in) to Ø250 mm (9.8 in), square profile up to 160 x 160 mm (6.3 x 6.3 in) and rectangular profile up to 200 x 150 mm (7.9 x 5.9 in), in lengths up to 6,000 mm (236.2 in).

The Durma HD-TC 60350 MEGA opens the heavy end of the HD-TC tube laser range. Its chucks take round tube up to Ø350 mm (13.8 in) and square or rectangular profile up to 350 x 350 mm (13.8 x 13.8 in), in material up to 6,500 mm (255.9 in) long. Compared with the HD-TC 60220 , section weight more than doubles: 125 kg/m and 800 kg (1,764 lb) per workpiece.

Stock longer than the usual six metres is the reason for the Durma HD-TC 80220. This tube and profile laser accepts material up to 8,500 mm (334.6 in) long, with the section capacity of the HD-TC 60220 : Ø220 mm (8.7 in) round, 160 x 160 mm (6.3 x 6.3 in) square and 200 x 100 mm (7.9 x 3.9 in) rectangular.

Twelve-metre structural sections go through the Durma HD-TC 120350 MEGA in one piece. This tube and profile laser takes material up to 12,500 mm (492.1 in) long and unloads finished parts up to 12,000 mm (472.4 in), in round tube to Ø350 mm (13.8 in) and square or rectangular profile to 350 x 350 mm (13.8 x 13.8 in).

The Durma HD-TC 120500 MEGA is the largest tube and profile laser Durma lists. It holds round tube up to Ø500 mm (19.7 in), square profile up to 380 x 380 mm (15.0 x 15.0 in) and rectangular profile up to 400 x 350 mm (15.7 x 13.8 in), in lengths up to 12,500 mm (492.1 in). A single workpiece may weigh 2,100 kg (4,630 lb).

The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 2.5x1.25 is the entry size of Ermak's end-loading flatbed fiber laser range. It takes sheets of 2,500 x 1,250 mm (98.4 x 49.2 in) on two shuttle pallets, each rated for 1,000 kg (2,205 lb).

Three metres by one and a half is the sheet most European stockholders carry, and the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 3x1.5 is built around it: a 3,000 x 1,500 mm (118.1 x 59.1 in) working area with 3,050 mm of X travel and 1,550 mm of Y travel.

With a 4,000 x 2,000 mm (157.5 x 78.7 in) working area, the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 4x2 is the first size in the range that takes two-metre-wide sheet. Y travel is 2,050 mm and X travel 4,050 mm.
The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 6x2 stretches the two-metre table to a 6,150 x 2,000 mm (242.1 x 78.7 in) working area. It is the longest model that Ermak still lists at 2.5 G.
The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 6x2.6 opens the wide-format half of the range. Its working area is 6,150 x 2,600 mm (242.1 x 102.4 in), and the bridge travels 2,700 mm in Y.

At 8,000 x 2,000 mm (315.0 x 78.7 in), the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 8x2 is where Ermak's table steps the acceleration down. This size is listed at 1.5 G; the four shorter two-metre models are all at 2.5 G.
Eight metres long and 2,600 mm wide: the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 8x2.6 has a working area of 8,000 x 2,600 mm (315.0 x 102.4 in) and pallets rated for 6,500 kg (14,330 lb).
The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 9x2 is the longest of the two-metre-wide models, with a working area of 9,000 x 2,000 mm (354.3 x 78.7 in) and 9,200 mm of X travel.

The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 9x2.6 cuts 9,000 x 2,600 mm (354.3 x 102.4 in) and marks a boundary in Ermak's table. It is the largest size listed at 113 m/min resultant, and the last for which a linear motor speed is printed at all.
From ten metres up, Ermak's large-format lasers form a separate group, and the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 10x2.6 is its first member. The working area is 10,000 x 2,600 mm (393.7 x 102.4 in).
Twelve-metre plate is a standard mill length, and the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 12x2.6 takes it whole: the working area is 12,000 x 2,600 mm (472.4 x 102.4 in), with 12,200 mm of travel in X.

The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 14x2.6 has a 14,000 x 2,600 mm (551.2 x 102.4 in) working area, which puts it past the usual twelve-metre plate and into the territory of special-length material and multi-sheet loading.
Sixteen metres of table make the Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 16x2.6 the longest 2,600 mm wide model Ermak lists. Its working area is 16,000 x 2,600 mm (629.9 x 102.4 in).

The Ermak Fibermak Momentum Gen-5 SM 18x3 is the largest flatbed laser in Ermak's table and the only one with a three-metre-wide bed: 18,000 x 3,000 mm (708.7 x 118.1 in) of working area under a bridge with 3,200 mm of Y travel.

The Ermak Fibermak SL 2.5x1.25 is the smallest of Ermak's side loading fiber lasers. Its cutting area is 2,500 x 1,250 mm (98.4 x 49.2 in), and the pallets leave the machine from the side instead of the end, which is what the SL in the name stands for.
A standard three-metre sheet, loaded from the side: the Ermak Fibermak SL 3x1.5 is the reference size of Ermak's side loading fiber laser line. The cutting area is 3,000 x 1,500 mm (118.1 x 59.1 in).

The Ermak Fibermak SL 4x2 is the largest side loading fiber laser that Ermak builds with two exchange pallets. It cuts sheets of 4,000 x 2,000 mm (157.5 x 78.7 in), and each pallet carries 2,500 kg (5,511 lb), the highest two-pallet load in the SL table.

With the Ermak Fibermak SL 6x2 the side loading laser moves to long sheet. The cutting area is 6,150 x 2,000 mm (242.1 x 78.7 in), and the loading arrangement changes with it: the table lists an automatic single pallet, not the two exchange pallets of the shorter models.

Eight metres of cutting length puts the Ermak Fibermak SL 8x2 among the large-format machines of Ermak's laser range. The cutting area is 8,100 x 2,000 mm (318.9 x 78.7 in), served by an automatic single pallet that loads from the side.

The Ermak Fibermak SL 8x2.6 is the widest machine in Ermak's side loading laser table, with a cutting area of 8,100 x 2,700 mm (318.9 x 106.3 in). It exists for plate that is wider than the usual two metres.

The Ermak Fibertube is a tube and profile laser with automatic loading and unloading. According to its specification table it cuts round tube from Ø20 to Ø120 mm, square profile from 20x20 to 120x120 mm and rectangular profile from 20x20 to 80x120 mm, with an IPG YLS 2000 resonator.

The Ermak Thunderbird 3x1.5 is a flatbed fiber laser cutting machine with a 3,000 x 1,500 mm (118.1 x 59.1 in) cutting area and a double shuttle table. Ermak positions it as the simpler, lower-cost line beside its Fibermak machines, and the table shows how the simplification was done.

Ermak's lowest-cost flatbed fiber laser is the Ermak Thunderbird Competition 3x1.5. It keeps the 3,000 x 1,500 mm (118.1 x 59.1 in) cutting area and two-pallet layout of the Thunderbird 3x1.5 and changes the components around them.

The Flow LZR 3015 is a fiber laser cutting machine with a 120 x 60 in (3,048 x 1,524 mm) cutting area and a choice of 6 kW, 12 kW or 20 kW of laser power. It is the smaller of the two LZR sizes. The LZR 4020 offers the same three power levels over 158 x 79 in (4,013 x 2,007 mm).

With a 158 x 79 in (4,013 x 2,007 mm) cutting area, the Flow LZR 4020 is the larger of Flow's two LZR fiber laser cutting machines. The LZR 3015 covers 120 x 60 in (3,048 x 1,524 mm), so this model is about 32% longer and wider at the bed. Laser power is a choice of 6 kW, 12 kW or 20 kW.

The Haco HFL 1510 C is the smallest fiber laser in the HFL range: a single-table machine with 1,500 mm (59.1 in) of X travel and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) of Y, offered with a 3 kW or 6 kW source. It is a half-sheet machine. Longer sheets have to be cut down first or go to the HFL 3015 C , which has 3,000 mm (118.1 in) of X travel on the same design.

A full-size sheet on a single table is the idea behind the Haco HFL 3015 C. X travel is 3,000 mm (118.1 in), Y travel 1,500 mm (59.1 in), and the source is 3 kW or 6 kW. It is the larger of the two C models and the smallest Haco laser that takes a standard sheet whole.

For standard-format sheet with table exchange, the Haco HFL 3015 CE is the base model of the CE line. It is fully enclosed, has dual interchangeable tables, and comes with a 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW source. X travel is 3,050 mm (120.1 in) and Y travel 1,550 mm (61.0 in).

Sheet and tube on one machine: the Haco HFL 3015 CEG is a combi laser that adds two chucks to the right side of an enclosed flatbed. Sheet travels are 3,030 mm (119.3 in) by 1,520 mm (59.8 in). Tubes can weigh up to 200 kg (441 lb) and measure up to 200 mm (7.9 in) across, and the source is 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW.

The Haco HFL 3015 CEW is an enclosed fiber laser with two interchangeable tables. Its axes travel 3,010 mm (118.5 in) in X and 1,505 mm (59.3 in) in Y, and it is sold with a 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW source.
The Haco HFL 4020 CE is the mid-size flatbed of the CE line. X travel is 4,050 mm (159.4 in) and Y travel 2,050 mm (80.7 in), on the enclosed CE design with a 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW source.

The Haco HFL 4020 CEG is the mid-size combi laser of the range, with a large-format flatbed and a two-chuck tube station at its side. Sheet travels are 4,030 mm (158.7 in) in X and 2,020 mm (79.5 in) in Y. The table is rated for 2.50 tons.

Six metres of X travel put the Haco HFL 6020 CE in the long-bed class. The figures are 6,050 mm (238.2 in) in X and 2,050 mm (80.7 in) in Y, with a table rated for 3.70 tons and a 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW source.

At the top of the combi line, the Haco HFL 6020 CEG pairs a long flatbed with a tube station. Sheet travels are 6,030 mm (237.4 in) by 2,020 mm (79.5 in) and the table takes 3.70 tons. Like its smaller siblings it handles tubes up to 200 kg (441 lb) and 200 mm (7.9 in).

The Haco HFL 6025 CE is the largest flatbed in the HFL brochure. It combines 6,050 mm (238.2 in) of X travel with 2,550 mm (100.4 in) of Y, the widest Y travel in the range, and its table is rated for 4.70 tons.

The Han's Laser G3015HF is the smallest machine in the HF Expert series of high-speed fiber laser cutting machines. It cuts sheet on a 3,000 × 1,500 mm (118.1 × 59.1 in) processing area and is the quickest of the four sizes on paper: 200 m/min maximum positioning speed in X and Y with 2.8 G of acceleration.

The Han's Laser G4020HF is the 4,000 × 2,000 mm (157.5 × 78.7 in) member of the HF Expert series, a high-speed fiber laser cutting machine for sheet metal. It keeps the top dynamics of the series, 200 m/min and 2.8 G in X and Y, while moving up from the 3,000 × 1,500 mm format of the G3015HF to the larger standard sheet.

The Han's Laser G6020HF is where the HF Expert series turns from a sheet cutter into a plate cutter. Its processing area is 6,000 × 2,000 mm (236.2 × 78.7 in), but the more telling figures are the table load of 5,600 kg (12,346 lb) and the Z-axis travel of 300 mm (11.8 in).

The Han's Laser G12025HF is the largest machine in the HF Expert table, a fiber laser cutting machine with a 12,000 × 2,500 mm (472.4 × 98.4 in) processing area. It is built for plate that does not fit a standard bed: long structural parts, wide sheets, or several ordinary sheets laid end to end and cut in one program.

The Han's Laser MPS-3015D is the 3,000 × 1,500 mm (118.1 × 59.1 in) model of the MPS-D series of gantry laser cutting machines for sheet metal. It is the entry size of the series and also its quickest, with a maximum positioning speed of 120 m/min and 1.2 g of acceleration. The MPS-4020D is listed at 100 m/min and 1.0 g, and so are the sizes above it.

The Han's Laser MPS-4020D is a gantry laser cutting machine with a 4,000 × 2,000 mm (157.5 × 78.7 in) processing area, the second size in the MPS-D series. Its worktable takes 1,200 kg (2,646 lb) and the machine weighs approx. 4.5 T.

The Han's Laser MPS-6020D cuts sheet and plate on a 6,000 × 2,000 mm (236.2 × 78.7 in) bed. It is the first six-metre machine in the MPS-D series and the lighter of the two: the worktable is rated for 1,800 kg (3,968 lb) and the machine weighs approx. 6.0 T.

The Han's Laser MPS-6025D is the 6,000 × 2,500 mm (236.2 × 98.4 in) machine of the MPS-D laser cutting series. The extra half metre of width over the MPS-6020D brings a much stronger table, 3,000 kg (6,614 lb) against 1,800 kg (3,968 lb), and a heavier machine at approx. 7.5 T.

The Han's Laser MPS-8025D is the largest model in the MPS-D table, a gantry laser cutting machine with an 8,000 × 2,500 mm (315.0 × 98.4 in) processing area. Its worktable is rated for 4,000 kg (8,818 lb) and the machine itself weighs approx. 9.5 T.

The Han's Laser MPS-C Series is a fiber laser cutting machine for sheet metal with a 3,000 × 1,500 mm (118.1 × 59.1 in) processing area. Han's Laser publishes one data sheet for it, with a single format and no individual model codes, so this page describes the series as the maker prints it.

The Han's Laser W3015D is a 3D five-axis laser cutting machine for hot-formed automotive parts, the smallest of the three W series sizes. Instead of cutting flat sheet it trims and pierces pressed parts such as pillars and door beams after forming, when the steel is too hard to be punched economically. Its working envelope is 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Y and 650 mm (25.6 in) in Z.

The Han's Laser W3122D is the middle size of the W series, Han's Laser's 3D five-axis laser cutting machines for hot-formed automotive parts. It differs from the smallest model mainly in one direction. X travel is 3,100 mm (122.0 in), barely more than the W3015D , but Y travel grows to 2,200 mm (86.6 in).

The Han's Laser W4025D is the largest W series machine: a 3D five-axis laser cutter for hot-formed automotive parts with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y travel. It is the size for the biggest pressings in a car body, or for fixtures that hold a set of parts at once.

The HSG Cell 3015G is a five-axis laser cell for cutting formed three-dimensional parts held in fixtures; HSG files it under thermoforming and processing. Its processing format is 3,000 × 1,500 mm (118.1 × 59.1 in), laser power is 3,000-6,000 W, and the head adds a B axis of ±135° and a C axis of N*360° to the three linear axes.

The HSG R1 Pro is a tube laser for small sections: round tube from Φ8 to 120 mm (4.7 in), square tube up to 120 × 120 mm, and rectangular tube with 8-120 mm on each side. Laser power is offered from 1,500 to 6,000 W. What sets it apart in the HSG tube range is how fast it moves for its size. The table gives 2.0 G of acceleration, a maximum synchronized speed of 200 m/min and a chuck speed of 240 r/min.

The LVD LaserTWO 3015 is the smaller of two sizes in LVD's entry flatbed fiber laser line, built around a 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) sheet and offered with a 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW source. LVD sells it in two forms: a single-table machine with local covers, and a shuttle-table machine with full covers. That choice matters more than the wattage for most buyers, because it decides how the machine is loaded.

A 4,050 x 2,035 mm (159.4 x 80.1 in) bed is what separates the LVD LaserTWO 4020 from its smaller sibling. Everything that defines the cutting process is shared between the two sizes: the same 3 kW, 6 kW or 12 kW fiber sources, the same 110 m/min X-Y positioning speed, the same stated accuracy. What changes is how much sheet fits and how heavy it may be.

The LVD Puma 3015 is a 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) flatbed fiber laser with integrated shuttle tables, sold with a 3, 6, 12 or 20 kW source. It is the smallest of four Puma sizes and the one that shares its sheet format with the LaserTWO 3015 , so the useful question is what the Puma adds.

With a 4,065 x 2,035 mm (160.0 x 80.1 in) sheet capacity, the LVD Puma 4020 is the second of four Puma flatbed fiber lasers and the first size in the range that takes a sheet two metres wide. It shares its 2,070 mm (81.5 in) Y travel with the Puma 6020 , which is as wide and has a longer bed; the Puma 4020 stops at 4,200 mm (165.4 in) of X.

Six metres of bed is the reason to choose the LVD Puma 6020. Its maximum sheet is 6,160 x 2,035 mm (242.5 x 80.1 in), with 6,280 mm (247.2 in) of X travel over the same 2,070 mm (81.5 in) Y travel as the Puma 4020 . The machine suits long parts, or several smaller sheets laid along the table and cut in one program.

The LVD Puma 6525 is the largest Puma flatbed fiber laser and the only one LVD offers with a bevel head. In straight cutting it takes a 6,400 x 2,500 mm (252.0 x 98.4 in) sheet; with the optional bevel head the working format is 6,100 x 2,000 mm (240.2 x 78.7 in).

The LVD Taurus is a gantry fiber laser for extra-large plate: a modular bed that starts at 14 m and grows in 4 m steps to 42 m, a straight-cutting width of 3,200 mm (126.0 in) and sources of 12 kW, 20 kW or 30 kW.

The Machitech Fiber Prime 5x10 is a compact fiber laser with automatic shuttle tables, built for sheet up to 122 in (3,100 mm) long and 63 in (1,600 mm) wide. It is offered with a 6 or 12 kW source and sits at the entry of Machitech's laser range, below the high-power Fiber Prime S.

Larger sheet on the same platform: the Machitech Fiber Prime 6x12 takes plate 157 in (4,000 mm) long and 78 in (2,000 mm) wide, where the Fiber Prime 5x10 stops at 122 in (3,100 mm) by 63 in (1,600 mm). Source options are unchanged at 6 or 12 kW.

The Machitech Fiber Prime S 5x10 is the fastest machine in Machitech's laser range. It accelerates at 4 G and reaches a rapid speed of 9,500 ipm (240 m/min), figures the three larger Fiber Prime S sizes do not match, and it takes sources from 12 to 60 kW.

The Machitech Fiber Prime S 6x12 brings 12 to 60 kW of laser power to sheet 157 in (4,000 mm) long and 78 in (2,000 mm) wide. It is the second of four sizes and the first of the three that share one set of motion figures: 2.8 G of acceleration and a rapid speed of 7,875 ipm (200 m/min).

Plate 98 in (2,500 mm) wide goes onto the Machitech Fiber Prime S 8x20, the first Fiber Prime S size in the wide format. Sheet length is 244 in (6,200 mm). The step from the 6x12 is large in one figure above all: workpiece weight jumps to 26,100 lbs (12,000 kg).

The Machitech Fiber Prime S 8x24 is the longest shuttle-table laser Machitech lists, with a sheet length of 315 in (8,000 mm) at 98 in (2,500 mm) of width. Beyond it the range changes concept, to the Fiber Prime XL, whose laser travels over a fixed bed.
The Machitech Fiber Prime XL 10x24 is the entry size of Machitech's large-format laser. Sheet length is 323 in (8,200 mm) and sheet width 120 in (3,050 mm), and the laser source is 12 to 60 kW.

A 40 ft plate fits the Machitech Fiber Prime XL 10x40 in one piece: sheet length is 480 in (12,200 mm) at a width of 120 in (3,050 mm). It is the second of five XL sizes and the first that covers the long plate formats mills supply to heavy fabricators.

At 756 in (19,200 mm) of sheet length, the Machitech Fiber Prime XL 10x60 is longer than any single plate most shops will buy. The bed is meant to be divided. Sheet width is 120 in (3,050 mm), and the source is 12 to 60 kW.

The Machitech Fiber Prime XL 10x80 is the longest of the four XL sizes built on the 120 in (3,050 mm) width. Its sheet length is 960 in (24,400 mm), and it carries a workpiece weight of 130,680 lbs (59,275 kg).

Everything about the Machitech Fiber Prime XL 12x120 is the largest figure in Machitech's laser tables. Sheet length is 1,512 in (38,400 mm), sheet width 159 in (4,050 mm), and the workpiece weight is 235,230 lbs (106,700 kg).

Machine Name: Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 14" Ø
Description: The Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 14" Ø is the smallest of three tube and profile lasers in the Fiber Tube XL line. Its processing range is 0.8 - 13.2 in (20 - 350 mm), and it is the only model of the three that reaches down to small tube, since the next model up starts at a larger minimum size.

Machine Name: Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 19" Ø
Description: Twice the load of the smallest model: the Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 19" Ø carries 135 lb/ft (200 kg/m) and a workpiece of 5,300 lbs (2,400 kg), and processes profiles in a range of 2.2 - 19.7 in (60 - 500 mm). It is the middle of the three Fiber Tube XL machines.

Machine Name: Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 26" Ø
Description: The largest Fiber Tube XL has a fourth chuck. The Machitech Fiber Tube XL 60' L - 26" Ø is listed with 4 chucks where the other two models have 3, a processing range of 3 - 24.8 in (80 - 630 mm) and a workpiece weight of 6,600 lbs (3,000 kg).

It takes sheets up to 3050 x 1525 mm (5 ft x 10 ft). The laser side handles material up to 25 mm (1 in) thick and the machining side up to 16 mm (5/8 in).

The Penta Laser BOLT CUBE 3015 is the smallest of three 3D 5-axis fiber laser cutting machines that Penta Laser builds for automotive hot-formed parts. Its head travels 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Y and 680 mm (26.8 in) in Z, and the maker states the job plainly: cutting holes and trimming edges on hot-formed components.

Between the two ends of Penta Laser's 3D range sits the BOLT CUBE 4020, a 5-axis fiber laser cutting machine with 4,000 mm (157.5 in) of X travel and 2,000 mm (78.7 in) of Y travel. Z travel is 680 mm (26.8 in). It is built for one kind of work, the trimming and hole cutting of automotive hot-formed parts.

With 4,500 mm (177.2 in) of X travel and 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y travel, the Penta Laser BOLT CUBE 4525 is the largest machine in the BOLT CUBE series of 3D 5-axis fiber laser cutters. The series exists for automotive hot-formed components, and this size is the one to look at when the pressing, or the fixture that carries it, will not fit the smaller tables.

The Penta Laser GAN 4525 is a gantry-type 3D 5-axis laser cutting machine with 4,500 mm (177.2 in) of X travel, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) of Y travel and 680 mm (26.8 in) of Z travel. Penta Laser describes the GAN series as a machine for complex-shaped workpieces that also cuts flat sheet, and states that it supports up to 8 kW of laser power for both.

The Penta Laser NLF 12036V is a four-chuck laser tube cutting machine for long structural stock. It clamps diameters from 20 - 360 mm (0.8 - 14.2 in), takes a single piece of up to 1,200 kg (2,646 lb), and both loads and unloads lengths of 12 m.

Heavy members are what the Penta Laser NLF 12050V is for. This four-chuck laser tube cutting machine accepts a single piece of up to 2,000 kg (4,409 lb), clamps diameters of 30 - 508 mm (1.2 - 20.0 in) and handles 12 m on both the loading and the unloading side.

The Penta Laser NLT 12036V belongs to the NLT series, which Penta Laser sells as its three-chuck laser tube cutting machine for structural sections. The clamping diameter range is 30 - 350 mm (1.2 - 13.8 in), one piece may weigh up to 1,200 kg (2,646 lb), and the machine loads and unloads 12 m lengths.

For pipe and sections up to 508 mm across, Penta Laser's three-chuck NLT series offers the NLT 12050V. Its clamping diameter range is 30 - 508 mm (1.2 - 20.0 in) and its maximum tube weight is 2,000 kg (4,409 lb) per piece, on a machine that loads and unloads 12 m.

The Penta Laser SEA HORSE II 26025 is a gantry laser cutting machine for structural steel: H-beams, channel steel, C-beams and flat plate. Its X travel is 26,050 mm (1,025.6 in), with 2,550 mm (100.4 in) of Y and 960 mm (37.8 in) of Z. That long bed is split into two stations, which Penta Laser calls a dual-station design for steel sections and plate.

The Penta Laser WPB 6025 / 9025 is a dual-chuck laser tube cutting machine listed with 3 - 6 kW of laser power. It cuts round tube of Ф20 - 230 mm and square tube from 20 × 20 to 230 × 230 mm, with a maximum loading length of 6.5 m and 9.5 m as an option, which is what the two halves of the model name refer to.

Tube up to Ф260 mm and 60 kg/m is the limit of the Penta Laser WPB 6028 / 9028, the larger of the two dual-chuck columns in Penta Laser's WPB series. Square tube runs from 20 × 20 to 260 × 260 mm. Laser power is 3 - 6 kW.

The Penta Laser WPC 12036 / 9036 / 6036 is a three-chuck laser tube cutting machine offered in three bed lengths, with maximum loading lengths of 12.5 / 9.5 / 6.5 m and matching unloading lengths. Laser power is 6 - 12 kW. The profile range is Ф30 - 350 mm for round tube and 30 × 30 to 350 × 350 mm for square.

At 12 - 20 kW and 200 kg/m, the Penta Laser WPC 12050 / 9050 is the heavy variant of Penta Laser's three-chuck laser tube cutting machine. It takes round tube of Ф60 - 500 mm and comes in two lengths, with loading and unloading of 12.5 / 9.5 m.

The Penta Laser WPL6025 / 9025 puts three chucks on a horizontal bed at the small end of Penta Laser's tube range. It is listed with 3 - 6 kW, a profile range of Ф20 - 240 mm round and 20 × 20 to 240 × 240 mm square, and a bearing capacity of 45 kg/m.

Round tube up to Ф270 mm goes through the Penta Laser WPL6028 / 9028, the larger column of the three-chuck WPL series. Square tube is listed from 20 × 20 to 270 × 270 mm and the bearing capacity is 60 kg/m. Power is 3 - 6 kW.

Four laser heads cut the same part at the same time on the Prima Power Giga Laser Next. It is a 3D fiber laser cell for high production volumes, such as automotive stampings and castings, and it replaces the usual row of single-head machines with one station.

The Prima Power Laser Next 1530-2130 is a 3D fiber laser built for one task above all: trimming hot-stamped steel automotive components in volume. Prima Power lists it as one machine in two widths, with X 3,050 mm (120.1 in), Z 612 mm (24.1 in) and a Y of either 1,530 mm (60.2 in) or 2,100 mm (82.7 in).

The Prima Power Laser Next 2141 is a 3D five-axis fiber laser with a large work area: X 4,140 mm (163.0 in), Y 2,100 mm (82.7 in) and Z 1,020 mm (40.2 in). It is the flexible member of the Laser Next family, intended for job shops and press shops that cut stamped parts of many sizes, and it also handles 2D cutting and welding.

The Prima Power Laser Next Core 2131 is the compact 3D fiber laser of the Laser Next line, aimed at job shops and small to medium batches. Axis strokes are X 3,160 mm (124.4 in), Y 2,100 mm (82.7 in) and Z 750 mm (29.5 in).

Two metres of X travel distinguish the Prima Power LASERDYNE 795 XL. Its travels are X 2,000 mm (78.7 in), Y 1,000 mm (39.4 in) and Z 1,000 mm (39.4 in), where the LASERDYNE 795 XS has 1,000 mm on all three.

The Prima Power LASERDYNE 795 XS is a multi-axis laser processing system for welding, drilling and cutting, with a cubic travel of X 1,000 mm, Y 1,000 mm and Z 1,000 mm (39.4 in each). It is the shorter of the two 795 versions.

The Yawei HLA-1530 is a single-table fiber laser cutting machine with an open cutting area, sized for one 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) sheet. It is the smallest laser Yawei lists, with a layout of 5,000 x 3,700 x 2,000 mm (196.9 x 145.7 x 78.7 in).

With one open table of 4,065 x 2,035 mm (160.0 x 80.1 in), the Yawei HLA-2040 is the four-metre member of Yawei's single-table HLA laser series. Laser power is 3 or 6 kW and trajectory speed 140 m/min.
The Yawei HLA-2560 is the largest HLA single-table laser in the low-power group: a 6,100 x 2,545 mm (240.2 x 100.2 in) cutting range with 3 or 6 kW. Above it, the HLA-2580 starts at 12 kW.
High power on an open single table begins with the Yawei HLA-2580. It cuts 8,100 x 2,545 mm (318.9 x 100.2 in) and is listed with 12, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 or 80 kW.

Twelve-metre plate on one open table: the Yawei HLA-25120 has a cutting range of 12,100 x 2,545 mm (476.4 x 100.2 in) and a layout of 15,500 x 5,500 x 2,000 mm (610.2 x 216.5 x 78.7 in). Laser power options are 12, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 or 80 kW.

The Yawei HLA-30130 is the largest single-table laser Yawei lists, with a cutting range of 13,100 x 3,100 mm (515.7 x 122.0 in). It is the only HLA wide enough for three-metre plate, on a Y stroke of 3,120 mm (122.8 in).
The Yawei HLB-1530 is the smallest HLB high-speed series fiber laser, a machine Yawei aims at medium-thin sheet. It cuts 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) at up to 140 m/min with 3, 6 or 12 kW.

For four-metre sheet in thin and medium gauges, Yawei's HLB series offers the Yawei HLB-2040: a 4,065 x 2,035 mm (160.0 x 80.1 in) cutting range, 3, 6 or 12 kW, and a maximum trajectory speed of 140 m/min.

The Yawei HLB-2560 stretches the HLB medium-thin sheet laser to six metres. The cutting range is 6,100 x 2,545 mm (240.2 x 100.2 in), the worktable load 3,000 kg (6,614 lb), and the power options 3, 6 or 12 kW.

The Yawei HLE-1530 is the entry size of the HLE high-performance fiber laser series, cutting 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) with 3, 6 or 12 kW of laser power. Maximum X-Y trajectory speed is 170 m/min.

A four-metre table at moderate power: the Yawei HLE-2040 cuts 4,065 x 2,035 mm (160.0 x 80.1 in) and is offered with 3, 6 or 12 kW. It belongs to Yawei's HLE high-performance series, the line the maker describes as high performance at low running cost.
The Yawei HLE-2560 is the six-metre model of the HLE fiber laser series and the largest one sold in the lower power band: 3, 6 or 12 kW. Its cutting range is 6,100 x 2,545 mm (240.2 x 100.2 in).

From the Yawei HLE-2580 upward, the HLE series is a high-power plate line. This model cuts 8,100 x 2,545 mm (318.9 x 100.2 in) and is listed with 12, 20, 30, 40, 60 or 80 kW, the lowest option being 12 kW.

The Yawei HLE-25120 is a twelve-metre fiber laser cutting machine with a 12,100 x 2,545 mm (476.4 x 100.2 in) cutting range, and the one HLE model for which a machine weight is published: 32,000 kg (70,547 lb).

Width is what the Yawei HLE-32130 adds. Its cutting range is 13,000 x 3,200 mm (511.8 x 126.0 in), on a Y stroke of 3,220 mm (126.8 in), where every other HLE model stops near 2,545 mm. Power options are 12, 20, 30, 40, 60 or 80 kW.

The Yawei HLF-1530 opens Yawei's HLF line, which the maker calls its classic flagship series of fiber laser cutting machines. It cuts 3,000 x 1,500 mm (118.1 x 59.1 in) at up to 200 m/min and is offered with 3, 6, 12 or 20 kW.

With a cutting range of 4,000 x 2,000 mm (157.5 x 78.7 in), the Yawei HLF-2040 is the second size in the HLF classic flagship series and the larger of the two that can still be ordered with a 3 kW source. Power options are 3, 6, 12 or 20 kW.

The Yawei HLF-2560 is a six-metre fiber laser cutting machine with a 6,000 x 2,500 mm (236.2 x 98.4 in) cutting range and power options of 6, 12, 20 or 30 kW. It is the only HLF model for which Yawei prints a machine weight: 16,000 kg (35,273 lb).

Eight metres of cutting length and up to 80 kW: the Yawei HLF-2580 is where the HLF classic flagship series becomes a heavy-plate machine. The cutting range is 8,000 x 2,500 mm (315.0 x 98.4 in), and the laser generator options are 12, 20, 30, 40, 60 or 80 kW.

The Yawei HLF-25120 is the longest machine in Yawei's HLF series: a 12,000 x 2,500 mm (472.4 x 98.4 in) cutting range on an X stroke of 12,040 mm (474.0 in). Power options are 12, 20, 30, 40, 60 or 80 kW.

The Yawei HLG-25120 is a floor-mounted gantry laser cutting machine with a machining range of 12,000 x 2,500 mm (472.4 x 98.4 in). In the HLG design the rails are fixed to the floor and the gantry travels along them, which is how Yawei reaches formats that a machine bed cannot.

Twenty-four metres by three: the Yawei HLG-30240 has the largest machining range of any laser with fixed figures on Yawei's site, 24,000 x 3,000 mm (944.9 x 118.1 in). It is a floor-mounted gantry machine, and its table is rated for 28,000 kg (61,728 lb).

The Yawei HLX-1530 is the smallest of the HLX ultra-fast fiber laser cutting machines, with a cutting range of 3,050 x 1,525 mm (120.1 x 60.0 in) and a maximum X-Y trajectory speed of 200 m/min. Laser power is 6, 12 or 20 kW.

Four metres by two is the sheet format of the Yawei HLX-2040, the middle model of the HLX ultra-fast series. Its cutting range is 4,065 x 2,035 mm (160.0 x 80.1 in), served by strokes of 4,085 mm (160.8 in) and 2,055 mm (80.9 in).

The Yawei HLX-2560 is the largest HLX ultra-fast fiber laser, cutting 6,100 x 2,545 mm (240.2 x 100.2 in). It is the one model in the series with a 340 mm (13.4 in) Z stroke and a worktable rated for 3,500 kg (7,716 lb).

Yawei lists the YDAC, YDGC as a single 3D five-axis laser cutting machine page with one specification table. The linear strokes are 3,000 mm (118.1 in) in X, 1,500 mm (59.1 in) in Y and 650 mm (25.6 in) in Z, and the head rotates N x 360° on the C axis and ±135° on the A axis.

Small tube, cut quickly: the Yawei YTB-6024 handles Round tube Φ10-Φ240 mm and positions at 90 m/min. It is the lighter model of the YTB universal tube laser series and takes tubes up to 300 kg (661 lb).

The Yawei YTB-6035 is the larger of two YTB universal tube laser cutting machines. Yawei lists its range as Round tube Φ20-Φ350 mm; square tube Φ20-Φ250 mm, with a maximum tube weight of 500 kg (1,102 lb) and an X axis stroke of 6,800 mm (267.7 in).
The Yawei YTF-6024 is the smallest YTF high-performance tube laser: 6,800 mm (267.7 in) of X-axis travel, round tube listed as Round tube Φ10-Φ240 mm, and a pipe weight of up to 200 kg (441 lb).

The Yawei YTF-6035 is the larger of the two short YTF tube lasers, with 6,800 mm (267.7 in) of X-axis travel and a round tube range printed as Round tube Φ20-Φ360 mm. Maximum pipe weight is 300 kg (661 lb).
The Yawei YTF-9020 is the small-section, long-travel member of the YTF tube laser series. It cuts Round tube Φ20-Φ210 mm and square pipe □20-□150 mm, on an X-axis travel of 9,800 mm (385.8 in).

Speed returns to the top of the list with the Yawei YTF-9025. This YTF tube laser turns its A and B axes at 120 r/min and accelerates at 1.2 G on X and Y, twice the rotary speed of the heaviest models in the series.

In the middle of the YTF high-performance tube laser series sits the Yawei YTF-9035: 9,800 mm (385.8 in) of X-axis travel, a machining range of Round tube Φ20-Φ350 mm; square pipe □20-□250 mm, and a pipe weight limit of 500 kg (1,102 lb).

The Yawei YTF-9045 brings the largest section range of the YTF tube laser series, Round tube Φ20-Φ430 mm and square pipe □20-□300 mm, to a mid-length machine with 9,800 mm (385.8 in) of X-axis travel.

A long bed with a mid-size chuck opening defines the Yawei YTF-12035. Its X-axis travel is 12,800 mm (503.9 in), the longest Yawei lists for a tube laser, and its machining range is Round tube Φ20-Φ350 mm; square pipe □20-□250 mm.

The Yawei YTF-12045 is the top model of the YTF high-performance tube laser series by every measure of size: an X-axis travel of 12,800 mm (503.9 in), Round tube Φ20-Φ430 mm and a maximum pipe weight of 800 kg (1,764 lb).

Bar capacity is 52 mm (2 in), but the work envelope is not small: maximum workpiece diameter is 386 mm (15.2 in) and maximum workpiece length is 515 mm (20.3 in). Two spindles, gang tooling and a built-in loader make the Accuway GX-100 a small production cell for parts no bigger than a fist. Both spindles are identical: A2-5 nose, 5 in chuck, 6,000 rpm, 5.5/7.5 kW (7.4/10.1 hp).
The Accuway GX-100TM swaps the gang slide of the GX-100 for a turret. It is a twin-spindle loader lathe with a 12-station BMT-45 turret, servo mechanical drive and rotary tools at 6,000 rpm.

Speed between cuts is the selling point of the Accuway JT-150. It is a slant-bed lathe on linear ways, and both axes rapid at 30 m/min (1,181 in/min), half as fast again as the 20 m/min (787 in/min) of the box-way UL-15 that shares its spindle.

The Accuway JT-150M pairs 30 m/min (1,181 in/min) rapids with rotary tools that turn at 6,000 rpm. Everything about it is aimed at short cycles on small parts: linear ways, a 350 mm (13.8 in) Z travel, a 12-station BMT/VDI turret.

For shops that want a mid-size lathe with quick axes, Accuway lists the JT-200. It has 600 mm (23.6 in) of Z travel and a 300 mm (11.8 in) turning diameter, and it runs on linear ways at 30 m/min (1,181 in/min). The box-way UL-20 , its nearest relative, rapids at 20 m/min (787 in/min).

The Accuway JT-200M is the longest of the JT linear-way lathes and the only one of the four that combines 600 mm (23.6 in) of Z travel with rotary tools. It turns 230 mm (9.1 in) in diameter and 450 mm (17.7 in) in length.

The Accuway UA-200LY is a long-bed, Y-axis turning center with one fixed spindle configuration. Where the other UT-200 and UA-200 pages print four spindle columns, this table has a single one: an A2-6 nose, an 8 in chuck, 52 mm (2.0 in) of bar capacity, 4,500 rpm and an 11/15 kW (14.8/20.1 hp) motor.

Fifteen turret stations and 6,000 rpm rotary tools set the Accuway UA-330LY apart from the UT-300 lathes it resembles in size. It is a long-bed, single-spindle Y-axis machine: 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of Z travel, ±50 mm (±2.0 in) of Y, and a tailstock.

The Accuway UL-15 is a short, box-way lathe for 6 in and 8 in chuck work. Accuway's heading calls it a flat bed CNC turning center. It has 350 mm (13.8 in) of Z travel, 175 mm (6.9 in) of X travel and an 11/15 kW (14.8/20.1 hp) spindle motor in a machine that weighs 2,850 kg (6,283 lb).

The Accuway UL-15A is a two-turret version of the UL-15 , set up for bar work in a collet. Accuway heads the page Two Turret Flat Bed CNC Turning Center and files it under two turret, single spindle lathes.
Fast live tools on a short, stiff lathe: the Accuway UL-15M runs rotary tools at 6,000 rpm from a 3.7/5.5 kW (5.0/7.4 hp) motor, in a 12-station BMT/VDI turret with servo mechanical drive.

With 625 mm (24.6 in) of Z travel the Accuway UL-20 doubles the turning length of the UL-15 to 600 mm (23.6 in). The rest of the machine is carried over: box ways, 175 mm (6.9 in) of X travel, a 280 mm (11.0 in) turning diameter and an 11/15 kW (14.8/20.1 hp) spindle.

The Accuway UL-20M is a box-way lathe with live tools and half a metre of turning length. Its figures: 625 mm (24.6 in) of Z travel, a 500 mm (19.7 in) turning length, a 180 mm (7.1 in) turning diameter and rotary tools at 6,000 rpm.

The Accuway UT-100 is a small chucker that loads itself. A two-axis lathe with a 6 in chuck is combined with a built-in gantry loader, in a cell 1.7 m long that weighs 1,900 kg (4,189 lb). Accuway lists it under integrated loader lathes.

Take the loader off the UT-100 and the result is the Accuway UT-100E: a plain, very compact two-axis lathe with a 6 in chuck, 1,800 kg (3,968 lb) in weight and 1.7 x 1.8 x 1.8 m (66.9 x 70.9 x 70.9 in) in size. Accuway lists it with its single-turret, single-spindle lathes.

The Accuway UT-100EM is the smallest live-tool lathe on Accuway's site that is sold without a loader. It weighs 1,800 kg (3,968 lb), holds a 6 in chuck, and drives rotary tools at 6,000 rpm with 3.7/5.5 kW (5.0/7.4 hp).
The Accuway UT-100EY is the stand-alone Y-axis lathe of the UT-100 group. Its table matches the lathe part of the UT-100Y row for row, and leaves out the loader.

Small turned parts that also need a cross hole or a milled slot can run unattended on the Accuway UT-100M. It is the UT-100 loader lathe with rotary tools: 6,000 rpm at the tool, a 3.7/5.5 kW (5.0/7.4 hp) driver, 12 stations.

On the Accuway UT-100MX the loader is bigger than the lathe. Its traverse axis has a 1,650 mm (65.0 in) stroke, against a lathe Z travel of 230 mm (9.1 in), and the loader has its own control system, named in the table as OMRON.

A Y axis on a 6 in loader lathe: the Accuway UT-100Y gives small automated parts ±25 mm (±1.0 in) of off-centre reach. It keeps the built-in loader of the UT-100 line and the 6,000 rpm rotary tools of the UT-100M .

The Accuway UV-55E is the small frame of the maker's vertical turning centers: 550 mm (21.7 in) maximum turning diameter, 550 mm (21.7 in) turning length and a 750 mm (29.5 in) swing. With the chuck facing up, a heavy disc or ring is lowered onto the jaws and gravity seats it, which is the reason to choose a vertical lathe for short, wide parts.

A BMT turret with servo mechanical drive is what the Accuway UV-55EC adds to the small vertical turning frame. The base model carries a hydraulic BOT turret. Here the tooling system row reads BMT, and the options list includes 0 degree and 90 degree rotary tool holders, which is the hardware for drilling and milling on a turned part without a second machine.

Instead of a turret, the Accuway UV-75ATC carries its tools in a 12-position magazine and loads them into a ram with a BT50 taper. That is the ATC type of vertical turning center: one tool in the cut at a time, held in a large, stiff interface, and exchanged automatically.

The Accuway UV-75ATCC is a vertical turning center whose ram carries a driven tool spindle. The tool spindle section of its table lists a BT50 taper, 3,000 rpm, belt drive, a 100 mm (3.9 in) bearing diameter, a 5.5/7.5 kW (7.4/10.1 hp) motor and 105 N-m (77.4 lb-ft) of maximum torque. On the UV-75ATC the same section holds the taper alone.

The Accuway UV-75E turns parts up to 750 mm (29.5 in) in diameter and 700 mm (27.6 in) tall on a 24 in chuck. It weighs 15,000 kg (33,069 lb), nearly three times the UV-55E , and that mass is the main thing a buyer gets for stepping up: a vertical lathe heavy enough for large castings and forgings.

On the Accuway UV-75EC the 750 mm class vertical lathe gets a BMT turret with servo mechanical drive in place of the hydraulic BOT unit. The rest of the table is that of the UV-75E : 750 mm (29.5 in) maximum turning diameter, 700 mm (27.6 in) turning length, an A2-11 spindle and 15,000 kg (33,069 lb) of machine.

The Akira Seiki GT12 is a gang-tool CNC lathe. It has no turret: the tool storage row reads Gang Tool 8, meaning the tools stand in a row on the cross slide and the slide moves from one to the next. That is why X travel is 400 mm (15.7 in), far longer than on a turret lathe of this size, while Z is only 220 mm (8.7 in).

The Akira Seiki SL15 is the smallest turret lathe in the SL two-axis range, set up as a collet machine. The chuck row lists a CR42 or 5C collet, the draw tube bore is 42 mm (1.7 in), and maximum cutting length is 200 mm (7.9 in). Maximum cutting diameter is 290 mm (11.4 in) under a 450 mm (17.7 in) swing.

A 6" chuck, a tailstock and 350 mm (13.8 in) of Z travel define the Akira Seiki SL20, the small general-purpose lathe of the SL two-axis line. Maximum cutting diameter is 290 mm (11.4 in), maximum cutting length 330 mm (13 in), and the draw tube bore is 45 mm (1.8 in).

The Akira Seiki SL20 UHP is listed among the maker's special purpose machines as a super performance turning center. Akira Seiki states its aim plainly: turning instead of grinding, to shorten the production process. In other words it is an SL20 -size lathe intended for finish turning to tolerances that would otherwise go to a grinder.

The Akira Seiki SL25 is an 8" chuck lathe with a 530 mm (20.9 in) swing, a maximum cutting diameter of 350 mm (13.8 in) and a maximum cutting length of 400 mm (15.7 in). It is the first SL model with the A2-6 spindle nose and the 12-station turret used on the larger machines.

The Akira Seiki SL25MC is the smallest lathe in the SL Mill-Turn group. Its application row reads X+Z+C: a two-axis turning center with a C axis on the spindle and driven tools in the turret, so cross holes, flats and keyways can be machined without a second setup.

The SL30 is the mid-size workhorse of Akira Seiki's two-axis lathes: an 8" chuck as standard with a 10" option, a 400 mm (15.7 in) maximum cutting diameter and a 600 mm (23.6 in) cutting length. Swing over the bed is 600 mm (23.6 in).

The Akira Seiki SL30L is the long-bed version of the SL30 . Maximum cutting length is 1,000 mm (39.4 in) and Z travel 1,010 mm (39.8 in), where the SL30 stops at a 600 mm (23.6 in) cutting length. Chuck, bore and swing are unchanged: an 8" chuck with a 10" option, a 65 mm (2.6 in) draw tube bore, and a 400 mm (15.7 in) maximum cutting diameter.

On the Akira Seiki SL30MC the SL30 lathe gains a C axis and a driven-tool turret. The application row reads X+Z+C. The turret has 12 stations on a VDI40 interface, with ER32 collets on the live holders and a power-tool speed of 4,000 rpm.

The Akira Seiki SL30SMC is the sub-spindle lathe of the SL family. The application row lists X+Z+B+C: turning axes, a C axis, and a B axis that carries the second spindle along the bed to take the part from the main chuck. With driven tools in the turret, a part can be turned and milled on both ends and dropped complete.
8" chuck (STD): 4,500 rpm; 10" chuck (OPT): 4,200 rpm

Torque is the story of the Akira Seiki SL35. Its A2-8 spindle delivers 727 Nm (536 lb-ft) at peak, with 30 HP (22.4 kW) and a top speed of 3,500 rpm. The SL30 , one size down, has 305 Nm (225 lb-ft). For a 10" chuck lathe, standard here with a 12" option, that is a large step.

The Akira Seiki SL35L combines the high-torque SL35 headstock with a one-metre bed. Maximum cutting length is 1,000 mm (39.4 in), Z travel 1,025 mm (40.4 in), and the spindle still delivers 727 Nm (536 lb-ft) and 30 HP (22.4 kW) at peak through an A2-8 nose.

The Akira Seiki SL35LMC is the long-bed mill-turn lathe in the 10" chuck class. Cutting length is 940 mm (37 in) and Z travel 1,000 mm (39.4 in), and the tailstock travels 970 mm (38.2 in) on an MT4 quill.

The Akira Seiki SL35MC pairs the highest-torque belt-drive headstock in the SL line with a driven-tool turret. The A2-8 spindle gives 727 Nm (536 lb-ft) and 30 HP (22.4 kW) at peak, up to 3,500 rpm, and the application row lists X+Z+C.

The Akira Seiki SL40 is the big-bore, geared-head lathe of the SL line. It carries a 15" chuck as standard and an 18" chuck as an option on an A2-11 spindle nose, with a 103 mm (4.1 in) draw tube bore. Peak torque is 2,944 Nm (2,171 lb-ft), which the table marks as coming through a gear box, and peak power is 60 HP (44.7 kW).

With a maximum cutting length of 1,500 mm (59 in), the Akira Seiki SL40L is the longest lathe in the SL two-axis range. Z travel is 1,520 mm (58.9 in) and the tailstock travels 1,550 mm (61 in), on an MT5 quill with a 100 mm (3.9 in) stroke.

The SL40LMC is the largest turning machine Akira Seiki lists with driven tools: a long-bed, geared-head lathe with a C axis. Cutting length is 1,380 mm (54.3 in), Z travel 1,450 mm (57.1 in), and the tailstock travels the same 1,450 mm (57.1 in) on an MT5 quill.

Akira Seiki's SL40MC is a geared-head mill-turn lathe. The headstock is that of the SL40 : A2-11 nose, 2,500 rpm, 60 HP (44.7 kW) peak and 2,944 Nm (2,171 lb-ft) of peak torque through a gear box, with a 103 mm (4.1 in) draw tube bore and a 15" chuck (18" optional). To that the MC version adds a C axis and a driven-tool turret.

The Biglia B620 ASA 5" is the small-spindle column of the B620 universal turning centre: 51 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity, a 250 mm (9.8 in) maximum machining diameter and a main spindle that runs to 5,000 rpm. Biglia builds the B620 in six versions, from a two-axis machine with CNC tailstock to the B620YS with driven tools, Y-axis and sub-spindle, and its table gives one column per spindle size instead of one per version. This page is the ASA 5" column.

With the ASA 6" spindle the Biglia B620 takes 70 mm (2.8 in) bar and machines up to 360 mm (14.2 in) in diameter over a 620 mm (24.4 in) length. Of the three spindle sizes in Biglia's B620 table this one carries the most motor power, 30 - 40 kW (40.2 - 53.6 hp), and it turns at up to 4,500 rpm.

Torque is the reason to pick the ASA 8" spindle on a Biglia B620. The table gives 398 - 700 Nm (294 - 516 lb-ft) at the main spindle, the highest of the three spindle sizes, together with the largest bar capacity in the range at 80 mm (3.1 in). Maximum speed is 3,200 rpm and motor power 15 - 22 kW (20.1 - 29.5 hp).

In the Biglia BMX 51-Y2 the main spindle and the sub-spindle are the same unit, and that symmetry is the point of the model. Each has an ASA 5" nose, runs to 5,000 rpm and is rated 17 / 25 kW with 108 / 159 Nm. The machine takes 51 mm (2.0 in) bar and belongs to what Biglia calls the fourth generation of its QUATTRO series of double-spindle, double-turret turning centres.

The Biglia BMX 70-Y2 is the middle size of Biglia's twin-spindle, twin-turret BMX line and the one with the strongest motor: 30 / 40 kW (40.2 / 53.6 hp) at the main spindle, with 255 / 286 Nm and a top speed of 4,500 rpm. Bar capacity is 70 mm (2.8 in) through a 78 mm bore on an ASA 6" nose.

Biglia's brochure for the BMX twin-turret line has a third column beside the 51 and 70 mm machines: the BMX 80-Y2, with 80 mm (3.1 in) bar capacity and an ASA 8" main spindle. It is the torque version of the family. Maximum torque is 441 / 477 Nm (325 / 352 lb-ft), motor power 23 / 25 kW and top speed 3,500 rpm.

The Campro CPL-10MC is the smallest of the maker's turning and milling centers: a 6 in chuck slant-bed lathe with a C axis and a 12-position servo live turret. The main spindle runs to 6,000 rpm and the driven tools to 5,000 rpm.

With an 8 in chuck, an 11 / 15 kW (20 HP) spindle and a VDI-40 live turret, the Campro CPL-20MC is the mid-size turning and milling center of the CPL-MC series. It turns up to 260 mm (10.2 in) in diameter and 470 mm (18.5 in) in length, and mills over 432 mm (17 in).

The Campro CPL-30MC stretches the maker's VDI-40 turning and milling center to 670 mm (26.3 in) of turning length and gives it a 10 in chuck and a Ø75 mm (Ø2.9 in) hole through the draw tube. Maximum turning diameter is 260 mm (10.2 in).

The Campro CPL-106 is a 6 in chuck slant-bed CNC lathe and the fastest-turning model in the CPL series: its A2-5 spindle runs to 6,000 rpm. Maximum turning diameter is Ø290 mm (11.4 in), the standard turning diameter Ø240 mm (9.4 in), and the maximum turning length 350 mm (13.7 in).

An 8 in chuck on the smallest bed in the range: the Campro CPL-158 is a short, stout CNC lathe for chucking work. Its maximum turning diameter is Ø270 mm (10.6 in) and its maximum turning length only 320 mm (12.5 in), on the same 2,962 x 1,591 mm (116 in x 62 in) floor plan as the CPL-106 .

The Campro CPL-208 is the general-purpose 8 in lathe of the CPL series. It turns up to Ø400 mm (15.7 in) in diameter and 500 mm (19.6 in) in length, with 580 mm (22.8 in) between centers, and its spindle motor is 11 / 15 kW (20 HP).

The Campro CPL-3010SY is the most fully equipped lathe in the CPL range: main spindle, sub-spindle, Y axis and a 12-station BMT-65 live turret on a one-piece 30° slant bed. The main spindle has a 10 in chuck and runs to 4,000 rpm with a 15 / 22 kW (30 HP) motor.

A Y axis, a live turret and a tailstock: the Campro CPL-3010Y is a single-spindle turning and milling center for shaft-type parts with off-centre features. It has a 10 in chuck and turns up to 470 mm (18.5 in) in diameter and 755 mm (29.7 in) in length.

Power is what distinguishes the Campro CPL-3510. This 10 in chuck CNC lathe carries a 22 / 26 kW (35 HP) spindle motor, the same rating Campro fits to its largest CPL machines, on a bed that turns Ø400 mm (15.7 in) by 700 mm (27.5 in).

The Campro CPL-3512 is a 12 in chuck CNC lathe with a metre of turning length and a spindle bore large enough for pipe and heavy bar. Maximum turning diameter is Ø500 mm (19.6 in); the hole through the draw tube is Ø117.5 mm (Ø4.6 in).

The Campro CPL-3512MC brings live tooling to a big-bore lathe. It has a 12 in chuck on an A2-11 spindle with a Ø117.5 mm (Ø4.6 in) hole through the draw tube, a C axis, and a 12-position servo live turret on the VDI-50 system.

The Campro NT-208 (Box) is the plain 2-axis version of the NT series: an 8 in chuck CNC lathe on a 30° slant bed with box ways, a 10-station hydraulic turret and a tailstock. It turns up to Ø420 mm (16.5 in) in diameter and 550 mm (21.6 in) in length.

The Campro NT-208M adds milling to the box-way NT-208 lathe. It keeps the 8 in chuck, the tailstock and the Ø420 mm (Ø16.5 in) by 550 mm (21.6 in) turning envelope, and replaces the plain turret with a 12-station servo live turret and a C axis.

Two spindles and no live tools: the Campro NT-208S is a twin-spindle CNC lathe for parts that are turned on both ends. The main spindle carries an 8 in chuck and the sub spindle a 6 in chuck, on the box-way 30° slant bed of the NT series.

The Campro NT-208SM is a twin-spindle turning and milling center: an 8 in main spindle, a 6 in sub-spindle and a 12-station servo live turret with C-axis control, on the box-way slant bed of the NT series. It has no Y axis.

The Campro NT-208SY carries every option of the NT-208 platform at once: a sub-spindle, a Y axis and a BMT live turret. It is an 8 in chuck turning and milling center with Ø400 mm (Ø15.7 in) of turning diameter, 520 mm (20.4 in) of turning length and 100 (±50) mm of Y travel.

For shafts and chucked parts that need off-centre milling but not a second spindle, Campro builds the NT-208Y. It is an 8 in chuck box-way lathe with a Y axis of 100 (±50) mm, a 12-station BMT-55 live turret, a C axis and a tailstock.

Campro presents the NT-2510SY as a 30° slant-bed, box way turning and milling center with a Y axis, a BMT living turret and a sub-spindle. The published table gives a maximum turning diameter of Ø400 mm (Ø15.7 in), a maximum turning length of 520 mm (20.4 in) and a Y travel of 100 (±50) mm.

The Campro NT-2510Y is the Y-axis turning and milling center of the NT-2510 pair without a sub-spindle. Campro publishes a short table for it: Ø400 mm (Ø15.7 in) maximum turning diameter, 520 mm (20.4 in) maximum turning length, 630 mm (24.8 in) of Z travel and a Y axis of 100 (±50) mm.

The Campro VT-350 is a compact vertical CNC lathe: the chuck faces upward, the part is loaded from above and gravity seats it. It has a 12 in chuck on an A2-8 spindle and a maximum turning diameter of Ø350 mm (Ø13.8 in).

Campro lists two vertical lathes, and the VT-420 is the one with the longer cross slide. Its X axis travels 210 + 25 mm, which raises the maximum turning diameter to Ø420 mm (Ø16.5 in). In every other row of the table it is identical to the VT-350 .

The Chevalier FBL-230 is an 8 in chuck slant-bed CNC lathe with box ways, the entry model of the FBL two-axis range. It turns up to 12.2 in (311 mm) in diameter and 17.4 in (443 mm) in length, with 20.0 in (507 mm) between centers, on a spindle that reaches 4,000 rpm.

The Chevalier FBL-230 MC is the live-tooling version of Chevalier's 8 in box-way lathe. MC stands for the driven tool function: the 12-station BMT-55 turret can carry rotating drills and end mills, so cross holes, flats and bolt patterns are done in the lathe instead of on a second machine.

The Chevalier FBL-250SY is a box-way turning center with a Y axis, live tooling and a sub-spindle, sized around an 8 in (203 mm) chuck and an 18.1 in (Ø460 mm) maximum cutting diameter. Where Chevalier's FNL-220LSY is a compact bar machine limited to 10.6 in (Ø270 mm), this one has the swing and the bed for chucked castings and forgings as well.

The Chevalier FBL-250Y is the tailstock version of Chevalier's box-way Y-axis turning center. It turns up to 18.1 in (Ø460 mm) in diameter and 22 in (558 mm) in length, takes a chuck of 8 in or 10 in, and supports the free end of the work on a servo tailstock that travels 25.6 in (650 mm).

The Chevalier FBL-300 is a mid-size slant-bed CNC lathe with box ways and a 3.0 in (77 mm) bar capacity. It turns 20 in (510 mm) in diameter and 23.4 in (594 mm) in length through an A2-8 spindle with a 3.5 in (88 mm) bore, at up to 2,500 rpm.

The Chevalier FBL-300L is the long-bed version of the FBL-300, a box-way slant-bed lathe for shafts. Z travel is 63 in (1,600 mm), distance between centers 67.2 in (1,708 mm) and maximum cutting length 62.2 in (1,554 mm), on the same A2-8 spindle and 20 in (510 mm) cutting diameter as the short machine.

The Chevalier FBL-300LMC is the long-bed, live-tooling member of the FBL-300 family: 63 in (1,600 mm) of Z travel and 67.2 in (1,708 mm) between centers, with a driven-tool turret. It exists for long shafts that need more than turning, such as keyways, cross-drilled oil holes, wrench flats and drilled ends.

The Chevalier FBL-300MC adds live tooling to the FBL-300 box-way lathe, using a 12-station BMT-75 turret. BMT-75 is a large driven-tool interface, a size up from the BMT-55 on Chevalier's 8 in MC machine, and it suits the heavier drilling and milling that parts of this diameter call for.

The Chevalier FBL-320SY is the big-bore model of the box-way Y-axis turning centers, with a sub-spindle. Its main spindle has an A2-8 nose, takes a 10 in or 12 in chuck and passes 3 in (77 mm) bar, at a top speed of 3,500 rpm. That is a heavier front end than the FBL-250SY, whose A2-6 ASA spindle runs to 4,500 rpm with 2.5 in (65 mm) bar.

The Chevalier FBL-320Y pairs the larger A2-8 spindle of the FBL-320 line with a servo tailstock and a Y-axis live turret. It is the heaviest-duty single-spindle machine among Chevalier's Y-axis lathes: a 10 in (254 mm) chuck, a 3.5 in (88 mm) spindle bore, 3 in (77 mm) bar capacity and 14,330 lb (6,500 kg) of machine on box ways.

The Chevalier FBL-360B is a large slant-bed CNC lathe with box ways, built around an A2-11 spindle nose and a choice of two spindle bores. It turns 22.4 in (570 mm) in diameter and 30 in (762 mm) in length, and it is the short-bed, turning-only member of a family that also comes with live tooling and a long bed.

The Chevalier FBL-360B MC puts a 12-station BMT-75 live turret on Chevalier's A2-11 box-way lathe. With driven tools the machine drills, taps and mills a part while it is still in the chuck, on a frame heavy enough for the turning that comes first.

Shaft length is the whole point of the Chevalier FBL-360BL. This long-bed box-way lathe cuts 79.7 in (2,026 mm) between a chuck on an A2-11 spindle and a programmable tailstock, with 90.5 in (2,300 mm) between centers and 82.6 in (2,100 mm) of Z travel.

The Chevalier FBL-360L MC combines the two options of the family, the long bed and the live turret. It offers 82.6 in (2,100 mm) of Z travel, 90.5 in between centers and a 12-station BMT-75 driven turret, for long parts that need keyways, cross holes or milled flats as well as turning.

The Chevalier FBL-460 is a big-bore slant-bed lathe: an A2-15 spindle nose with a 6 in (153 mm) hole through it and a top speed of 1,500 rpm. Those three figures say what it is for. This is a machine for large-diameter, slow, heavy turning and for pipe and tube that must pass through the headstock.

The Chevalier FBL-460 MC is the live-tooling version of the A2-15 big-bore lathe, with a 12-station BMT-75 turret and a 6 in (153 mm) spindle bore. It is meant for large rings, flanges and tubular parts that need holes or milled features after turning.

The Chevalier FBL-460L is the long-bed model of Chevalier's A2-15 big-bore lathe. It keeps the 6 in (153 mm) spindle bore, the 1,500 rpm spindle and the 26.7 in (680 mm) cutting diameter of the FBL-460, on a heavier bed: net weight is 29,762 lb (13,500 kg).

The Chevalier FBL-460L MC is the top model on its product page: A2-15 spindle, 6 in (153 mm) bore, long bed and BMT-75 live turret together. Z travel is 78.7 in (2,000 mm), and the maker lists 78.8 in (2,000 mm) both for cutting length and for the distance between centers.

The Chevalier FBL-510 is the shortest of Chevalier's largest slant-bed lathes, and the one with the most room around the chuck. Swing over the bed is 44.7 in (1,136 mm), maximum cutting diameter Ø37.0 in (Ø940 mm) and cutting length 41.3 in (1,050 mm).

The Chevalier FBL-510 MC is the live-tooling version of the short-bed FBL-510. Chevalier's description of its MC models is brief: the live tooling function offers additional machining capabilities to make more complex workpieces with one machine. On a lathe that swings 44.7 in (1,136 mm), the practical meaning is that a heavy part is not lifted onto a second machine for its holes.

The Chevalier FBL-520 is the two-metre model of Chevalier's largest slant-bed lathe series, with 78.7 in (2,000 mm) of cutting length, Z travel and tailstock travel. It keeps the Ø37 in (940 mm) cutting diameter of the series and is the first size in it that is a shaft machine and not a chucker.

The Chevalier FBL-520 MC adds live tooling to the two-metre bed of Chevalier's largest slant-bed lathes. Z travel is 78.7 in (2,000 mm), maximum cutting diameter Ø34.6 in (880 mm), and the 12-tool turret carries driven tools for drilling and milling along the length of a shaft.

The Chevalier FBL-530 is a three-metre slant-bed CNC lathe: 118.1 in (3,000 mm) of cutting length on a machine that also turns Ø37 in (940 mm). Few slant-bed lathes are built this long, and the size shows in the installation figures of 50,600 lb (23,000 kg) and a floor space 338.6 in wide.

The Chevalier FBL-530 MC is the three-metre live-tooling lathe in Chevalier's largest slant-bed series, with 118.1 in (3,000 mm) of Z travel and cutting length. It exists for shafts too long and too heavy to carry to a milling machine for a few keyways and holes.

The Chevalier FBL-540 is the longest lathe Chevalier lists, with 157.5 in (4,000 mm) of cutting length. It weighs 59,400 lb (27,000 kg) and its enclosure is 378 in wide, which puts it in the class of machine that a building is planned around.
The Chevalier FBL-540 MC is the four-metre model of Chevalier's largest slant-bed lathes with the live tooling function. Z travel is 157.5 in (4,000 mm), and the machine weighs 59,400 lb (27,000 kg).

The Chevalier FNL-220LSY is a two-spindle turning center with live tooling and a Y axis, built to finish a bar part on both ends without an operator turning it around. The main spindle runs to 4,500 rpm with a 2.5 in (65 mm) bar capacity. The sub-spindle runs to 6,000 rpm, carries a 6 in (152 mm) chuck and passes 1.8 in (Ø45 mm) bar.

The Chevalier FNL-220LY is a Y-axis turning center with live tooling and a servo tailstock. It is the single-spindle sibling of the FNL-220LSY: the same 4,500 rpm main spindle, the same 16-station Power BMT45 turret and the same Y axis, with a tailstock in the place where the other machine has a sub-spindle.

The Chevalier FVL-1250VTC is a vertical turning lathe with a 49.2 in (1,250 mm) table that swings and cuts 63.0 in (1,600 mm) in diameter. It is the smallest of three FVL sizes, and at 48,500 lb (22,000 kg) it is still a foundation machine built for heavy rings, flanges, housings and discs up to 17,600 lb (8,000 kg).

The Chevalier FVL-1250VTC+C is the live-tooling version of Chevalier's smallest vertical turning lathe. The +C adds a C axis on the 49.2 in (1,250 mm) table and a machining spindle in the ram that runs from 25 to 2,500 rpm, so drilled bolt circles, milled flats and tapped holes can be finished in the same clamping as the turning.

The Chevalier FVL-1600VTC is the middle size of the FVL vertical turning lathes, with a 63.0 in (1,600 mm) table and a maximum swing of 78.7 in (2,000 mm). Table load is 22,000 lb (10,000 kg) and maximum torque 19,030 Nm, about two thirds more torque than the FVL-1250VTC delivers at 11,461 Nm.

The Chevalier FVL-1600VTC+C combines a 78.7 in (2,000 mm) vertical turning lathe with a C axis and a live machining spindle. It is the mid-size FVL machine in its mill-turn form, for parts that need 19,030 Nm of turning torque and then a pattern of holes or milled features on the same faces.

The Chevalier FVL-2000VTC is the largest of Chevalier's vertical turning lathes: a 78.7 in (2,000 mm) table, a 98.4 in (2,500 mm) swing and 35,594 Nm of table torque. It weighs 99,200 lb (45,000 kg), and everything about it is scaled for parts that arrive on a flatbed.

The Chevalier FVL-2000VTC+C is the top of the FVL range: a 98.4 in (2,500 mm) vertical turning lathe with a C axis table and a live machining spindle in the ram. It is meant for the largest parts a shop will ever put on a chuck, machined complete so that they are lifted once.

The Colchester Multiturn 1000 is the smallest of Colchester's flat-bed CNC centre lathes, built round a Siemens 828D control with ShopTurn conversational programming. It swings 350 mm (13.8 in) over the bed, measures 650 mm (25.6 in) between centres and carries an 8 in (203 mm) chuck. The 7 kW (9.4 hp) spindle runs from 1 - 3,500 rpm.

The Colchester Multiturn 2000 is a 400 mm (15.7 in) swing flat-bed CNC lathe offered with 1,200 / 1,850 mm (47.2 / 72.8 in) between centres. It has a 10 in (254 mm) chuck on a D1-6 camlock nose, a 55 mm (2.2 in) spindle bore and a 7 kW (9.4 hp) spindle with a range of 1 - 2,700 rpm.

Colchester's Multiturn 2000XC adds a C-axis and a fully driven turret to its 400 mm (15.7 in) swing flat-bed CNC lathe. All 8 tool stations are driven, on VDI 20 / DIN 5480 tooling, with 2.2 kW (3.0 hp) at the tool and speeds up to 6,000 rpm. The maker calls the XC a 3-axis range that combines turning with milling, drilling and tapping to reduce second operations.

A 12 in (305 mm) chuck and a 78 mm (3.1 in) spindle bore give the Colchester Multiturn 3000 noticeably more workholding than its 460 mm (18.1 in) swing suggests. This flat-bed CNC lathe has an 11 kW (14.8 hp) spindle with a range of 1 - 2,200 rpm, a D1-8 camlock nose and bed lengths of 1,500 / 2,000 mm (59.1 / 78.7 in) between centres.

The Colchester Student CNC is a compact flat-bed CNC lathe that Colchester says is designed and engineered in the UK using the same construction as its manual Student centre lathe. It swings 330 mm (13.0 in) over the bed, takes 1,000 mm (39.4 in) between centres and carries a 6 in (152 mm) chuck on a D1-4 camlock nose. The spindle is rated 5.5 kW (7.4 hp) with a top speed of 3,000 rpm.

The Colchester Tornado SL25 is the smallest slant-bed turning centre in the Tornado range: a 2-axis production lathe with an 8 in (203 mm) chuck, a 52 mm (2.0 in) spindle bore and 400 mm (15.7 in) of turning length. The spindle runs to 5,000 rpm on an 11 kW (14.8 hp) motor through an A2-6 nose.

Two spindles and a Y-axis make the Colchester Tornado SL25 MSY the only machine in the Tornado range that can finish both ends of a part without an operator turning it round. The main spindle carries an 8 in (203 mm) chuck and runs to 5,000 rpm on 15 kW (20.1 hp). Facing it is a sub-spindle with a 6 in (152 mm) chuck, 6,000 rpm and 11 kW (14.8 hp) on an A2-5 nose.

Driven tools are what separate the Colchester Tornado SL25MC from the plain 2-axis machine it is based on. It is a slant-bed turning centre with a C-axis, an 8 in (203 mm) chuck and a 12-station VDI 30 turret whose driven tools are rated 3.5 kW (4.7 hp) at up to 5,000 rpm. The main spindle is unchanged: 5,000 rpm, 11 kW (14.8 hp), A2-6 nose, 52 mm (2.0 in) bore.

Colchester sells the Tornado SL30 / SL30L as one model in two bed lengths, and its page gives a single specification column for both. It is a 2-axis slant-bed turning centre with a 65 mm (2.6 in) spindle bore, a chuck listed as 8 / 10 in (203 / 254 mm) and a turning length listed as 600 / 1,000 mm (23.6 / 39.4 in).

The Colchester Tornado SL30MC / SL30LMC is the mid-size Tornado with a C-axis and driven tools, offered in two bed lengths under one specification column. The driven tools are rated 3.5 kW (4.7 hp) and run to 4,000 rpm. The main spindle has a 65 mm (2.6 in) bore, 15 kW (20.1 hp) and a top speed of 4,500 rpm.

With a 78 mm (3.1 in) spindle bore and an A2-8 nose, the Colchester Tornado SL35 / SL35L is where the Tornado range moves from light production turning to heavier bar and chuck work. It is a 2-axis slant-bed lathe with 18.5 kW (24.8 hp) at the spindle, a top speed of 3,500 rpm and a chuck listed as 10 / 12 in (254 / 305 mm). The two names are two bed lengths; Colchester prints one table for both.

The Colchester Tornado SL35MC / SL35LMC puts a C-axis and driven tools on the 78 mm (3.1 in) bore Tornado. Its main spindle is the heavy one of the mid-range, with 18.5 kW (24.8 hp), an A2-8 nose and 3,500 rpm, and the driven tools add 3.5 kW (4.7 hp) at up to 4,000 rpm. Two bed lengths share one table.

37 kW (49.6 hp) and a 103 mm (4.1 in) spindle bore put the Colchester Tornado SL40 / SL40L in a different class from the rest of the Tornado line. It is the largest 2-axis model: an A2-11 spindle nose, a chuck listed as 15 / 18 in (381 / 457 mm), and turning lengths of 950 / 1,500 mm (37.4 / 59.1 in) across its two bed lengths.

BMT 65 tooling and 5.5 kW (7.4 hp) driven tools make the Colchester Tornado SL40MC / SL40LMC the one Tornado MC model built for real milling loads. The Tornado SL35MC / SL35LMC below it lists VDI 40 tooling and 3.5 kW (4.7 hp); this one bolts its holders to the turret face, which is the stiffer arrangement for side-loaded cutters. Driven tools run to 4,000 rpm.

The Harrison Alpha 1350XS is the entry point to the Alpha range of CNC/manual combination lathes: a flat-bed machine that can be driven by handwheels like a centre lathe or run as a full CNC. It swings 350 mm (13.8 in) over the bed, has 650 mm (25.6 in) between centres and uses an 8 in (203 mm) chuck. The spindle covers 1 - 3,500 rpm on a 7.5 kW (10.1 hp) motor.

The Harrison Alpha 1400XC is the smallest Alpha with milling capability: a flat-bed CNC/manual combination lathe with a C-axis and an 8-station turret in which every station is driven. Driven tools are rated 2.2 kW (3.0 hp) and reach 6,000 rpm. Tooling is listed as VDI 20 / DIN 5480.

Two bed lengths and two spindle bores are the reasons to pick the Harrison Alpha 1400XS over the smallest Alpha. This CNC/manual combination lathe swings 400 mm (15.7 in) over the bed and is listed with 1,200 / 1,850 mm (47.2 / 72.8 in) between centres. The spindle bore is given as 55 / 80 mm (2.2 / 3.1 in), on a D1-6 camlock nose with a 10 in (254 mm) chuck.

A 78 mm (3.1 in) spindle bore as standard is the headline of the Harrison Alpha 1460XS. This mid-size CNC/manual combination lathe swings 460 mm (18.1 in) over the bed, is offered with 1,500 / 2,000 mm (59.1 / 78.7 in) between centres and drives its D1-8 camlock spindle with 11 kW (14.8 hp) over a range of 1 - 2,200 rpm.

The Dainichi DL65/75 puts a long bed under a moderate swing. The DL65 swings 650 mm (25.6 in) over the bed and the DL75 750 mm (29.5 in), with 380 / 480 mm (15.0 / 18.9 in) over the carriage, and the distance between centres is listed from 1,000 to 8,000 mm (39.4-315.0 in). Both sizes are 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathes.

The Dainichi DL95 is a 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe with 980 mm (38.6 in) of swing over the bed, 630 mm (24.8 in) over the carriage and between-centres lengths from 1,500 to 10,000 mm (59.1-393.7 in). It is rated for 5,000 kg (11,023 lb) between centres.

The Dainichi DL120 is a 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe for large shaft and roll work: 1,200 mm (47.2 in) of swing over the bed, 800 mm (31.5 in) over the carriage, and a distance between centres that Dainichi lists from 1,500 to 10,000 mm (59.1-393.7 in). It carries up to 7,500 kg (16,535 lb) between centres.

Two swing sizes share one specification here. The Dainichi DL132/152 is a 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe with 1,320 / 1,520 mm (52.0 / 59.8 in) of swing over the bed and 900 / 1,100 mm (35.4 / 43.3 in) over the carriage, the smaller figures belonging to the DL132 and the larger to the DL152. Distance between centres is listed from 1,500 to 15,000 mm (59.1-590.6 in). That upper limit is the reason to look at this model: the DLII142/152 matches the 1,520 mm (59.8 in) swing, but its bed range ends at 10,000 mm (393.7 in).

The Dainichi DL530 is a 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe with 530 mm (20.9 in) of swing over the bed and a choice of 1,000 / 1,500 mm (39.4 / 59.1 in) between centres. Its spindle runs 17-1,700 min-1, against 1,120 min-1 on the DL65/75 and 900 min-1 on the DL95 , which makes it the model in this family to look at when the parts are small enough for speed to matter.

The Dainichi DLII142/152 is a large-swing 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe offered in two sizes. The DLII142 swings 1,420 mm (55.9 in) over the bed and 1,000 mm (39.4 in) over the carriage; the DLII152 swings 1,520 mm (59.8 in) and 1,100 mm (43.3 in). Both take 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) between centres on beds from 1,500 to 10,000 mm (59.1-393.7 in).

The Dainichi TL132/152 has the same working envelope as the DL132/152 and a stronger spindle and higher load rating to go with it. Swing over the bed is 1,320 / 1,520 mm (52.0 / 59.8 in) for the TL132 and TL152, swing over the carriage is 900 / 1,100 mm (35.4 / 43.3 in), and distance between centres is 1,500 to 15,000 mm (59.1-590.6 in). What changes first is the weight the centres will carry: 10,000 kg (22,046 lb).

The Dainichi W16L is a 2-axis (X, Z) CNC lathe for very heavy shaft work. It carries 16,000 kg (35,274 lb) between centres, with swing over the bed listed from 1,400 to 2,200 mm (55.1-86.6 in) and distance between centres from 3,000 to 10,000 mm (118.1-393.7 in).
