The Kent CNC CT-1118 is a small collet lathe: 11 in (279 mm) of swing over the bed, 18 in (457 mm) between centers, a 5C spindle that runs from 25 to 4,000 rpm and a guaranteed circular accuracy of 50 millionths of an inch (1.3 µm). It weighs 2,200 lb (998 kg) and stands in an 81 x 40 x 65 in (2,057 x 1,016 x 1,651 mm) footprint.

The Kent CNC KLS-1840N is a fully covered CNC lathe with an 18 in (457 mm) swing over the bed, 39.4 in (1,001 mm) between centers and a 3 in (76 mm) spindle bore. It is supplied with a 10 in (254 mm) 3-jaw manual chuck, a 4-way electric tool post and the FANUC 0i-Mate TF control.

The KRC Velocity VTC-12 is the entry size of KRC's Velocity series of vertical turning lathes, with a 1,250 mm (49.2 in) table, a 1,500 mm (59.1 in) maximum turning diameter and 1,250 mm (49.2 in) of turning height. The table carries 6,000 kg (13,228 lb) and turns at 1 - 300 rpm.

KRC's Velocity VTC-16 is a vertical turning lathe with a 1,600 mm (63 in) table that swings 2,000 mm (78.7 in) and turns up to 1,900 mm (74.8 in) in diameter. It sits between the Velocity VTC-12 and the Velocity VTC-20 and shares its 1,600 mm (63 in) maximum turning height with the larger machine.

The KRC Velocity VTC-20 is the largest lathe in the Velocity series: a 2,000 mm (78.7 in) table, 2,400 mm (94.5 in) maximum turning diameter, 2,500 mm (98.4 in) swing and a table load of 13,000 kg (28,660 lb).

The Litz LT-350 is a compact two-axis CNC turning lathe with an A2-5 spindle nose, 45 mm (1.8 in) bar capacity and a maximum turning diameter of 240 mm (9.4 in). Maximum turning length is 350 mm (13.8 in), and the spindle runs from 40-6,000 rpm.

The Litz LT-400 is a two-axis CNC turning lathe one size above the LT-350 , with an A2-6 spindle nose, 52 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity, a 320 mm (12.6 in) maximum turning diameter and 530 mm (20.9 in) of turning length.

The Litz LT-400M is an 8 in (203 mm) chuck turning centre with a C axis and a 12-station live turret, so cross holes, flats and keyways are cut in the same clamping as the turning. Turning capacity is 215 mm (8.5 in) in diameter and 530 mm (20.9 in) in length, with 52 mm (2.0 in) bar capacity.

The Litz LT-520 is the largest of the three two-axis LT slant-bed lathes: a 10 in (254 mm) chuck machine with an A2-8 spindle nose, 78 mm (3.1 in) bar capacity, a 400 mm (15.7 in) maximum turning diameter and 710 mm (28.0 in) of turning length.
The Litz LT-520M puts a C axis and a 12-station live turret on the larger LT bed: a 10 in (254 mm) chuck, an A2-8 spindle with 78 mm (3.1 in) bar capacity and 710 mm (28.0 in) of turning length.

The Milltronics SL8-II is a CNC turning center fitted with an 8 in 3-jaw hydraulic chuck on an A2-6 spindle nose, turning parts up to 14 in (356 mm) in diameter and 21 in (533 mm) long. The spindle runs up to 4,000 rpm with 30/20 hp (22.4/14.9 kW) and 161 lb-ft (218 Nm) of torque.

The Milltronics SL10-II is a 10 in chuck turning center built on an A2-8 spindle nose, with 260 lb-ft (352 Nm) of spindle torque and a turning envelope of 17.7 in (450 mm) in diameter by 29.9 in (759 mm) in length. It trades speed for torque: the spindle tops out at 3,000 rpm.

The Milltronics TRL22/60 is a gap-bed CNC lathe on solid box ways with 64.96 in (1,650 mm) of Z travel, a 4.13 in (105 mm) spindle bore and 620 lb-ft (841 Nm) of spindle torque. The figures describe a machine for long, heavy turning at an unhurried pace: rapids are 500 ipm (12.7 m/min) and the spindle range is 40 to 2,500 rpm.

The Pinnacle L210A is a slant bed CNC turning center with an 8 in chuck, 610 mm (24.0 in) between centers and a maximum turning diameter of Ø440 mm (Ø17.3 in). It is the base model of four L210 variants that share one bed and differ in chuck and spindle.

Pinnacle sells a 10 in chuck in two ways, and the Pinnacle L210B is the lighter of them: the larger chuck on the A2-6 spindle of the L210A , keeping 45 - 4,500 rpm and the 11 / 15 kW (14.8 / 20.1 hp) motor.
Bar capacity is the reason to choose the Pinnacle L210C: Ø77 mm (Ø3.0 in), through an Ø88 mm (Ø3.5 in) spindle bore on an A2-8 nose. The L210A and L210B stop at Ø65 mm (Ø2.6 in).
The Pinnacle L210D carries the largest chuck in the L210 range, 12 in, on the A2-8 spindle with a 15 / 18.5 kW (20.1 / 24.8 hp) motor. It is the heaviest of the four at 4,300 kg (9,480 lb).

The Pinnacle PK-L150A is a compact CNC turning center for small chucked and bar-fed parts: a 6 in chuck on an A2-5 spindle, Ø42 mm (Ø1.7 in) of bar capacity and a turning length of 150 mm (5.9 in). It weighs 2,100 kg (4,630 lb) and occupies 1.8 x 1.4 x 1.65 m.

The Pinnacle PK-L210A/BMY is a slant bed turning center with a VDI 30 live tooling turret and a Y axis of 80 mm (3.1 in), listed as ±40 mm. It mills, drills and taps on a turned part in the same chucking, using a C axis that positions to 0.001 degree.

The Pinnacle PK-L210C/DMY combines Pinnacle's larger lathe spindle with driven tools and a Y axis: an A2-8 nose, Ø77 mm (Ø3.0 in) of bar capacity and a 15 / 18.5 kW (20.1 / 24.8 hp) motor in front of a 12-station VDI 30 turret.

The Quicktech i-42 Twin is a gang-tooling bar lathe with a main spindle, a sub-spindle and one shared tool system. It takes 42 mm (1.7 in) bar, or 65 mm (2.6 in) as an option, and turns up to 300 mm (11.8 in) long on the main spindle. That is the longest turning length in the i-42 line; the i-42 Ultimate lists 230 mm (9.1 in).

The Quicktech T8 Mill-Y is the single-spindle version of the maker's Y-axis turret lathe: a 75° slant bed, a BMT-55 power turret with 12 stations, and 80 mm = ±40 mm (3.1 in = ±1.6 in) of Y1 travel. It takes 65 mm (2.6 in) bar and turns up to 300 mm (11.8 in) in diameter. Quicktech describes the T8 series as designed primarily for heavy duty turning and milling in mass production.

The Quicktech T8 Twin-Y is a 75° slant-bed turret lathe with a Y axis and a sub-spindle, sized for 65 mm (2.6 in) bar and for chucked parts up to 300 mm (11.8 in) in turning diameter. One BMT-55 power turret with 12 stations serves both spindles. It is the conventional twin-spindle layout in the T8 group, between the single-spindle T8 Mill-Y and the two-system T8 Hybrid-Y .

The ROMI C 670 tops the New Generation C Series: a flat-bed CNC lathe with 670 mm (26.38 in) of swing over the bed, 2,000 mm (78.74 in) between centers and a single A2-8” headstock bored to 104 mm (4.09 in). The ROMI VT 1400M is the smallest of Romi's ram-type vertical CNC lathes, and still a large machine: a 1,400 mm (55 in) chuck, 1,600 mm (63 in) of turning diameter and a table that accepts 10,000 kg (22,000 lbs). The M in the name refers to the driven tool in the ram, which with the C axis turns the lathe into a machine that also drills and mills.

Wide, flat work is the territory of the ROMI VT 2000M. This vertical CNC lathe turns up to 2,200 mm (87 in) in diameter on a 2,000 mm (79 in) chuck, yet its maximum turning height is the same 1,500 mm (59 in) as on the smaller VT 1400M . Slewing rings, large flanges, gear rims and tyre moulds have that shape.

From the ROMI VT 2500M upward the VT Series becomes a twin-column machine. The cross rail hangs between two cast columns joined by a traverse and is moved by two servomotors and ball screws to programmed stops, and that structure buys height: 2,100 mm (83 in) of turning height with the ram, where the two smaller models stop at 1,500 mm.

Diameter without added weight capacity: the ROMI VT 3000M turns up to 3,400 mm (134 in) on a 3,000 mm (118 in) chuck, but its table is rated for the same 25,000 kg (55,100 lbs) as the VT 2500M . It is the choice for parts that are very wide and comparatively light for their size.

The ROMI VT 5000 belongs to a different order of size from the M models below it. Its table accepts 90,000 kg (198,400 lbs), its chuck is 5,000 mm (197 in) across, and it turns parts up to 7,000 mm (276 in) in diameter and 4,000 mm (157 in) high. The machine itself weighs 207,000 kg (456,400 lbs).
7,000 mm (276 in); 8,000 mm (315 in) optional under request

Driven tools are what the M in ROMI VTL 500MR stands for. It is the 500 mm (20 in) vertical turning center with a BMT 65 turret, 12 stations for fixed and driven tools, so bolt circles, cross holes and milled flats are cut while the part is still in the chuck. Romi prints its figures in a shared column with the VTL 500ML.

The ROMI VTL 500R is a vertical turning center for chucked parts up to 500 mm (20 in) in diameter, with the spindle pointing up and a 12-station turret for fixed tools above it. Romi lists it in one column with the VTL 500L and gives the two identical figures. On a vertical lathe gravity seats the part in the chuck, which is why this layout is chosen for discs, hubs, flywheels and brake components that are awkward to load horizontally.

For large chucked parts that also need milling and drilling, Romi offers the ROMI VTL 700MR: the 700 mm (28 in) vertical turning center with a BMT 75 driven-tool turret. It appears in the catalogue together with the VTL 700ML, with one set of figures for the pair.

The ROMI VTL 700R takes the vertical turning center format up to 700 mm (28 in) of turning diameter and changes the machine underneath to suit heavier cuts. It has an A2-11” spindle, a 46 hp / 34 kW motor and hardened and ground square guideways in place of the linear roller guides of the 500 size. The VTL 700L shares its column in the specification table.

The Sharp 1840TC-F is a flat bed CNC lathe of toolroom size: 18 in (457.2 mm) of swing over the bed, 39.4 in between centers and a 2.37 in spindle bore behind a D1-6 camlock nose. It is the smallest of Sharp's TC-F lathes.

A 20 in (508 mm) swing and 59.05 in between centers define the Sharp 2060TC-F, the middle of the three smaller flat bed CNC lathes Sharp builds around the FANUC Oi-TF control. Its spindle bore is 3.37 in (85.59 mm), a full inch more than the 2.37 in (60.19 mm) of the 1840TC-F .
The Sharp 2460TC-F is the 24 in (609.6 mm) swing flat bed CNC lathe in the TC-F line, with 59 in between centers, a 4.09 in (103.88 mm) spindle bore and a Fanuc 15 hp (11.18 kW) spindle motor.

The Sharp 3060TC-F opens the 3000 series of flat bed CNC lathes: 29.92 in (760 mm) of swing over the bed, 59 in (1,500 mm) between centers and a 6.7 in (170 mm) bore through an A2-11 spindle. This is oil-country and heavy-shaft territory, a clear step above the 2460TC-F .

Sharp's 3080TC-F stretches the 30 in flat bed CNC lathe to 78.75 in (2,000 mm) between centers. The headstock is the one used across the 3000 series, with a 6.7 in (170 mm) bore, an A2-11 nose and a 20 hp (14.91 kW) motor, so the choice between this model and its siblings comes down to how long the work is and how much floor can be given up.

The Sharp 30120TC-F is where the 3000 series changes character. With 118 in (3,000 mm) between centers on a 177 in (4,500 mm) bed it weighs 15,400 lb (6,985 kg), about half as much again as the 78.75 in model, the 3080TC-F , at 10,120 lb (4,590 kg).

Longest of Sharp's TC-F flat bed CNC lathes, the 30160TC-F turns work up to 157 in (3,988 mm) between centers on a 216.5 in (5,500 mm) bed. Swing is 29.92 in (760 mm), and pipe up to 6.7 in (170 mm) passes through the A2-11 spindle.

The Tormach 8L is a small enclosed CNC lathe with an 8 in (200 mm) swing over the bed, a 5C spindle nose and a tailstock. X travel is 4.5 in (114 mm) and Z travel is 10 in (254 mm) with the tailstock in place. The spindle is rated 1.5 hp (1.11 kW) and covers 180 to 5,000 rpm.

The YCM GT-200B is the smallest two-axis turning center in the GT series: an 8" chuck on an A2-6 spindle nose, a maximum turning diameter of ø260 mm (ø10.24 in) and a turning length of 345 mm (13.58 in). The spindle runs to 4,500 rpm and the turret is a 10-station servo unit with hydraulic clamping.

Live tools are what the YCM GT-200MA adds to the small GT lathe. It has a 12-station radial power turret, a 6" chuck on an A2-5 nose and a 6,000 rpm main spindle, for turned parts up to ø230 mm (ø9.06 in) in diameter and 370 mm (14.57 in) long.

The YCM GT-250B is a 10" chuck turning center for mid-size shaft and flange work: ø350 mm (ø13.78 in) maximum turning diameter, 515 mm (20.28 in) between the chuck and the end of the cut, and a 3,500 rpm spindle on an A2-8 nose.

In the YCM GT-250MA the mid-size GT lathe gets a 12-station radial power turret and trades chuck size for reach. It carries an 8" chuck on an A2-6 nose, spins at 4,500 rpm, and turns parts up to ø270 mm (ø10.63 in) in diameter and 560 mm (22.05 in) in length.

The YCM GT-300B is the big-bore two-axis lathe of the GT series. Its spindle has a ø105 mm (ø4.13 in) through hole and a ø91 mm (ø3.58 in) draw bar hole, and it turns parts up to ø440 mm (ø17.32 in) in diameter and 700 mm (27.56 in) long at up to 3,000 rpm.

Long bed, big bore, live tools: the YCM GT-300LMB combines the three. Its maximum turning length is 1,233 mm (48.54 in) on a Z travel of 1,283 mm (50.51 in), the spindle has a ø105 mm (ø4.13 in) through hole, and the 12-station radial power turret drives tools at 3,000 rpm.

The YCM GT-300MA is a live-tool turning center on the GT-300 bed, with a 12-station radial power turret that is servo rotated and hydraulically clamped. It turns up to ø360 mm (ø14.17 in) in diameter and 742 mm (29.21 in) in length, with a spindle speed of 3,500 rpm.

The YCM NT-2500SY is a twin-spindle turning center with a Y axis, built to finish a part on both ends without an operator turning it round. The main spindle has an A2-8 nose and runs to 3,500 rpm; the sub-spindle has an A2-5 nose and runs to 6,000 rpm. Maximum turning diameter is ø350 mm (ø13.78 in) and turning length 686 mm (27.01 in).

Sub-spindle plus Y axis on a fast 8" lathe: that is the YCM NTC-2000LSY. The main spindle turns 5,000 rpm on an A2-6 nose, the sub-spindle 6,000 rpm on an A2-5 nose with a 6" chuck, and one 12-station BMT55 power turret works on both.

The YCM NTC-2000LY is a Y-axis turning center with an 8" chuck, a 5,000 rpm spindle and a BMT55 live-tool turret. It turns parts up to ø320 mm (ø12.6 in) in diameter and 570 mm (22.44 in) in length, and its Y axis is listed as 90 mm, split 50 above and 40 below centre.

The YCM TC-16LA is a light, fast two-axis turning center on linear guideways. It has a 6" chuck on an A2-5 nose, a 5,000 rpm spindle, and turns parts up to ø260 mm (ø10.24 in) in diameter and 600 mm (23.62 in) in length.

Give the TC-16L bed a bigger spindle and you have the YCM TC-16LB. This two-axis turning center mounts an 8" chuck on an A2-6 nose, with a ø77 mm (ø3.03 in) spindle bore and a ø66 mm (ø2.6 in) hole through the draw bar. Top speed is 4,500 rpm.

A long-bed, geared-head lathe for big shafts, the YCM TC-36 turns up to ø590 mm (ø23.23 in) in diameter and 1,189 mm (46.81 in) in length. Z travel is 1,250 mm (49.21 in) and the main motor is rated 22/26 kW (30/35 HP).

The You Ji AH06 is the fastest of three heavy-duty horizontal turning lathes that share one bed, one Ø950 mm (37.4 in) swing and one 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp) spindle motor. What sets it apart is the spindle: an A2-15 nose with Ø153 mm (6.0 in) of bar capacity, a Ø690 mm (27.2 in) hydraulic chuck in the table, and a top gear that reaches 1,200 rpm.

With Ø306 mm (12.0 in) of bar capacity and an A2-20 spindle nose, the You Ji AH12 is the largest-bore machine in the AH family of heavy-duty horizontal turning lathes. Casing, large-diameter line pipe and hollow rolls go through the headstock so that only the end being machined sits in the work zone.

The You Ji CY550H is a CNC vertical turning lathe designed around its pallet changer. The base machine has a 15 in (381 mm) chuck and a horizontal turret (the H in the name); the CY550H-APC adds an automatic pallet changer, which You Ji describes as a high efficiency APC system for workpiece loading and unloading.

The You Ji HV320 combines two lathes in one machine: a CNC vertical turning lathe and an inverted spindle lathe. The catalogue table has one column for each, the inverted spindle labelled OP1 and the vertical turning lathe OP2, so a part is turned on one side, handed over and finished on the other without leaving the enclosure.

The You Ji TY400H is a narrow-bodied CNC vertical turning lathe with a 10 in (254 mm) chuck and a horizontal turret. The frame is built front to back: the floor dimension is 1,030 x 3,200 mm (40.6 x 126.0 in), so several machines can stand side by side with little width per spindle.

A 12 in (305 mm) chuck, Ø450 mm (17.7 in) of turning diameter and an equal 450 mm (17.7 in) of turning height: the You Ji TY600H is the larger of the two TY vertical turning lathes. The series is laid out deep and narrow, and this model measures 1,300 x 3,800 mm (51.2 x 149.6 in) on the floor.

The You Ji VHL1200ATC is a CNC vertical turning center with a side head: a second tool carrier mounted on the column that works on the outside of the part while the main ram works from above. The table is Ø1,250 mm (49.2 in) and the maximum turning diameter Ø1,350 mm (53.1 in).

On the You Ji VHL1600ATC a side head works alongside the main ram of a Ø1,600 mm (63.0 in) vertical turning center. The machine turns Ø1,800 mm (70.9 in), swings Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) and takes parts 1,200 mm (47.2 in) high.

Every drive and travel row is larger on the You Ji VHL2000ATC than on the two smaller side-head machines. This vertical turning center has a Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) table, a 60/75 kW (80.5/100.6 hp) table motor and an 11/15 kW (14.8/20.1 hp) live spindle motor on the side head.

The You Ji VTH3000ATC is a heavy-duty vertical turning lathe whose Ø3,000 mm (118.1 in) table runs on a hydrostatic bearing. That bearing is the point of the VTH series: the table floats on a pressurised oil film, and the rated load is 45,000 kg (99,206 lb).

Take the VTH3000ATC , widen the table to Ø3,500 mm (137.8 in), and the result is the You Ji VTH3500ATC. It is a hydrostatic-table vertical turning lathe that turns Ø3,800 mm (149.6 in) and swings Ø4,100 mm (161.4 in).

Sixty tonnes on a four-metre table: the You Ji VTH4000ATC is rated for a 60,000 kg (132,275 lb) loading weight and driven by a 100/140 kW (134.1/187.7 hp) spindle motor. It is a CNC vertical turning lathe with a hydrostatic table bearing, Ø4,000 mm (157.5 in) across.

The You Ji VTH4500ATC is the largest VTH vertical turning lathe driven by a single motor. From the VTH5000ATC upward the catalogue lists the spindle motor twice over; here it is one 100/140 kW (134.1/187.7 hp) unit turning a Ø4,500 mm (177.2 in) hydrostatic table.

The You Ji VTH5000ATC begins the very large half of the VTH range. This hydrostatic-table vertical turning lathe has a Ø5,000 mm (196.9 in) table, carries 100,000 kg (220,459 lb) and lists its spindle motor as 2 x 60/84 kW (2 x 80.5/112.6 hp).

A Ø6,000 mm (236.2 in) table rated for 150,000 kg (330,688 lb) is what the You Ji VTH6000ATC offers. The machine is a hydrostatic-bearing CNC vertical turning lathe that turns up to Ø6,900 mm (271.7 in) inside a Ø7,400 mm (291.3 in) swing.

Quarter of a million kilograms: the You Ji VTH7000ATC has a maximum loading weight of 250,000 kg (551,146 lb). Its hydrostatic table is Ø7,000 mm (275.6 in) across, and the machine turns Ø8,500 mm (334.6 in) within a Ø9,000 mm (354.3 in) swing.

You Ji's biggest vertical turning lathe is the VTH8000ATC. The hydrostatic table measures Ø8,000 mm (315.0 in), the maximum turning diameter is Ø8,900 mm (350.4 in) and the maximum loading weight is 300,000 kg (661,376 lb).

The You Ji VTL1200ATC is a CNC vertical turning lathe with an automatic tool changer, a Ø1,250 mm (49.2 in) table and a maximum turning diameter of Ø1,350 mm (53.1 in). It is the entry point to the VTL series on You Ji's current list, a family the maker describes as a symmetric design for column and base.

Two rams become possible at the You Ji VTL1600ATC. You Ji's model key offers the double ram (2R) version from the 1600 upward, which makes this the smallest VTL vertical turning lathe that can cut with two heads at once or keep a turning ram and a milling ram set up side by side.

The You Ji VTL2000ATC is the size at which the VTL series gets a bigger drive: a 60/75 kW (80.5/100.6 hp) spindle motor in place of the 37/45 kW (49.6/60.3 hp) unit of the VTL1600ATC . It is a CNC vertical turning lathe with a Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) table, an automatic tool changer and a BT-50 tool shank.

For shops that want a pallet changer on the biggest possible table, the You Ji VTL2500ATC is the limit. You Ji lists the automatic pallet changer for VTL sizes 1000 to 2500, and this CNC vertical turning lathe sits at the top of that span with a Ø2,500 mm (98.4 in) table.

At three metres of table, the You Ji VTL3000ATC is a different class of installation from the smaller VTL vertical turning lathes. The catalogue lists a floor dimension of 11,000 x 7,000 mm (433.1 x 275.6 in) and a height of 7,400 mm (291.3 in).

The You Ji VTL3500ATC stretches the VTL vertical turning lathe to a Ø3,500 mm (137.8 in) table while keeping the drive and load rating of the size below it. Maximum turning diameter is Ø3,800 mm (149.6 in) and the swing Ø4,100 mm (161.4 in).

100 kW (134.1 hp) is the spindle motor rating of the You Ji VTL4000ATC, the first VTL vertical turning lathe with a three-figure motor rating. The table is Ø4,000 mm (157.5 in), the turning diameter Ø4,300 mm (169.3 in) and the swing Ø4,600 mm (181.1 in).
The largest machine in You Ji's VTL table is the VTL4500ATC, a CNC vertical turning lathe with a Ø4,500 mm (177.2 in) table. It turns Ø4,800 mm (189.0 in) and swings Ø5,100 mm (200.8 in).

The You Ji VTS1000ATC is a fixed cross-rail vertical turning lathe with a Ø1,000 mm (39.4 in) table, an automatic tool changer and Capto C6 tooling. It opens the VTS series, which You Ji defines by that fixed type cross-rail: the rail does not travel up and down the columns, so the ram works from one rigid height.

Ø1,400 mm (55.1 in) of turning diameter on a Ø1,250 mm (49.2 in) table: the You Ji VTS1200ATC turns slightly wider than You Ji's other machines of this table size. It is the second model of the VTS family of vertical turning lathes, built with a fixed type cross-rail and an automatic tool changer.

The You Ji VTS1600ATC is a fixed cross-rail vertical turning lathe for discs and rings up to Ø1,800 mm (70.9 in). Its table is Ø1,600 mm (63.0 in), the swing Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) and the loading weight 8,000 kg (17,637 lb).

A two-metre table under a fixed cross-rail: the You Ji VTS2000ATC is a CNC vertical turning lathe with a Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) table, a 60/75 kW (80.5/100.6 hp) spindle motor and a Capto C6 automatic tool changer.

The You Ji VTS2500ATC carries 15,000 kg (33,069 lb) on a Ø2,500 mm (98.4 in) table and turns up to Ø2,800 mm (110.2 in). It is a fixed cross-rail vertical turning lathe with an automatic tool changer and the Capto C6 tool shank common to the VTS series.

With the You Ji VTS3000ATC the fixed cross-rail is set higher: maximum turning height is 1,000 mm (39.4 in), up from the 800 mm (31.5 in) of the VTS2500ATC and every smaller VTS model. The table is Ø3,000 mm (118.1 in).

The top of the VTS range, the You Ji VTS4000ATC, puts a Ø4,000 mm (157.5 in) table under a fixed cross-rail and drives it with a 100 kW (134.1 hp) motor. Maximum turning diameter is Ø4,500 mm (177.2 in) and the swing Ø4,800 mm (189.0 in).

The You Ji YH15 is a compact CNC horizontal turning lathe with a 6 in (152 mm) chuck, an A2-5 spindle nose and an 8-st. turret. It is the smallest machine in the YH series and the only one with a chuck this small.

An 8 in (203 mm) chuck, an A2-6 spindle nose and Ø52 mm (2.0 in) of bar capacity put the You Ji YH21 in the most common size class of CNC horizontal turning lathes. Maximum turning diameter is Ø416 mm (16.4 in) under a Ø560 mm (22.0 in) swing.

The You Ji YH28 is a 10 in (254 mm) chuck CNC horizontal turning lathe offered in two bed lengths. The catalogue gives the maximum turning length as 550/1,050 mm (21.7/41.3 in), so the same headstock and turret serve either a chucker or a short-shaft machine.

Four bed lengths are listed for the You Ji YH36, a 15 in (381 mm) chuck CNC horizontal turning lathe: the maximum turning length is given as 750/1,350/2,000/3,000 mm (29.5/53.1/78.7/118.1 in). The catalogue pictures the machine as YH36/200 and YH36+C/200, the suffix naming the length.

The You Ji YV200 is the smallest machine in the YV range of CNC vertical turning lathes: an 8 in (203 mm) chuck, a maximum turning diameter of Ø250 mm (9.8 in) and 200 mm (7.9 in) of turning height. It is a chucker for small discs, hubs, flanges and bearing-size rings that sit flat on a vertical spindle and load by gravity.

With a 10 in (254 mm) chuck and Ø350 mm (13.8 in) of turning diameter, the You Ji YV250 is the second size in the YV family of CNC vertical turning lathes. Turning height is 250 mm (9.8 in) and the swing is Ø500 mm (19.7 in).

The You Ji YV500 is a 15 in (381 mm) chuck vertical turning lathe that turns up to Ø550 mm (21.7 in) in diameter and 500 mm (19.7 in) in height. It is the size at which the YV range changes character: the table load jumps to 1,200 kg (2,646 lb) and the tooling list opens up to include an automatic tool changer.

An 18 in (457 mm) chuck defines the You Ji YV550. This vertical turning lathe turns Ø650 mm (25.6 in) by 500 mm (19.7 in) high, swings Ø800 mm (31.5 in) and carries 1,200 kg (2,646 lb) on the spindle.
The You Ji YV600 moves the YV vertical turning lathe onto a 24 in (610 mm) chuck. Maximum turning diameter is Ø750 mm (29.5 in), turning height 600 mm (23.6 in) and swing Ø850 mm (33.5 in).

Ø800 mm (31.5 in) is the figure to remember for the You Ji YV700. That is the maximum turning diameter of this CNC vertical turning lathe, held in a 24 in (610 mm) chuck with Ø900 mm (35.4 in) of swing and 600 mm (23.6 in) of turning height.

The You Ji YV1000 is where the YV line stops being a chucker and becomes a table-type vertical turning lathe. The catalogue quotes its chuck as Ø1,000 mm (39.4 in), the maximum turning diameter as Ø1,100 mm (43.3 in) and the turning height as 900 mm (35.4 in).

Turning height is the reason to look at the You Ji YV1200. At 1,200 mm (47.2 in) it clears parts a third taller than the YV1000 can take, on a table quoted at Ø1,250 mm (49.2 in) with a maximum turning diameter of Ø1,350 mm (53.1 in).

The You Ji YV1600 tops the YV range: a vertical turning lathe with a Ø1,600 mm (63.0 in) table, Ø1,800 mm (70.9 in) maximum turning diameter and Ø2,000 mm (78.7 in) swing. Workpieces up to 1,200 mm (47.2 in) high and 8,000 kg (17,637 lb) are within its table figures.
